records.title: Brain Alteration Patterns in Children with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Machine Learning Approach to Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.model_family: support vector machine on multimodal structural and diffusion measures
records.clinical_problem: whether the absent dystrophin in Duchenne muscular dystrophy leaves a detectable mark on the brain, which would explain the cognitive and behavioral features
records.patient_population: 18 children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and 18 age- and sex-matched controls with similar cognitive and behavioral profiles
records.model_description: Combines cortical thickness, structure volumes and diffusion measures in one multivariate classifier, with controls deliberately matched on cognitive and behavioral profile so that the classification cannot simply be picking up comorbidity. The forward model then localizes the signal to long fiber bundles — cerebellar peduncles, posterior thalamic radiation, fornix, medial lemniscus — and to motor, cingulate, hippocampal and insular cortex. The sample is small and the accuracy correspondingly optimistic.
records.headline_result: 97.2% classification accuracy between patients and matched controls

records.title: Safe for kids? AI medical devices in radiology overlook paediatric suitability.
records.clinical_problem: whether the AI devices a European radiology department can buy say anything about being safe for children
records.patient_population: 213 regulatory-approved radiology AI medical devices reviewed
records.model_description: Two reviewers went through every regulatory-approved radiology AI device in a public European database and asked a simple question: who is it for. Four of 213 were clearly labelled for pediatric use. Forty-one percent gave no clear intended population at all, and half of those remained unclear even after reading the scientific literature and the marketing material. The risk the authors name is inadvertent off-label use in children, and their proposal is a standardized pediatric safety indicator.
records.release_evidence: reviews regulatory-approved commercial AI medical devices
records.headline_result: 4 of 213 devices (2%) clearly labelled for pediatric use; a further 11% intended for all ages; 41% gave no clear intended population, and 47% of those remained unclear after reviewing literature and marketing

records.title: AI implementation in pediatric radiology for patient safety: a multi-society statement from the ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR, SPIN.
records.clinical_problem: how a children's hospital should buy, deploy, monitor and teach AI safely
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
records.model_description: A joint statement from the ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR and SPIN covering four pillars: regulation and purchasing, implementation, post-market surveillance, and education. Concretely it asks for pediatric-specific safety ratings, training data drawn from diverse pediatric populations, quantifiable transparency metrics, phased rollout with pilot testing and continuous benchmark monitoring, explicit protocols for discrepancies and adverse incidents, and AI literacy training for every clinician who touches these tools. This is the document to hand a procurement committee.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics for pediatric brain tumor classification and molecular characterization: a systematic review.
records.clinical_problem: classifying pediatric brain tumors and predicting their molecular subtype from imaging
records.patient_population: children aged 0-18 with brain tumors, across 24 studies published 2010-2025
records.model_description: A systematic review that scores the methodological quality of the field rather than only its accuracy, using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and the CLAIM checklist. The headline accuracies are high — median AUC 0.91 — and most studies were rated low risk of bias, but only three of 24 validated on an independent cohort. Radiomics still dominates over deep learning here, which reflects how small the available pediatric cohorts are.
records.headline_result: reported AUCs 0.73-0.98 (median 0.91); 96% used MRI and 88% radiomics-based machine learning; only 12.5% performed external validation

records.title: BIBSNet: A Deep Learning Baby Image Brain Segmentation Network for MRI Scans.
records.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
records.model_family: deep segmentation network trained on manual plus SynthSeg-generated labels
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the infant brain in the first months of life, when tissue contrast inverts and adult tools fail
records.patient_population: 90 participants aged 0-8 months (median 4.6 months)
records.model_description: Segments neonatal and infant brain MRI and emits FreeSurfer-compatible labels, so it drops into existing processing pipelines rather than requiring a new one. Trained with data augmentation on manually annotated images plus synthetic segmentations. It beat joint label fusion on Dice across every region and on nearly every downstream derived metric, and runs 600 times faster.
records.release_evidence: introduced as an open-source, community-driven model
records.headline_result: outperformed joint label fusion on Dice across all regions and on nearly all derived metrics, at 600 times the speed

records.title: Multimodal deep learning improves recurrence risk prediction in pediatric low-grade gliomas.
records.model_family: deep logistic hazard model on features from a pretrained segmentation network
records.clinical_problem: predicting which children will recur after surgery for a low-grade glioma, which conventional clinical, radiographic and genomic factors do poorly
records.patient_population: 396 children with pediatric low-grade glioma from Dana-Farber/Boston Children's and the Children's Brain Tumor Network, median follow-up 85 months
records.model_description: Reuses a segmentation network trained for pediatric low-grade glioma as a feature extractor on the preoperative T2 image, then predicts postoperative event-free survival from those features alone or combined with clinical variables. The multimodal version separated a high-risk group with 31% three-year event-free survival from a low-risk group at 92%, which is the kind of separation that could change whether a child is watched or treated.
records.headline_result: time-dependent concordance 0.85 for the multimodal model versus 0.79 imaging-only and 0.72 clinical-only; three-year event-free survival 31% predicted high risk versus 92% low risk

records.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection and Radiological Data Monitoring Using Statistical Process Control.
records.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
records.model_family: feature-representation drift detection with statistical process control
records.clinical_problem: knowing when a deployed model is being shown images it was not built for, including adult models being fed pediatric radiographs
records.patient_population: adult and pediatric chest radiographs, and CT images, used as drift scenarios
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model but a guard on one: it detects when an incoming image is out of distribution for the deployed model, and monitors the data stream for gradual drift using statistical process control. One of its three demonstrations is exactly the failure mode a children's hospital should worry about — telling adult chest radiographs from pediatric ones, which it flagged within a day of the shift beginning. Modality- and model-agnostic by design.
records.headline_result: sensitivity for out-of-distribution detection 0.980 (CT), 0.984 (chest radiograph modality) and 0.854 (pediatric versus adult chest radiographs); a simulated adult-to-pediatric drift was detected within a day at a low false positive rate

records.title: Children Are Not Small Adults: Addressing Limited Generalizability of an Adult Deep Learning CT Organ Segmentation Model to the Pediatric Population.
records.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
records.model_family: nnU-Net, evaluated and then retrained or fine-tuned on pediatric data
records.clinical_problem: whether the field's default open organ segmentation model, built on adults, is safe to use on children
records.patient_population: 300 adult and 359 pediatric abdominal CT scans from external datasets
records.model_description: The title is the finding. TotalSegmentator, trained on adults, drops from 0.81 to 0.73 mean Dice on pediatric scans, and the failure concentrates in the small structures — adrenal glands fall to 0.35-0.41 against 0.68-0.69 in adults. The paper then shows both fixes work: a pediatric-only model and an adult model fine-tuned on children each beat it on every organ. This is the cleanest available demonstration of why adult-trained tools need pediatric validation before deployment.
records.release_evidence: evaluates the openly available TotalSegmentator model
records.headline_result: mean Dice 0.73 in children versus 0.81 in adults (P < .001); adrenal gland Dice 0.35-0.41 versus 0.68-0.69; pediatric-specific training and fine-tuning both improved every organ, by over 0.2 Dice for the adrenals
records.study_design: retrospective external evaluation with model retraining

records.title: An automated pipeline for computation and analysis of functional ventilation and perfusion lung MRI with matrix pencil decomposition: TrueLung.
records.model_family: neural network whole-lung and lobar segmentation inside an automated processing pipeline
records.clinical_problem: measuring regional ventilation and perfusion in children with cystic fibrosis without contrast, breath-holds or ionizing radiation
records.patient_population: 75 children with cystic fibrosis imaged at 1.5 T
records.model_description: An end-to-end pipeline that turns free-breathing, contrast-free lung MRI into ventilation and perfusion maps and quantified defect percentages, delivered as a short clinical report. It was feasible in every child attempted, with a six-minute scan and twenty-minute processing. The authors also report how often a human had to correct the segmentation and what difference that made to the numbers, which is the honest way to describe an automated pipeline in clinical use.
records.headline_result: feasible in all children, 6 min 20 s mean scan time; automatic whole-lung quantification satisfactory in 88% of patients and lobar quantification in 73%; manual refinement changed relative ventilation and perfusion by 0.7% and 2.0%

records.title: A critical comparative study of the performance of three AI-assisted programs for bone age determination.
records.model_family: three commercial bone age programs compared head to head
records.clinical_problem: which of the bone age products approved for the European market a department should buy
records.patient_population: 306 children aged 1-18, stratified by sex and age, at a Central European centre
records.model_description: The comparison the vendors do not run: three commercially available bone age programs on one cohort, against a three-expert Greulich-Pyle ground truth, reporting dropout rates alongside accuracy. All three were reliable across the main age range and differed mainly at the edges of childhood, and the spread between the programs was smaller than the spread between the human readers. Dropout rate varied enormously, from 0% to 20%, which is a practical difference a purchaser would not otherwise see.
records.release_evidence: three AI-supported programs approved for medical use in Europe: BoneXpert, PANDA and BoneView
records.headline_result: root mean squared error 0.62 years (BoneXpert), 0.65 (BoneView) and 0.75 (PANDA), with dropout rates of 2.3%, 20.3% and 0%; variation between AI readers was lower than between human readers (0.54 vs 0.62 years, p < 0.01)

records.title: Automated Neuroprognostication Via Machine Learning in Neonates with Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
records.model_family: elastic net on shape and radiomic features from a custom neonatal template
records.clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, where MRI is read subjectively and prognosis is uncertain
records.patient_population: 286 infants treated with therapeutic hypothermia, with Bayley scores at 18 months
records.model_description: Builds an anatomical template from cooled newborns, labels the deep gray-matter structures, extracts shape and radiomic measures from each, and predicts Bayley cognitive, language and motor scores at 18 months. The comparison is against demographic and laboratory data alone, which the imaging measures beat across all three domains and across the whole outcome range rather than only at the extremes. This is the decision families are actually asking about after cooling.
records.headline_result: MRI-based measures predicted Bayley scores with higher correlation, more explained variance and smaller error than demographic and laboratory data alone, across cognitive, language and motor domains

records.title: Deep learning algorithm enables automated Cobb angle measurements with high accuracy.
records.model_family: commercial deep learning measurement software
records.clinical_problem: measuring Cobb angles on full spine radiographs, the number that drives bracing and surgical decisions in scoliosis
records.patient_population: 345 patients (mean age 33, range over 2 years), of whom 179 were under 22
records.model_description: Measures Cobb angles automatically on a full spine radiograph, against a ground truth built from three expert annotators with a consensus review where they disagreed. Accuracy was better in the pediatric subgroup than in adults, which is the right way round for a scoliosis tool: 1.9 degrees mean absolute error in children versus 3.3 in adults.
records.release_evidence: the DL software (BoneMetrics, Gleamer)
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 2.6 degrees overall for the main curvature, 1.9 degrees in patients under 22 and 3.3 degrees in adults

records.title: Multiparametric MRI along with machine learning predicts prognosis and treatment response in pediatric low-grade glioma.
records.model_family: radiomic signature with a clinicoradiomic survival model
records.clinical_problem: identifying which children with low-grade glioma have an immunologically active tumor that might respond to immunotherapy
records.patient_population: children with pediatric low-grade glioma with paired MRI and RNA sequencing
records.model_description: A radiogenomic study: RNA sequencing separates the tumors into three immunological clusters, one with heightened immune activity and worse prognosis, and then a radiomic signature learns to identify those clusters from MRI alone with over 80% accuracy. The practical claim is that an image could stand in for a biopsy transcriptome when deciding who might benefit from immunotherapy.
records.headline_result: radiomic signature predicted the immune cluster with over 80% accuracy; the clinicoradiomic model predicted progression-free survival and correlated with treatment response

records.title: Predicting pediatric patient rehabilitation outcomes after spinal deformity surgery with artificial intelligence.
records.model_family: six machine-learning models compared, with SHAP explainability and confidence calibration
records.clinical_problem: telling an adolescent before scoliosis surgery how they are likely to feel afterwards, which radiographic correction alone does not predict
records.patient_population: 455 pediatric patients undergoing spinal fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis at two Shriners Children's hospitals
records.model_description: Predicts individual SRS-22R quality-of-life responses at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years after scoliosis surgery from 171 preoperative features including the radiographic parameters. The premise is a real clinical gap: how much the curve is corrected does not correlate with how the patient reports feeling. The authors also calibrate model confidence so a clinician knows when to override it, and audit the model for fairness across groups.
records.dataset_size: 455 patients at two hospitals, 171 preoperative features
records.headline_result: area under the ROC curve 0.86, 0.85 and 0.83 for patient-reported outcomes at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years

records.title: Whole examination AI estimation of fetal biometrics from 20-week ultrasound scans.
records.model_family: frame classification network with Bayesian aggregation across the whole video
records.clinical_problem: fetal biometry currently rests on a handful of frames a sonographer chose, and the choice is a source of error
records.patient_population: 1,457 recordings of 20-week anomaly scans, comprising 48 million frames
records.model_description: Inverts how biometry is done. Instead of measuring the image the operator froze, it classifies every frame of the recorded scan, measures wherever the right anatomy is visible, and estimates the true value from that whole population of measurements with a Bayesian model that rejects outliers. The result is not just a number but a credible interval, which no manual measurement provides, and it needs no operator intervention.
records.headline_result: human-level performance in estimating fetal biometrics, with well-calibrated credible intervals for the true value

records.title: Fear extinction retention in children, adolescents, and adults.

records.title: Clinical validation of explainable AI for fetal growth scans through multi-level, cross-institutional prospective end-user evaluation.
records.model_family: progressive concept bottleneck model with segmentation
records.clinical_problem: giving the sonographer usable feedback during a fetal growth scan, rather than a verdict afterwards
records.patient_population: 9,352 annotated images for development and 100 prospectively collected videos across centres
records.model_description: Explains itself in the terms clinicians already use: whether the image is optimized, whether each anatomical landmark is present, and where those landmarks are. The evaluation is the unusual part — prospective, across centres, with clinicians judging whether the explanations were correct and whether they were useful, and a check that the model can tell an experienced operator from an inexperienced one. Most explainable-AI papers stop at the method; this one tests whether the explanations help.
records.dataset_size: 9,352 images for development, 100 videos for prospective evaluation
records.headline_result: 96.3% classification accuracy; plane-quality assessment on par with clinicians; explanations judged correct in 74-83% and useful in 72-75% of cases; reliably discriminated clinician experience levels (p < 0.01)
records.study_design: prospective cross-centre validation with end-user evaluation

records.title: Assessment of glymphatic function and white matter integrity in children with autism using multi-parametric MRI and machine learning.
records.model_family: AutoGluon automated machine learning on multi-parametric MRI indices
records.clinical_problem: detecting autism spectrum disorder on imaging rather than by behavioral assessment alone
records.patient_population: 110 children with autism and 68 typically developing children from two centers, with a held-out validation cohort
records.model_description: Measures glymphatic function (diffusion along the perivascular space), perivascular space volume, CSF volume and white matter anisotropy, then feeds those indices to an automated machine-learning framework to separate autistic from typically developing children. The glymphatic index also tracked autism severity and developmental delay, which is what makes this more than a classifier.
records.dataset_size: 178 children across two centers, with a separate validation cohort of 61
records.headline_result: area under the curve 0.84 for autism diagnosis; glymphatic index correlated with severity (r = -0.27) and developmental delay (r = 0.63)

records.title: Scanner-based real-time three-dimensional brain + body slice-to-volume reconstruction for T2-weighted 0.55-T low-field fetal magnetic resonance imaging.
records.model_family: deep learning slice-to-volume registration pipeline deployed through Gadgetron
records.clinical_problem: motion-corrected 3D fetal MRI has stayed a research technique because reconstruction happens offline, after the patient has gone home
records.patient_population: 12 prospective cases at 22-40 weeks gestation, plus 83 retrospective datasets
records.model_description: Puts fetal motion correction inside the scanner rather than in a research pipeline afterwards: reconstruction launches automatically during the examination and the 3D brain and body volumes appear on the console about seven minutes after the last stack, while the patient is still there. It is also the first such solution reported for a low-field 0.55-T scanner, which is the class of machine that could make fetal MRI more widely affordable.
records.headline_result: reconstructions available on the scanner console 6:42 ± 3:13 minutes after the final stack, rated good to acceptable for interpretation

records.title: Development and validation of fully automated robust deep learning models for multi-organ segmentation from whole-body CT images.
records.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
records.model_family: nnU-Net ensemble trained in two strategies with five-fold cross-validation
records.clinical_problem: having organ masks on a child's CT, which patient-specific dose calculation and any quantitative analysis depend on
records.patient_population: 4,082 CT images from several databases, including 300 pediatric cases
records.model_description: Segments 26 organs on a whole-body CT, trained deliberately across databases with very different acquisition so that it holds up on both children and adults. The comparison that matters is against TotalSegmentator, the field's default open tool, which it outperformed on every mutual organ — TotalSegmentator having been built on adult data.
records.headline_result: Dice above 0.90 for 17 of 26 organs; outperformed TotalSegmentator on all mutual organs across three test subsets

records.title: Association between deep learning radiomics based on placental MRI and preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction: A multicenter study.
records.model_family: deep learning radiomics on semi-supervised placental segmentation
records.clinical_problem: identifying preeclampsia and, within it, the pregnancies where the fetus is growth restricted
records.patient_population: 420 pregnant women across centres: 140 with preeclampsia (65 with fetal growth restriction) and 280 normotensive
records.model_description: Segments the placenta automatically on T2-weighted MRI and derives a combined radiomic and deep-learning signature that separates preeclamptic from normotensive pregnancies, and then separates those where the fetus is growth restricted. The discrimination is markedly better for the growth-restricted subgroup than for preeclampsia without restriction, which is the clinically consequential half.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.84-0.89 across training, test, internal and external validation for preeclampsia; 0.918 for preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction versus normotensive, and 0.742 without restriction; placental segmentation Dice 0.917

records.title: Automatic Quantification of Serial PET/CT Images for Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma Using a Longitudinally Aware Segmentation Network.
records.model_family: longitudinally aware segmentation network with cross-attention between timepoints
records.clinical_problem: deciding from the interim PET whether a child's Hodgkin lymphoma is responding, which determines how much treatment they receive
records.patient_population: 297 children in two Children's Oncology Group trials (median age 15.4 and 15.8 years), 200 internal and 97 external
records.model_description: Reads the baseline and interim PET together rather than separately, letting features from the first scan inform where to look on the second, which is how a physician actually reads a response study. It then produces the quantities that drive therapy decisions — metabolic tumor volume, total lesion glycolysis, qPET and the change in SUVmax — which correlated strongly with physician measurements. Trained and externally tested on cooperative group trial data.
records.headline_result: F1 0.61 for detecting residual lymphoma on interim PET, beating all comparators (P < .01); baseline segmentation Dice 0.77; Spearman correlation with physician measurements 0.78-0.96 across the four PET metrics
records.study_design: retrospective study on clinical trial cohorts with external testing

records.title: Applications of artificial intelligence and advanced imaging in pediatric diffuse midline glioma.
records.clinical_problem: characterizing diffuse midline glioma, a fatal childhood tumor that is often not biopsied
records.patient_population: children with diffuse midline glioma across the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A narrative review of MRI-based AI for diffuse midline glioma, sorted into classification, segmentation, radiogenomics and survival prediction, alongside the advanced sequences (diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, PET) that feed them. The obstacle it names is structural rather than technical: the disease is rare and there is no publicly available multi-institutional multimodal dataset, so every group works on its own small cohort.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted approach to assessing bowel wall thickness in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease using intestinal ultrasound images.
records.model_family: segmentation network with threshold-based classification
records.clinical_problem: measuring bowel wall thickness on intestinal ultrasound in children with inflammatory bowel disease, so that repeat endoscopy under sedation can be avoided
records.patient_population: 260 pediatric patients contributing 4,565 intestinal ultrasound images
records.model_description: Delineates the bowel wall between the lumen-mucosa and muscularis-serosa interfaces on intestinal ultrasound, computes the average wall thickness, and classifies the segment as normal or abnormal at a chosen cutoff. The clinical prize is stated plainly: intestinal ultrasound could replace repeated endoscopy under sedation and cross-sectional imaging, but only if someone can interpret it, and interpretation is the bottleneck this addresses.
records.headline_result: at a 2 mm wall thickness cutoff, sensitivity 90.3% and specificity 93.7% on 3,953 test images; agreement with manual measurement 0.942

records.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiological paediatric fracture assessment: an updated systematic review.
records.clinical_problem: detecting bone injury in children, now that both research and commercial algorithms exist for it
records.patient_population: children in the 26 reviewed studies, most on a single joint (wrist, elbow or ankle)
records.model_description: The 2025 update to the earlier pediatric fracture review, and the change in the field is visible: 17 of 26 eligible studies appeared in the previous two years, and seven now concern commercial tools. Accuracies run 85 to 100 percent, but only two of six reader studies found a statistically significant human improvement, and the largest reader pool in any study was eleven. The conclusion is that clinical impact, cost-effectiveness and bias remain unevidenced.
records.headline_result: AI accuracy 85.0-100.0% across studies; 2 of 6 reader studies showed significant improvement with AI assistance; 6 of 26 used open datasets

records.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: An Updated Systematic Review of Their Role in Obstetrics and Midwifery.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of AI across obstetrics and midwifery, spanning assisted reproduction, risk scores and fetal monitoring; not specific to fetal imaging

records.title: Three-dimensional markerless surface topography approach with convolutional neural networks for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis screening.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network on surface deviation and depth maps
records.clinical_problem: screening adolescents for scoliosis without the unnecessary referrals and radiographs that current screening generates
records.patient_population: 558 adolescents aged 10-18: 285 with confirmed adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (curves 10-45 degrees) and 273 with typically developing spines
records.model_description: The input is a 3D surface scan of the torso rather than a radiograph, which is the point: it quantifies trunk asymmetry by mirroring the torso geometry against itself and feeding the deviation and depth maps to a network. Scans came from two different capture devices. Like the photograph-based screening work, its value is in deciding who needs a radiograph rather than in replacing one.
records.headline_result: classification of scoliotic from typically developing torsos with 10-fold cross-validation; accuracy figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: Real-life benefit of artificial intelligence-based fracture detection in a pediatric emergency department.
records.model_family: commercially available deep learning fracture detection software
records.clinical_problem: whether a bought AI tool actually helps the inexperienced physician working nights in a pediatric emergency department
records.patient_population: 1,672 radiographs of children under 18 (median age 10.9 years) from a tertiary pediatric emergency department, in a consecutive real-life cohort and a selected medicolegal cohort
records.model_description: Two things make this the most useful of the fracture-AI studies for a department. It uses a consecutive real-life cohort rather than a balanced set, and it separately assembles the fractures that generate medicolegal claims, where the tool caught every proximal tibial fracture but only 68% of radial condyle fractures. The reader gain was modest, and in 2% of cases residents talked themselves out of a correct diagnosis because of the AI.
records.release_evidence: a commercially available, deep learning-based software
records.dataset_size: 1,672 radiographs, three pediatric residents as readers
records.headline_result: stand-alone sensitivity 92%, specificity 83%; resident accuracy rose from 88% to 90% with AI, and in 2% of cases readers discarded a correct diagnosis after seeing the AI output
records.study_design: retrospective reader study in a real-life cohort

records.title: Review of the Current State of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.clinical_problem: cardiac MRI in congenital heart disease is slow to acquire and slow to analyze, which limits how widely it can be used
records.patient_population: children and adults with congenital heart disease
records.model_description: A review of AI across the whole cardiac MRI pipeline in congenital heart disease: acquisition and reconstruction, then image processing and reporting, then clinical use cases. The framing is throughput rather than accuracy — the barrier to using cardiac MRI more in this population is how long each study takes to acquire and to read.

records.title: Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Precision Medicine in Necrotizing Enterocolitis and Neonatal Sepsis: A State-of-the-Art Review.
records.clinical_problem: predicting and diagnosing necrotizing enterocolitis early enough to change its course in preterm infants
records.patient_population: neonates, particularly preterm infants, across the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A state-of-the-art review of AI for necrotizing enterocolitis and neonatal sepsis, covering risk stratification from clinical variables, novel biomarkers, and deep learning on abdominal imaging, which it reports detects abnormality earlier than conventional reading. It names the usual obstacles — data heterogeneity, interpretability, no large-scale validation — which in this disease are compounded by how rare and how fast-moving it is.

records.title: Development and validation of an early diagnosis model for severe mycoplasma pneumonia in children based on interpretable machine learning.
records.exclusion_reason: early warning model for severe mycoplasma pneumonia built from serum biomarkers; chest CT contributes one variable among 21 serum indicators and no image is analyzed

records.title: Innovative Strategies in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Liver Cirrhosis and Associated Syndromes.
records.exclusion_reason: review of diagnosis and treatment of liver cirrhosis in adults; AI is one forward-looking paragraph

records.title: Comparative accuracy of two commercial AI algorithms for musculoskeletal trauma detection in emergency radiographs.
records.model_family: two commercial deep learning fracture detection algorithms
records.clinical_problem: choosing between competing commercial fracture detection products, and knowing where both of them fail
records.patient_population: 998 emergency musculoskeletal radiographs (585 normal, 413 abnormal) covering adults and children
records.model_description: Two marketed products on the same cases, which is the comparison a purchaser needs and vendors do not publish. They performed almost identically and agreed with each other almost perfectly, and performance was similar in adults and children. The shared weakness is the useful finding: subtle abnormalities made up about two-thirds of both algorithms' false negatives but under a fifth of their true positives.
records.release_evidence: compares two commercial AI algorithms, BoneView and RBfracture
records.headline_result: BoneView sensitivity 0.893 and specificity 0.885; RBfracture 0.872 and 0.892; no significant difference, kappa 0.81; subtle abnormalities were 66-70% of false negatives versus 18-20% of true positives (p < 0.001)

records.title: PET Imaging in Psychiatric Disorders.
records.exclusion_reason: review of PET imaging across psychiatric disorders; largely adult, and artificial intelligence is not the subject

records.title: Lack of children in public medical imaging data points to growing age bias in biomedical AI.
records.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
records.clinical_problem: whether children are represented at all in the data that medical imaging AI is built on
records.patient_population: 181 public medical imaging datasets surveyed; adult-trained chest radiograph models then tested on children
records.model_description: A systematic audit rather than a model. It finds children make up just under 1% of the data in 181 public imaging datasets, while most machine learning imaging conference papers build methods on exactly those datasets, and only 17% of FDA-approved medical AI devices carry a pediatric label. It then demonstrates the consequence directly: adult-trained chest radiograph models show significant age bias applied to children, with higher false positive rates in younger ones.
records.release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
records.headline_result: children are under 1% of data in 181 public imaging datasets; adult-trained chest radiograph models show higher false positive rates in younger children

records.title: Screen Time Is Associated With Cardiometabolic and Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Childhood and Adolescence.
records.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
records.exclusion_reason: association between screen time and cardiometabolic risk in children; the machine learning is applied to blood metabolomics and there is no imaging

records.title: Predicting task-related brain activity from resting-state brain dynamics with fMRI Transformer.
records.exclusion_reason: transformer predicting task activation maps from resting-state fMRI in adults and children; a neuroscience methods target rather than a clinical imaging one

records.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Pediatric Bone-Age Assessment: A Comparative Accuracy Analysis.
records.model_family: closed-source multimodal large language models, used without task-specific training
records.clinical_problem: whether a general-purpose chatbot can substitute for dedicated bone age software, which is expensive
records.patient_population: 180 left-hand wrist radiographs of children aged 0-18 from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age dataset
records.model_description: A clean negative result, and a useful one. Three general multimodal chatbots were asked to read bone age directly from the radiograph with no fine-tuning. They can do it, in the sense of producing plausible numbers, but errors of two to three years and limits of agreement beyond four and a half years put them nowhere near clinical or medico-legal use. Worth citing whenever someone proposes a general chatbot in place of dedicated software.
records.release_evidence: closed-source multimodal large language models
records.dataset_size: 180 radiographs from the public RSNA dataset
records.headline_result: best model (Gemini 2.5 Pro) mean absolute error 28.5 months; all models had 95% limits of agreement exceeding ±4.5 years

records.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
records.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
records.exclusion_reason: international consensus on diabetic macular edema; ophthalmic imaging is outside radiology as scoped here

records.title: Toward governance of artificial intelligence in pediatric healthcare.
records.clinical_problem: who is accountable when AI is used on a child, and what governance is missing
records.patient_population: children generally; the device analysis covers FDA-cleared pediatric software as a medical device
records.model_description: Reviews existing AI governance frameworks and names the pediatric gaps: too little stakeholder engagement, no developmentally appropriate consent or assent, thin bias mitigation, and unclear accountability. Its empirical contribution is an analysis of FDA-cleared pediatric software as a medical device showing radiology dominates while other pediatric specialties have almost nothing, which is the same concentration this database sees from the literature side.

records.title: The newborn delivery room of tomorrow: emerging and future technologies.
records.exclusion_reason: review of delivery room technologies for newborn resuscitation; artificial intelligence is one item in a list that is mostly monitoring hardware, and none of it is diagnostic imaging

records.title: Novel AI-Based Algorithm for the Automated Computation of Coronal Parameters in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients: A Validation Study on 100 Preoperative Full Spine X-Rays.
records.model_family: anatomical landmark detection with automated parameter computation
records.clinical_problem: computing the coronal parameters that classify an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve and guide surgical planning
records.patient_population: 100 preoperative full spine radiographs of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
records.model_description: Detects clavicles, cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine and sacrum and computes T1 tilt, clavicle angle, coronal balance, lumbar modifier and the regional Cobb angles, with no human input, on every image attempted. Agreement with two experienced raters was excellent, and the pattern of which parameters are hardest matched the humans' — proximal thoracic Cobb angle worst, coronal balance and clavicle angle best.
records.headline_result: intraclass correlation with human raters 0.78-0.98 across all parameters, computed on 100% of images; mean error 4.7 degrees for proximal thoracic Cobb angle and 0.2 degrees for clavicle angle

records.title: Automatic and human level Graf's type identification for detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip.
records.model_family: deep keypoint registration network with angle computation
records.clinical_problem: universal newborn screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, which ultrasound could deliver if there were enough experienced operators
records.patient_population: 986 neonates aged 0-6 months, with 2,406 images from 921 patients labeled by senior orthopedists
records.model_description: Places the five anatomical keypoints that Graf's method requires on a hip ultrasound and derives the alpha and beta angles from them, rather than classifying the image directly. That makes the output auditable against the classification system clinicians already use. The stated motivation is screening capacity: ultrasound is the right test for hip dysplasia, and the shortage of experienced operators is what prevents universal screening.
records.dataset_size: 2,406 images from 921 patients, of 986 neonates screened
records.headline_result: keypoint error about 1 mm, alpha angle correlation 0.89 with ground truth, AUC 0.937 for alpha below 60 degrees and 0.974 for below 50; experts agreed with 96% of inferred images

records.title: MRI-Based End-To-End Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma Segmentation and Classification.
records.journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
records.model_family: two-step U-Net cascade feeding a radiomics classifier
records.clinical_problem: predicting BRAF status in pediatric low-grade glioma without the manual tumor outlining that radiomics normally requires
records.patient_population: children with pediatric low-grade glioma
records.model_description: Removes the manual step that keeps radiomics out of practice: one network locates the tumor on a downsampled image, a second refines the outline on patches, and the automatic segmentation then feeds the genetic-marker classifier. The result worth noting is the comparison against the same radiomics model run on manual segmentations, which it nearly matched — meaning automation cost little accuracy.
records.headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.795; classification AUC 0.843 (two-class) and 0.730 (three-class) from automatic segmentations versus 0.874 and 0.758 from manual ones

records.title: Machine Learning Diagnosis of Small-Bowel Crohn Disease Using T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic and Clinical Data.
records.model_family: support vector machine on T2-weighted radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ileal Crohn disease on MR enterography, where reader performance and agreement vary considerably
records.patient_population: 135 participants (mean age 15.2 years), 70 with ileal Crohn disease, retrospectively identified and prospectively enrolled
records.model_description: Extracts radiomic features from four regions on non-contrast T2-weighted images and classifies ileal Crohn disease, with endoscopy and biopsy as the reference. The comparison against three fellowship-trained pediatric abdominal radiologists is the useful part, as is the finding that the bowel-core region carried nearly all the signal while mesenteric fat and whole-bowel regions performed worse.
records.headline_result: best region (bowel core) AUC 0.95 and accuracy 89.6%, against radiologist accuracies of 83.7-88.1% and consensus accuracy 88.1%

records.title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT and Bard in a Text-Based Radiology Knowledge Assessment.
records.journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
records.exclusion_reason: benchmark of two general chatbots on radiology board practice questions; pediatric radiology is one exam subspecialty and no imaging task is performed

records.title: Morphologic Severity and Age at Surgery Are Associated with School-Age Neurocognitive Outcomes in Metopic Craniosynostosis.
records.model_family: AI-derived morphological severity score from CT
records.clinical_problem: whether how severe a metopic craniosynostosis looks on imaging predicts how the child reads and learns at school age
records.patient_population: 41 children aged 6-18 with surgically corrected metopic synostosis, tested at a mean age of 10.8 years
records.model_description: Uses an AI-derived quantification of skull morphology severity, rather than a subjective grade, and relates it to neurocognitive testing years after surgery. Greater AI-derived severity was associated with poorer reading comprehension, and older age at surgery with poorer visuomotor integration. The cohort is small, but the design is the interesting one: an automated imaging measurement used as an exposure in a long-term outcome study rather than as a diagnostic output.
records.headline_result: greater AI-derived severity was significantly associated with lower reading comprehension and reading composite scores (P = 0.008-0.040)
records.study_design: retrospective cohort with long-term neurocognitive testing

records.title: Deep learning-based segmentation of whole-body fetal MRI and fetal weight estimation: assessing performance, repeatability, and reproducibility.
records.model_family: whole-body segmentation network with a quality estimation module
records.clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight, and detecting growth restriction, from MRI rather than ultrasound formulas
records.patient_population: 348 fetuses at 19-39 weeks: 249 appropriate for gestational age, 19 with growth restriction, 80 with other abnormalities
records.model_description: Segments the whole fetal body on MRI and derives an estimated weight, then builds an MRI-based normal growth chart from the normal cases. The evaluation is unusually thorough about the things that decide whether a measurement is usable: repeatability on repeat scans in the same scanner, reproducibility across scanners, and accuracy against actual birth weight. It correctly identified every fetus below the tenth birth-weight centile, and found three referred as normal who were in fact below the third.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.973, repeatability coefficient 4.01%, ICC 0.99; estimated weight differed from birth weight by -0.39% on average; correctly predicted all 18 fetuses below the 10th birth-weight centile
records.study_design: retrospective study with repeatability and reproducibility analysis

records.title: The unintended consequences of artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology.
records.clinical_problem: the harms AI can cause in a pediatric setting that are not visible from its accuracy figures
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
records.model_description: A deliberately sceptical companion to the enthusiastic reviews: it works through AI ethics, bias, limitations and unintended consequences for patients, for society and for the profession, with attention to what is specific about a pediatric population. Worth reading alongside the position statements rather than instead of them.

records.title: Validation of machine-learning model for first-trimester prediction of pre-eclampsia using cohort from PREVAL study.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.exclusion_reason: first-trimester pre-eclampsia risk model from maternal history, blood pressure and serum biomarkers with one Doppler index; a maternal outcome rather than a fetal imaging task

records.title: Deep-learning model for prenatal congenital heart disease screening generalizes to community setting and outperforms clinical detection.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: deep learning classifier, previously trained at a tertiary center
records.clinical_problem: congenital heart defects missed at the routine second-trimester anomaly scan in a low-risk population
records.patient_population: 66 pregnancies with isolated severe congenital heart disease and 42 normal fetuses from a Dutch region, screened in community practice in 2015-2016
records.model_description: Takes a model developed on tertiary-center images and tests it on stored images from ordinary community screening, which is the transfer that usually breaks. It did not: the model reached 91% sensitivity where the original clinical reading had caught only half the cases, and where three blinded human experts working from the same stored images averaged 55%. Model correctness varied with image quality, which points at where the remaining errors come from.
records.headline_result: model sensitivity 91% and specificity 78%, versus 53% sensitivity for the original clinical diagnosis and 55% for blinded human experts on the same stored images

records.title: External validation of an artificial intelligence solution for the detection of elbow fractures and joint effusions in children.
records.model_family: commercial deep learning fracture and effusion detection
records.clinical_problem: elbow trauma in children, where the fracture is often invisible and only a joint effusion betrays it
records.patient_population: 712 children (mean age 7.3 years, range 7 months to 15 years) presenting consecutively to an emergency room with elbow trauma
records.model_description: An external validation on consecutive real emergency attendances, scored four ways including detection of joint effusion, which is the finding that matters most in a child's elbow because the fracture itself frequently is not visible. Eleven senior radiologists set the reference. The authors end on the number a department should weigh: 8% of the radiographic sets the algorithm called normal came from children who did have a traumatic lesion.
records.release_evidence: external validation of an AI solution
records.headline_result: sensitivity above 89% on all four approaches, highest at 95.0% for lesion detection; specificity 63-77%; 8% of sets ruled out by the algorithm belonged to children with a genuine traumatic lesion

records.title: Total and Regional Brain Volumes in Fetuses With Congenital Heart Disease.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.exclusion_reason: case-control comparison of fetal brain volumes in congenital heart disease; the segmentation network is a measurement tool and the study's subject is the biological difference, not the model

records.title: Deeplasia: deep learning for bone age assessment validated on skeletal dysplasias.
records.model_family: ensemble of convolutional neural networks, prior-free
records.clinical_problem: bone age in children with skeletal dysplasia, where the hand is malformed and general bone age tools have not been validated
records.patient_population: the public RSNA challenge set for training, plus 568 radiographs from 189 patients with molecularly confirmed diagnoses of seven genetic bone disorders including achondroplasia
records.model_description: Most bone age models are validated on ordinary hands; this one is deliberately tested where the anatomy is abnormal, in children with molecularly confirmed skeletal dysplasias whose growth monitoring depends on serial bone age. It also measures test-retest precision on longitudinal images, which matters more than single-scan accuracy when the number is used to time hormone treatment or surgery.
records.release_evidence: an open-source prior-free deep-learning approach
records.dataset_size: 14,236 RSNA radiographs for training; 568 dysplastic radiographs from 189 patients
records.headline_result: mean absolute difference 3.87 months on the RSNA test set and 5.84 months on the dysplastic cohort
records.study_design: retrospective development with disease-specific external validation

records.title: Interpretable and intervenable ultrasonography-based machine learning models for pediatric appendicitis.
records.model_family: multiview concept bottleneck model
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis, management and severity of suspected appendicitis in children, from the ultrasound that is already being done
records.patient_population: 579 pediatric patients with 1,709 ultrasound images plus clinical and laboratory data
records.model_description: The model predicts through an intermediate layer of concepts a clinician can read and correct — appendix diameter, wall layering, free fluid — rather than straight from pixels to a label. That means a radiologist who disagrees can intervene on the concept rather than override a black box. It matched comparable black-box networks on the same data, and it does not require the time-consuming image annotation at deployment.
records.headline_result: AUROC 0.80 and area under the precision-recall curve 0.92 for diagnosis, comparable to black-box networks on the same dataset

records.title: Innovative advances in pediatric radiology: computed tomography reconstruction techniques, photon-counting detector computed tomography, and beyond.
records.model_family: deep learning image reconstruction
records.clinical_problem: keeping pediatric CT dose as low as possible without losing the diagnosis
records.patient_population: children undergoing CT
records.model_description: Covers the two technologies that are actually changing pediatric CT dose: deep learning image reconstruction, which the authors report outperforms filtered back projection particularly in pediatric head and cardiac CT, and photon-counting detector CT, which gives high resolution at substantially lower dose and is especially valuable for children imaged repeatedly. It also covers cloud-based dose tracking, and is candid about the data, compute and privacy costs of deploying any of it.
records.release_evidence: the reviewed reconstruction technologies are described as available on clinical scanners

records.title: Artificial intelligence as a new answer to old challenges in maternal-fetal medicine and obstetrics.
records.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
records.clinical_problem: diagnostic accuracy and examination time in perinatal ultrasound, and fetal monitoring in labor
records.patient_population: pregnancies undergoing obstetric care, across the reviewed literature to August 2023
records.model_description: A clinician-facing review of AI in maternal-fetal medicine, with obstetric ultrasound as its main imaging strand: the argument is that AI can shorten the examination and improve accuracy at once, which is a workload claim as much as a diagnostic one. It closes on interpretability and reliability as the conditions for implementation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based detection of paediatric appendicular skeletal fractures: performance and limitations for common fracture types and locations.
records.model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection algorithm
records.clinical_problem: which pediatric fracture types a marketed AI tool actually detects, including indirect signs and dislocations that earlier studies ignored
records.patient_population: up to 1,000 radiographs per body part from a single emergency department, children aged 0-18
records.model_description: The most clinically pointed of the fracture-detection validations, because it breaks performance down by injury type rather than reporting one headline number. Overall accuracy is high for forearm and lower leg, but the tool essentially missed the characteristically pediatric injuries: toddler's fractures, trampoline fractures, proximal tibial Salter-Harris II, and one of eleven radial and none of seven ulnar bowing fractures. Elbow dislocation sensitivity was 66% with a 50% positive predictive value.
records.release_evidence: assessment of an existing AI tool, BoneView (Gleamer, Paris, France)
records.dataset_size: up to 1,000 radiographs per body part; 607 lower leg, 1,137 forearm and 517 elbow fractures
records.headline_result: forearm sensitivity 92.9% and specificity 98.1%; lower leg 87.5%/87.5%; elbow sensitivity 80.5%; bowing fractures and several pediatric-specific fracture types largely undetected; elbow dislocation sensitivity 65.8% with 50% positive predictive value

records.title: Machine Learning-Derived Active Sleep as an Early Predictor of White Matter Development in Preterm Infants.
records.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
records.exclusion_reason: the machine learning classifies sleep stage from heart and respiratory rate; MRI white matter volume is the outcome measured, not the model input

records.title: Automated bone age assessment in a German pediatric cohort: agreement between an artificial intelligence software and the manual Greulich and Pyle method.
records.model_family: commercial AI bone age software
records.clinical_problem: whether a bone age product can be swapped in for an expert reader, not merely correlate with one
records.patient_population: 306 children aged 1-18 (153 boys, 153 girls, 18 per year of life) in a German cohort
records.model_description: Tests interchangeability rather than agreement, which is the stricter and more decision-relevant question: can the software substitute for one of three blinded expert readers without changing the answer. It could, within the age range the product is declared for. Performance was slightly worse in boys, and the bias was constant across the range rather than drifting at the extremes.
records.release_evidence: evaluates an AI software with a declared intended-use age range
records.dataset_size: 306 children, 243 in the declared intended-use subgroup
records.headline_result: mean difference from the three-expert average 0.39 months, mean absolute difference 6.8 months (6.0 months in the intended-use subgroup); judged interchangeable with expert readers

records.title: Advances in the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Echocardiography.
records.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
records.clinical_problem: operator dependence in fetal echocardiography, where missing congenital heart disease costs survival
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography, across the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A systematic review of AI in fetal echocardiography organized by what the model does: image processing, biometry, and disease diagnosis. Its framing is the skill gap — fetal echocardiography depends heavily on operator experience and equipment, and the argument for AI here is bridging that gap between regions rather than outperforming an expert.

records.title: The Application of Large Language Models for Radiologic Decision Making.
records.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
records.exclusion_reason: benchmarking large language models against ACR Appropriateness Criteria across 11 expert panels; pediatrics is one panel and no pediatric imaging is analyzed

records.title: Automatic dental age calculation from panoramic radiographs using deep learning: a two-stage approach with object detection and image classification.
records.exclusion_reason: dental age calculation from panoramic radiographs; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence in paediatric dentistry: A systematic review on deep learning algorithms for dental anomaly detection.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of deep learning for dental anomaly detection in pediatric dentistry; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Using brain structural neuroimaging measures to predict psychosis onset for individuals at clinical high-risk.
records.model_family: machine learning classifier on harmonized structural MRI measures
records.clinical_problem: predicting which clinically high-risk individuals will go on to develop psychosis
records.patient_population: 1,165 individuals at clinical high risk and 1,029 healthy controls from 21 sites; the analysis is framed around adolescent brain development
records.model_description: Trains on the clinical high-risk individuals who later converted versus healthy controls, harmonizing subcortical volume, cortical thickness and surface area across 21 sites before modelling. Applied to the non-converters and the unknown-outcome group, most were classified as healthy, which is the behaviour a screening tool should show. Accuracy falls from 85% in training to 73% in the independent confirmatory set.
records.headline_result: 85% accuracy on training and 73% on the independent confirmatory dataset; 30% of converters classified as healthy versus 73% of non-converters and 80% of unknown-outcome individuals
records.study_design: multisite retrospective study with external validation

records.title: Role of artificial-intelligence-assisted automated cardiac biometrics in prenatal screening for coarctation of aorta.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: AI plane detection and biometry feeding a logistic regression predictor
records.clinical_problem: coarctation of the aorta, which is missed before birth in about 60% of cases and where prenatal detection changes survival
records.patient_population: 73 fetuses with a postnatal diagnosis of coarctation and 7,300 matched healthy controls from four Danish regions, 2008-2018
records.model_description: Rather than classifying the image directly, the model finds the standard cardiac planes and measures them automatically, and those measurements — ventricle areas and lengths, right-to-left ventricle area ratio, great vessel diameter ratio — go into a conventional regression. That makes the prediction inspectable in terms clinicians already use, at the routine 18-22 week anomaly scan rather than at a specialist referral.
records.headline_result: area under the ROC curve 0.96, with 90.4% sensitivity at 88.9% specificity

records.title: Dental Caries diagnosis from bitewing images using convolutional neural networks.
records.exclusion_reason: caries diagnosis on dental bitewing radiographs; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Commercially available artificial intelligence tools for fracture detection: the evidence.
records.clinical_problem: which commercial fracture-detection product to buy, and what evidence actually exists behind each
records.patient_population: adults and children, per each product's stated target population
records.model_description: Reviews the commercially available fracture-detection tools one by one and summarizes the evidence, or the absence of it, behind each — including how each was developed, what validation exists, and who the intended target population is, which the authors note is often unclear from vendor material. It flags a pediatric-specific stake: a missed fracture in a child can also mean a missed safeguarding opportunity.
records.release_evidence: reviews the range of available commercial products using AI for fracture detection

records.title: MRI-based synthetic CT for assessment of the bony elements of the sacroiliac joints in children.
records.model_family: MRI-to-CT synthesis network
records.clinical_problem: assessing the bony sacroiliac joints in children, which conventionally needs a CT and therefore ionizing radiation
records.patient_population: 10 children aged 9-16 (mean 14 years) who had a PET-CT and an additional MRI
records.model_description: Generates a CT-like image from MRI so the cortical detail of the sacroiliac joints can be assessed without irradiating a child. Two readers compared synthetic against real CT on specific bony features — cortical delineation, joint facet defects, growth plate fusion, ossified nuclei, bony bridges — and on quantitative measurements, with agreement from substantial to perfect. The cohort is very small, which is the main limitation on the equivalence claim.
records.headline_result: perfect agreement for cortical delineation, bony bridges and joint facet defects; measurements statistically equivalent to CT within a 1 mm margin; inter-reader ICC 0.806-0.998

records.title: AI Education for Fourth-Year Medical Students: Two-Year Experience of a Web-Based, Self-Guided Curriculum and Mixed Methods Study.
records.exclusion_reason: curriculum evaluation for teaching AI to medical students; not an imaging study

records.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Label Free-Text Operative and Ultrasound Reports for Grading Pediatric Appendicitis.
records.model_family: large language model prompted to structure free text
records.clinical_problem: turning free-text ultrasound and operative reports into the structured data that appendicitis research and grading depend on
records.patient_population: 103 randomly selected anonymized ultrasound and operative records from a series of 2,100 children operated on for acute appendicitis
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model but a data-extraction one, and the comparison is against trained human abstractors rather than against a machine baseline. Of the discordant fields, 98% of the errors were the humans'; the model assigned the appendicitis severity grade wrongly in 3% of cases against 28% manually, and worked roughly forty times faster. Anyone building a pediatric imaging dataset from an electronic record should read this before hiring abstractors.
records.headline_result: 98% of discordant-field errors were in manual extraction; appendicitis grade misassigned in 28.2% of cases manually versus 2.9% by the model, about 40 times faster
records.study_design: retrospective comparison against manual data extraction

records.title: Noninvasive Molecular Subtyping of Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma with Self-Supervised Transfer Learning.
records.model_family: self-supervised label cross-training on a pretrained medical imaging network
records.clinical_problem: determining BRAF mutational status in pediatric low-grade glioma without a biopsy
records.patient_population: 214 children at Dana-Farber/Boston Children's for development and 112 from the Children's Brain Tumor Network for external testing
records.model_description: A scan-to-prediction pipeline: it segments the tumor on a routine T2 image, then classifies BRAF wild type versus BRAF fusion versus BRAF V600E section by section. The distinction matters because V600E tumors have targeted therapy available. Performance drops from internal to external testing, which the authors report plainly, and they add a center-of-mass metric to check the model is actually attending to the tumor.
records.dataset_size: 214 children for development, 112 for external testing
records.headline_result: internal AUC 0.82-0.87 across the three classes, falling to 0.72-0.78 on external testing
records.study_design: retrospective two-cohort study with external validation

records.title: Deep learning methods for fully automated dental age estimation on orthopantomograms.
records.exclusion_reason: dental age estimation from orthopantomograms; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Emergency front-of-neck access in pediatric anesthesia: A narrative review.
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review of emergency front-of-neck airway access in children; artificial intelligence is mentioned among training tools and there is no imaging model

records.title: Automated body organ segmentation, volumetry and population-averaged atlas for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal body MRI.
records.model_family: neural network organ segmentation with a population-averaged atlas
records.clinical_problem: volumetry of fetal organs, which is currently done by slice-by-slice manual segmentation of motion-corrupted stacks
records.patient_population: 91 normal control fetal 3T MRI datasets across 22-38 weeks gestational age
records.model_description: Supplies the two things missing before fetal organ volumetry can be automated: a parcellation protocol defining ten organ regions, which did not previously exist in any standard form, and the first population-averaged T2-weighted atlas of the fetal body. The network trained on that protocol then produced organ growth charts across gestation that behaved as expected, which is the sanity check for a normative tool.
records.headline_result: robust segmentation across gestational ages, with organ growth charts from 22-38 weeks showing the expected volume increase

records.title: A precision functional atlas of personalized network topography and probabilities.
records.exclusion_reason: normative functional network atlas resource for brain-wide association studies and neuromodulation targeting; no diagnostic or prognostic imaging model
records.release_evidence: described as an open-source, method-flexible atlas with an online interface

records.title: AI-Assisted X-ray Fracture Detection in Residency Training: Evaluation in Pediatric and Adult Trauma Patients.
records.model_family: machine learning fracture detection algorithm used as a reading aid
records.clinical_problem: whether AI assistance helps radiology residents find fractures, and what that means for training
records.patient_population: 200 radiographs from patients aged 1 to 95 (mean 40.7 years), half containing at least one fracture, read by four residents of differing experience
records.model_description: A reader study framed around residency training rather than around the algorithm. Residents gained 19 points of sensitivity with the aid, at essentially no cost in specificity, with the largest gains for the least experienced. The authors raise the training question directly: a tool that lifts a trainee to expert-level detection also removes the errors trainees learn from.
records.headline_result: resident sensitivity rose from 58% to 77% with AI (p < 0.001) with specificity unchanged; stand-alone AI sensitivity 93% at 77% specificity; interpretation time fell and confidence rose

records.title: Artificial intelligence improves resident detection of pediatric and young adult upper extremity fractures.

records.patient_population: 240 patients (mean age 11.3 years, range 0-22, 37.9% female) with elbow, hand, humerus, wrist, forearm and clavicle radiographs
records.model_description: An openly accessible model, which is unusual in this literature and is the point: it is available at childfx.com rather than sold. Seven readers across three experience levels read the same cases with and without it. Residents and pediatric residents improved substantially; subspecialist musculoskeletal radiologists did not. With the model, residents reached the same accuracy as unaided subspecialists, and everyone read faster.

The argument for the database is a caution: automated segmentation can only be as consistent as the manual ground truth it learns from, so definitions have to be agreed before the models can help.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence vs. Doctors: Diagnosing Necrotizing Enterocolitis on Abdominal Radiographs.
records.model_family: ResNet-50 transfer learning with Grad-CAM
records.clinical_problem: recognizing pneumatosis intestinalis on a neonatal abdominal radiograph, the radiographic call that decides whether necrotizing enterocolitis is diagnosed
records.patient_population: 494 anteroposterior neonatal abdominal radiographs, 214 with necrotizing enterocolitis
records.model_description: Trained to recognize pneumatosis on neonatal abdominal radiographs and compared directly against senior surgical residents, who are often the ones making this call overnight. It matched every resident individually, and the attention maps confirmed it was looking at the right part of the film. Necrotizing enterocolitis is a diagnosis where hours matter and the radiographic sign is subtle, which is what makes this comparison the relevant one.
records.headline_result: AUROC 0.918 and accuracy 87.8%, statistically indistinguishable from each senior surgical resident (median resident AUROC 0.896)
records.study_design: retrospective cohort study with reader comparison

records.title: Stepwise Transfer Learning for Expert-level Pediatric Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation in a Limited Data Scenario.
records.model_family: stepwise in-domain transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: segmenting pediatric brain tumors for volumetric response assessment, when there is not enough pediatric data to train on directly
records.patient_population: 184 children from a national brain tumor consortium (median age 7) and 100 from a pediatric cancer center (median age 8), with an independent external test set
records.model_description: The methodological point is training in steps within the domain rather than transferring once from natural images, which is what makes expert-level accuracy reachable on a few hundred pediatric scans. The evaluation is unusually strong: three clinicians rated segmentations blind, and rated the model's higher than each other's, correctly identifying which were machine-made only a quarter of the time.
records.dataset_size: 284 children for development, plus an independent external test set
records.headline_result: median Dice 0.88 in development and 0.82 on external testing; clinicians rated AI segmentations at median Likert 9 versus 7 for other experts, and judged 80.2% clinically acceptable versus 65.4%
records.study_design: retrospective multi-cohort study with blinded clinician evaluation

records.title: Diagnostic performance of an AI algorithm for the detection of appendicular bone fractures in pediatric patients.
records.model_family: deep learning fracture detection algorithm trained on adult and pediatric data
records.clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in children with a tool that was trained on a mixed adult and pediatric population
records.patient_population: 600 extremity radiographs from patients under 17 (mean age 8.9 years), balanced positive and negative, grouped by body part
records.model_description: Evaluates a fracture algorithm at three levels — per patient, per radiograph and per anatomical location — with follow-up radiographs or second-level imaging as the reference rather than the original report. The per-location analysis is the informative one: of 606 bounding boxes the model drew, 78% were correct and 18% were in the wrong place, so a fracture called at the wrong site is a meaningful fraction of its output.
records.headline_result: per-patient sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 76.7%, accuracy 84%; per-radiograph accuracy 87.2%; of 606 bounding boxes, 77.9% correct and 18.1% incorrectly located

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of an Integrated AI Tool to Estimate Gestational Age From Blind Ultrasound Sweeps.

records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where no trained sonographer and no high-specification machine is available
records.patient_population: 400 individuals with viable single first-trimester pregnancies in Lusaka, Zambia and Chapel Hill, North Carolina
records.model_description: The productized form of the blind-sweep gestational age model: the algorithm ships inside a cheap battery-powered probe, and the study puts it in the hands of novice users with no sonography training at all. Ground truth was set by transvaginal crown-rump length in the first trimester, so the comparison is against a fact rather than against another estimate. It met prespecified equivalence to credentialed sonographers doing standard biometry.
records.release_evidence: incorporated into the software of a low-cost, battery-powered device
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.2 days for novice users with the AI device versus 3.0 days for credentialed sonographers (difference 0.2 days, within the prespecified 2-day equivalence margin)

records.model_description: A systematic review of the prediction half of scoliosis AI: which radiological and clinical factors have been used to forecast curve progression, and with what models. It reports that machine learning gives higher precision than the traditional progression rules, but that interpretability and data complexity keep it in the research literature; multi-centre work is what would move it.

records.title: Applications of artificial intelligence for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: mapping the evidence.
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, stratifying who will progress, and guiding treatment
records.patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis, across 40 reviewed articles
records.model_description: Maps what AI has been used for in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: 62.5% of the work is imaging analysis, mostly automatic Cobb angle and vertebral rotation measurement and curve classification, and 37.5% is prediction, mostly of curve progression. The limiting finding is governance rather than accuracy — only 15 of 40 studies offered any clinical implementation guidance, and external validation and model transparency are largely absent.

records.headline_result: average reported model accuracy 85.4% among the 52.5% of studies that reported it; only 37.5% gave clinical implementation guidance
