records.title: CortexODE: Learning Cortical Surface Reconstruction by Neural ODEs.
records.model_family: neural ordinary differential equation learning a diffeomorphic flow, inside a pipeline with a 3D U-Net white matter segmentation and topology correction
records.clinical_problem: reconstructing cortical surfaces from brain MRI, the step that conventional pipelines spend hours on and that every cortical thickness or folding measurement depends on
records.patient_population: large-scale neuroimaging datasets across age groups including neonates at 25-45 weeks, young adults 22-36 years and elderly subjects 55-90 years
records.model_description: Modeling the surface deformation as an ODE with a Lipschitz-continuous network buys a theoretical guarantee rather than an empirical one: the flow cannot self-intersect, which is the failure mode that makes conventional surface reconstruction need manual repair. Neonates at 25-45 weeks are one of the three evaluation cohorts, and they are the hardest - thin, low-contrast cortex in a rapidly changing brain. Hours become under five seconds.
records.dataset_size: large-scale public neuroimaging datasets spanning neonates, young adults and elderly subjects
records.headline_result: under 0.2 mm average geometric error, orders of magnitude faster than conventional pipelines, reconstructing surfaces in under 5 seconds

records.title: Deep learning reconstruction in pediatric brain MRI: comparison of image quality with conventional T2-weighted MRI.
records.model_family: vendor deep learning MRI reconstruction
records.clinical_problem: image quality in pediatric brain MRI at 3 T, where noise, truncation artifact and motion degrade the study and children tolerate long acquisitions poorly
records.patient_population: 107 consecutive children who underwent 3.0 T brain MRI, with 36 lesions among them
records.model_description: A straight three-way comparison on the same acquisitions - deep learning reconstruction, conventional intensity filtering, and the unfiltered original - read independently by two pediatric radiologists. The finding that matters clinically is lesion conspicuity, not noise: quieter images that hid lesions would be worse, and these did not. Truncation artifact, a specific and common nuisance on pediatric T2, fell significantly; motion and pulsation artifacts did not change, which is the honest limit of what reconstruction can fix.
records.release_evidence: a deep learning reconstruction mode available on the clinical scanner, compared against the scanner's conventional reconstruction
records.headline_result: significantly better overall image quality, noisiness and gray-white matter sharpness and fewer truncation artifacts than conventional or original reconstruction (all P < 0.001), with better lesion conspicuity and lower signal variation

records.title: Generalizability and Bias in a Deep Learning Pediatric Bone Age Prediction Model Using Hand Radiographs.
records.model_name: 2017 RSNA Bone Age Challenge winning model
records.model_family: deep learning bone age regression network
records.clinical_problem: whether an expert-level bone age model holds up outside its development hospitals and whether its errors fall evenly across demographic groups
records.patient_population: trained on 12 611 pediatric hand radiographs from two U.S. hospitals; tested on an internal validation set of 1425 children and an external set of 1202 children (mean age 133 months) with diverse demographic representation
records.model_description: The audit that the bone-age literature needed. It takes the challenge winner and asks the two questions a hospital would ask before deployment - does it generalize, and is it fair - and gets different answers to each. Generalization was clean, with no difference between internal and external error. Fairness was not: error differed by sex, and 16 percent of external predictions would have been clinically significant errors. A useful cautionary reference for any pediatric AI procurement discussion.
records.dataset_size: 12 611 training radiographs; 1425 internal and 1202 external test children
records.headline_result: mean absolute difference 6.8 months internally versus 6.9 months externally (P = .64), but 194 of 1202 external predictions (16%) would have changed the clinical diagnosis, and error was greater for girls than boys
records.study_design: retrospective external validation and bias audit

records.title: Pediatric magnetic resonance imaging: faster is better.
records.clinical_problem: long MRI acquisition times in young children, which force sedation or produce non-diagnostic studies
records.patient_population: children undergoing MRI
records.model_description: A practical framework for accelerating pediatric MRI, written from the authors' own deployment experience: parallel imaging, single-shot acquisition, controlled aliasing, compressed sensing and AI-based reconstruction, combined with the right hardware and pulse sequences. The argument is stated in departmental terms — shorter scans mean less sedation, fewer motion artifacts, more throughput.

It also collects the publicly available datasets and the performance metrics the field uses, and closes on why so little of this work has reached clinical practice.

records.title: Detecting pediatric wrist fractures using deep-learning-based object detection.
records.model_family: Faster R-CNN object detection
records.clinical_problem: subtle buckle fractures of the distal radius, which are the classic missed pediatric fracture
records.patient_population: 395 pediatric posteroanterior wrist radiographs, 65% with fracture and 30% with a distal radial buckle fracture
records.model_description: Detects and boxes wrist fractures, targeting the buckle fracture specifically because it is subtle and characteristically pediatric. Four trainees read the cases with and without the box. Both pediatric and radiology residents improved sharply, and — unusually — when reader and model disagreed after the model's prediction was shown, the residents were right nearly three times out of four, which suggests the box informed rather than overrode them.
records.dataset_size: 395 radiographs (229 train, 41 tune, 125 test), four readers
records.headline_result: AUC 0.92 and accuracy 88%, detecting 90% of buckle fractures; resident accuracy rose from 80% to 93% for any fracture and 69% to 92% for buckle fractures (both P < 0.001)

records.title: Superficial white matter analysis: An efficient point-cloud-based deep learning framework with supervised contrastive learning for consistent tractography parcellation across populations and dMRI acquisitions.
records.model_family: point-cloud network with supervised contrastive learning
records.clinical_problem: parcellating the superficial white matter, which most tract-segmentation methods avoid because of its complexity
records.patient_population: six independently acquired datasets spanning ages and health conditions, including neonates and patients with space-occupying brain tumors
records.model_description: Classifies tractography streamlines into 198 superficial white matter clusters, working on the streamline as a point cloud rather than on an image grid, with contrastive learning to separate plausible streamlines from outliers. The evidence that matters is the breadth of testing: six independently acquired datasets covering neonates through old age and including brains distorted by tumors, where registration-based parcellation typically fails.
records.dataset_size: large-scale training tractography plus six independent test datasets
records.headline_result: highly consistent and accurate parcellation across all six datasets including neonates and tumor patients, and much faster than comparators

records.title: iBEAT V2.0: a multisite-applicable, deep learning-based pipeline for infant cerebral cortical surface reconstruction.
records.model_family: deep-learning processing pipeline
records.clinical_problem: measuring cortical development in infants, whose brain MRI defeats adult-designed processing tools
records.patient_population: infants from birth to 6 years of age, across many imaging sites, protocols and scanners
records.model_description: An end-to-end pipeline for infant brain MRI: preprocessing, skull stripping, tissue segmentation, topology correction, cortical surface reconstruction and measurement. Infant scans are hard because myelination makes gray and white matter nearly isointense at some ages, and adult tools fail on them. Trained only on Baby Connectome Project data but shown to hold up on other sites, scanners and both T1- and T2-weighted images.
records.release_evidence: maintained as a public service at http://www.ibeat.cloud, which has processed over 16,000 infant MRI scans from more than 100 institutions
records.dataset_size: trained on the Baby Connectome Project; the public service has processed over 16,000 scans
records.headline_result: superior accuracy and robustness to existing pipelines across multisite, multimodal and multi-age datasets

records.title: Comparison of diagnostic performance of a deep learning algorithm, emergency physicians, junior radiologists and senior radiologists in the detection of appendicular fractures in children.
records.model_family: deep neural network fracture detection algorithm
records.clinical_problem: detecting fractures in children, where anatomical variation with age makes the task specific and a missed fracture can affect growth
records.patient_population: 878 patients under 18 with radiographs of shoulder, arm, elbow, forearm, wrist, hand, leg, knee, ankle and foot after non-life-threatening trauma
records.model_description: Places the algorithm on a ladder of readers rather than against a single comparator: pediatric radiologists, senior residents, junior residents and emergency physicians all read the same cases against an expert consensus. The model sat between pediatric radiologists and senior residents, above emergency physicians and junior residents, and found three fractures the pediatric radiologists had initially missed.
records.headline_result: sensitivity 95.6%, specificity 91.6%, negative predictive value 98.8%; against 98.4% for pediatric radiologists, 95.1% for senior residents, 90.1% for junior residents and 81.9% for emergency physicians

records.title: Machine learning for accurate estimation of fetal gestational age based on ultrasound images.
records.model_family: machine learning image analysis of standard ultrasound planes, using no measurement inputs
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters, where biometry assumes an average fetal size at each gestational age and its error widens to at least two weeks as growth deviates from that average
records.patient_population: two independent ultrasound datasets, one for training and internal validation and one for external validation, with gestational age ground truth from a reliable last menstrual period date confirmed by first-trimester crown-rump length
records.model_description: Attacks the assumption rather than the measurement. Conventional dating converts size to age through a population growth curve, so any fetus off the average is mis-dated - which is exactly the growth-restricted fetus whose dating matters most. Reading the image directly, with no measurements at all, sidesteps that and the paper shows it holds up in intrauterine growth restriction. Blinded external validation against first-trimester-confirmed dates is the right standard and rarely met in this literature.
records.dataset_size: two independent datasets, sizes not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.0 days (95% CI 2.9-3.2) in the second trimester and 4.3 days (95% CI 4.1-4.5) in the third, better than current ultrasound-based clinical biometry at those ages
records.study_design: retrospective model development with blinded external validation

records.title: Automated tumor segmentation and brain tissue extraction from multiparametric MRI of pediatric brain tumors: A multi-institutional study.
records.model_family: DeepMedic, a 3D convolutional neural network
records.clinical_problem: delineating pediatric brain tumor subregions for surgery, treatment planning and response monitoring
records.patient_population: 244 children with de novo brain tumors of varied subtype: 215 internal and 29 from an external institution
records.model_description: Extracts the brain and then segments the tumor into enhancing, non-enhancing, cystic and edematous components from four routine sequences. Performance held up on a withheld external cohort, which matters because most pediatric tumor segmentation work is single-institution. The subregion breakdown is what makes it usable for response assessment rather than only for volume.
records.dataset_size: 244 children (151 training, 43 validation, 21 internal test, 29 external test)
records.headline_result: Dice 0.91 internal and 0.88 external for whole tumor, 0.73/0.84 for enhancing tumor, and 0.98 for brain tissue

records.title: PediCXR: An open, large-scale chest radiograph dataset for interpretation of common thoracic diseases in children.
records.model_family: annotated dataset release rather than a model
records.clinical_problem: the shortage of physician-annotated pediatric chest radiographs that has kept pediatric CXR AI far behind adult CXR AI
records.patient_population: 9125 studies retrospectively collected from a major pediatric hospital in Vietnam between 2020 and 2021, each read by a pediatric radiologist with more than ten years of experience
records.model_description: Infrastructure, and the most consequential kind for this field. Adult chest radiograph AI advanced because large annotated datasets existed and pediatric CXR AI did not; PediCXR is a direct attempt to close that gap. What distinguishes it from re-used public collections is lesion-level annotation - 36 findings and 15 diseases, each abnormality drawn as a bounding box, not merely an image-level label - with a fixed 7728/1397 split so results are comparable across groups. Publicly released on PhysioNet.
records.release_evidence: the dataset is publicly available on PhysioNet at https://physionet.org/content/vindr-pcxr/1.0.0/
records.headline_result: the first and largest pediatric chest radiograph dataset with both lesion-level bounding boxes and image-level labels, covering 36 findings and 15 diseases

records.title: Fetal brain tissue annotation and segmentation challenge results.
records.model_family: 21 submitted algorithms, all deep learning and mostly U-Nets
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the developing fetal brain into tissues, the step every quantitative prenatal neurodevelopment study depends on
records.patient_population: fetuses in the open FeTA dataset of reconstructed brain MRI segmented into seven tissues
records.model_description: The benchmark this subfield lacked: an open dataset, seven tissue labels, and 20 international teams evaluated on the same terms. The finding is instructive about the state of the art — almost all 21 submissions performed similarly, four of the top five used ensembles, and the differences that mattered were fine-tuning and pre- and post-processing rather than architecture. One asymmetrical U-Net stood apart.
records.release_evidence: the challenge used the FeTA Dataset, an open dataset of fetal brain MRI reconstructions
records.dataset_size: the open FeTA dataset; 21 algorithms from 20 teams
records.headline_result: almost all submissions performed similarly; one asymmetrical U-Net performed significantly better than the rest

records.title: AI aided workflow for hip dysplasia screening using ultrasound in primary care clinics.
records.model_family: FDA-cleared AI app interpreting cine-sweep images from a handheld probe, with real-time decision support
records.clinical_problem: universal newborn screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, which prevents premature osteoarthritis if caught in infancy but is not cost-effective when every scan needs an expert to perform and a radiologist or surgeon to read
records.patient_population: 369 scans in 306 infants, scanned by nurses or family physicians at three primary care clinics after video, slide and brief in-person training
records.model_description: The clearest example in this database of AI changing who can do a study rather than how well it is read. Nurses and family physicians with an afternoon of training, a handheld probe and real-time decision support reached follow-up and case-detection rates comparable to formal screening done by a sonographer and read by a specialist. The learning curve is quantified rather than asserted - follow-up rates fell from 40% to 14% after about 60 cases per site. All six infants referred on had confirmed dysplasia, and four had no risk factors that would have flagged them for selective screening.
records.release_evidence: the FDA-cleared MEDO-Hip AI app used with a commercial handheld ultrasound probe
records.dataset_size: 369 scans in 306 infants across three primary care clinics
records.headline_result: internal follow-up rate fell from 40% (nurses) and 20% (physicians) to 14% after about 60 cases per site; all 6 infants referred to pediatric orthopedics had confirmed dysplasia, 4 of them with no risk factors

records.title: Children's dental panoramic radiographs dataset for caries segmentation and dental disease detection.

records.title: Machine learning in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: new approaches toward understanding the neural mechanisms.
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review of machine learning across behavioral, genetic, MRI, EEG and fNIRS data in ADHD; no model developed or evaluated

records.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Impact on Pediatric Patients, a White Paper From the ACR Pediatric AI Workgroup.
records.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
records.clinical_problem: the near absence of AI tools developed and validated for children, framed as a health equity problem
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice generally
records.model_description: The ACR Pediatric AI Workgroup's position statement. Its argument is that pediatric AI is not adult AI applied to smaller patients: design, training, validation and safe deployment in children all require distinct approaches, and the current shortage of pediatric-specific tools is a health equity issue rather than a market gap. It closes by inviting the community to join the Image Gently-affiliated Image IntelliGently initiative.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in obstetric ultrasound: A scoping review.
records.clinical_problem: the whole span of obstetric ultrasound, from first-trimester scanning to fetal echocardiography and neurosonography
records.patient_population: pregnancies in the 127 reviewed studies
records.model_description: The broadest map of AI in obstetric ultrasound: 127 studies sorted by application, covering first-trimester scanning, placenta, biometry, echocardiography, neurosonography, anatomy assessment, lung maturity and adverse-outcome prediction. Its stated promise is efficiency and improved outcomes in low-resource settings, which is where the strongest evidence in this database also sits.

records.title: Fetal MRI: what's new? A short review.
records.exclusion_reason: short review of new fetal MRI sequences, the 1.5-T to 3-T transition and the emerging role of AI motion-correction software; no model developed or evaluated

records.title: Deep Learning Model to Classify and Monitor Idiopathic Scoliosis in Adolescents Using a Single Smartphone Photograph.
records.model_family: deep learning model deployed inside the AlignProCARE open platform smartphone app
records.clinical_problem: classifying severity and curve type in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and detecting progression, from a single photograph of the unclothed back instead of a radiograph
records.patient_population: adolescent patients attending spine clinics, with radiographs and smartphone photographs; ground truth annotated by two experienced spine specialists from spine radiographs
records.model_description: A radiation-sparing substitute for the screening examination rather than for the diagnostic radiograph. The comparison is the honest one - the app's output and the radiographic ground truth were both put blind against two spine surgeons judging the same unclothed back - so the question asked is whether the model beats the clinical examination it would replace, not whether it beats the X-ray. Progression detection over six-month follow-up is the harder and more clinically valuable half.
records.release_evidence: incorporated into and tested in the AlignProCARE open platform app in 2022
records.dataset_size: not stated in the abstract beyond a prospective training cohort and a clinic test cohort
records.headline_result: the app classified AIS severity and curve type and distinguished six-month progression, benchmarked blind against two spine surgeons assessing unclothed back appearance

records.title: Defocus incorporated multiple segments (DIMS) spectacle lenses increase the choroidal thickness: a two-year randomized clinical trial.
records.exclusion_reason: myopia control trial using optical coherence tomography of the choroid; ophthalmic imaging is outside radiology as scoped here

records.title: Artificial intelligence to identify fractures on pediatric and young adult upper extremity radiographs.
records.model_family: Faster R-CNN object detection compared against EfficientNetV2 image classification
records.clinical_problem: pediatric upper extremity fractures, which respond to injury differently from adult bone and which most fracture AI has ignored
records.patient_population: 58,846 upper extremity radiographs from 14,873 pediatric and young adult patients, with internal and external test splits
records.model_description: The development paper behind the openly shared childfx model, and unusually explicit about sharing it. It compares strong supervision (object detection with boxes) against weak supervision (whole-image classification) and finds the former clearly better. The comparison that matters operationally is against on-call residents on the cases they actually preliminary-read overnight, where the model was more accurate.
records.release_evidence: develop and transparently share an AI model capable of detecting a range of pediatric upper extremity fractures
records.headline_result: AUC 0.96, accuracy 89.7%, sensitivity 90.8%, specificity 88.7%; accuracy on overnight preliminary-read cases 89.4% versus 85.1% for residents (P = 0.01)
records.study_design: retrospective development with external testing and resident comparison

records.exclusion_reason: benchmarking a large language model on a radiation oncology in-training exam; pediatrics is one of many exam knowledge domains and no pediatric imaging task is performed

records.title: Can GPT-4V(ision) Serve Medical Applications? Case Studies on GPT-4V for Multimodal Medical Diagnosis
records.exclusion_reason: case studies of a general multimodal model across 17 body systems and 8 modalities; pediatrics is one system among many and no pediatric task is evaluated separately

records.exclusion_reason: overview of a neuroimaging consortium's first five years in obsessive-compulsive disorder; machine learning is described as ongoing work and no model is presented

records.title: Predicting Depression Onset in Young People Based on Clinical, Cognitive, Environmental, and Neurobiological Data.
records.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
records.model_family: penalized logistic regression over 145 multimodal baseline variables, including structural MRI features
records.clinical_problem: identifying which healthy 14-year-olds will develop major or subthreshold depression, so that risk can be monitored and early intervention offered
records.patient_population: a subsample of the multisite IMAGEN adolescent cohort: 407 for training and 137 from three independent IMAGEN sites held out for validation, grouped by 2-year and 5-year follow-up diagnosis
records.model_description: Imaging is one of four modalities here rather than the whole model, and the honest reading of the result is that it contributes modestly - one structural feature, supramarginal gyrus surface area, survives alongside baseline symptom severity, sex, neuroticism and stressful life events. That is itself worth recording: a well-powered multimodal test of how much brain structure adds over cheap clinical variables. Validation on three independent sites held the AUC, which most prediction studies in this literature cannot show.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.70-0.72 in training and 0.68-0.72 in the independent validation sample

records.title: How does artificial intelligence in radiology improve efficiency and health outcomes?
records.clinical_problem: whether radiology AI actually improves efficiency, dose, accuracy and outcomes
records.patient_population: not specified; the review is written for a pediatric radiology readership
records.model_description: A review, not a model. It names six clinical objectives AI is meant to serve — faster workflow, shorter reading time, less dose and contrast, earlier detection, better accuracy, more personalized diagnostics — and grades the published evidence for each against a hierarchical model of efficacy. Its conclusion is that the market is still maturing and very little is known about what AI contributes in practice, which is the argument for real-world monitoring before procurement.

records.title: Automated Brain Masking of Fetal Functional MRI with Open Data.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network brain masking model, packaged with existing fMRI preprocessing steps
records.clinical_problem: isolating the fetal brain from surrounding maternal tissue across thousands of non-stationary volumes, the step that blocks any resting-state functional MRI study of the brain before birth
records.patient_population: 1241 manually traced fetal fMRI images from 207 fetuses, with two held-out test sets from separate scanners and populations
records.model_description: Fetal resting-state fMRI grew faster than the tooling to process it, and brain masking is where that gap bites - the brain moves unpredictably between volumes, so a single mask never holds. Rather than publishing a network alone, the authors wire it into the surrounding preprocessing steps and explain each adaptation, and release code and data openly. Two held-out test sets from different scanners and populations is a stronger generalization claim than the field usually makes.
records.release_evidence: openly shared code and data, presented as an advance toward a fully comprehensive open-source workflow
records.headline_result: excellent auto-masking performance across two held-out test sets from separate scanners and populations

records.title: Deep learning-based automatic tumor burden assessment of pediatric high-grade gliomas, medulloblastomas, and other leptomeningeal seeding tumors.
records.model_family: 3D U-Net segmentation with automated bidimensional and volumetric measurement
records.clinical_problem: measuring tumor burden reproducibly across serial MRI to judge whether a child's brain tumor is responding
records.patient_population: 794 children with preoperative MRI and 122 with serial postoperative MRI, covering high-grade glioma, medulloblastoma and leptomeningeal seeding tumors
records.model_description: Segments the tumor on contrast-enhanced T1 and T2/FLAIR and then computes the RAPNO response measurement automatically, both as bidimensional product and as volume. The result worth noting is not accuracy but repeatability: it was more consistent than human raters when a child had multiple lesions, which is exactly where manual response assessment becomes unreliable and where treatment decisions turn.
records.headline_result: intraclass correlation with expert volumes 0.90-0.96; agreement of automated with manual RAPNO scores 0.85-0.91; superior repeatability to human raters for multifocal disease
records.study_design: retrospective study with two independent expert raters

records.title: Current and emerging artificial intelligence applications for pediatric musculoskeletal radiology.
records.clinical_problem: where AI stands in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging, beyond bone age
records.patient_population: children in the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A sober review from Pediatric Radiology: bone age has been in clinical use for a decade and is deployed in an assist mode rather than replacing anyone, and almost everything else — appendicular fracture detection, vertebral fracture detection — remains in the research literature. It ends by asking pediatric radiologists to join the research teams rather than wait for products, which is a reasonable reading of why so little pediatric-specific development happens.

records.title: Neuroimaging in Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Recent Advances.
records.exclusion_reason: neuroradiology review of structural and functional imaging findings in ADHD; AI is one paragraph and the review concludes no definitive imaging pattern defines the disorder

records.title: Current and emerging artificial intelligence applications in chest imaging: a pediatric perspective.
records.clinical_problem: whether any of the certified chest AI products can be used in children
records.patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography or CT
records.model_description: A review of the more than 40 certified AI products for chest radiography and chest CT, read from a pediatric standpoint. Its central finding is blunt: none of them is designed for children. The partial exceptions are adult tuberculosis detectors, which are also applicable to children, and software under development for early cystic fibrosis change on chest CT, which the authors flag as the most promising pediatric opening.
records.release_evidence: more than 40 certified AI products are available for chest radiography or chest CT

records.title: The Developmental Brain Age Is Associated With Adversity, Depression, and Functional Outcomes Among Adolescents.
records.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
records.exclusion_reason: brain-age gap against adversity and depression in adolescents; a developmental psychiatry association study rather than a diagnostic or prognostic imaging application

records.title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology: international survey of health care professionals' opinions.
records.exclusion_reason: international survey of 240 health care professionals' attitudes toward AI in pediatric radiology; opinion research rather than a model

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Pediatric Brain Tumor Imaging: A Systematic Review.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of 22 studies of AI in pediatric brain tumor imaging; a survey rather than a model

records.title: The augmented radiologist: artificial intelligence in the practice of radiology.
records.clinical_problem: where AI fits in the pediatric radiologist's working day, and what it cannot do
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
records.model_description: A review in Pediatric Radiology arguing for augmentation rather than replacement. It sets out what AI does better than a person (measuring size, shape, texture and kinetics; handling high-dimensional data) against what it does worse (it is only as good as its training sample and cannot reason toward a near-optimal solution), and proposes explainable AI and an assistant that frees the radiologist's attention for the generic parts of the job.

records.title: Self-supervised IVIM DWI parameter estimation with a physics based forward model.
records.exclusion_reason: self-supervised diffusion parameter estimation in abdominal organs of Crohn disease patients; the abstract does not identify the cohort as pediatric

records.title: Using chest computed tomography and unsupervised machine learning for predicting and evaluating response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in people with cystic fibrosis.
records.model_family: k-means clustering over 120 radiomics features from pre-therapeutic chest CT
records.clinical_problem: identifying, before treatment starts, which people with cystic fibrosis will respond to lumacaftor-ivacaftor, and measuring the structural lung change the drug produces
records.patient_population: 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis from a French multicentre real-world prospective study, with pre-therapeutic and one-year follow-up chest CT
records.model_description: Unsupervised rather than supervised, and that choice carries the argument: the clusters are morphological phenotypes discovered in the pre-treatment CT without reference to who responded, and only afterwards are they checked against response. One of the three clusters contained most of the responders. Alongside this, visual Bhalla scoring quantifies what the drug did to the airways - mucus plugging, wall thickening and consolidation all fell over a year.
records.headline_result: Bhalla score fell 1.40 +/- 1.53 points at one year (p<0.001); 54% of one radiomic cluster achieved a >= 5% FEV1 gain versus 32% and 33% in the others (p=0.02)
records.study_design: prospective multicentre observational study with retrospective radiomic analysis

records.title: External validation of a commercially available deep learning algorithm for fracture detection in children.
records.model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection algorithm
records.clinical_problem: detecting fractures on radiographs of children presenting to the emergency room after trauma
records.patient_population: 2,549 children aged 0-17 (mean 8.5 years) referred from a pediatric emergency room for trauma
records.model_description: This is the study a department should read before buying: an independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on a consecutive real-life pediatric emergency cohort, scored three ways (is there a fracture, how many, and are they in the right place) with subgroup analysis by age and by whether the limb was in a cast. Performance was materially worse in children under 5 and in casted limbs, which are exactly the pediatric cases that matter.
records.release_evidence: external validation of the commercially available Rayvolve algorithm
records.headline_result: sensitivity 95.7%, specificity 91.2%, accuracy 92.6% for detection; sensitivity and negative predictive value significantly lower in children aged 0-4 and in casted limbs

records.title: Detecting the presence of supernumerary teeth during the early mixed dentition stage using deep learning algorithms: A pilot study.
records.exclusion_reason: detection of supernumerary teeth on dental panoramic radiographs; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: The COVID-19 epidemic analysis and diagnosis using deep learning: A systematic literature review and future directions.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic literature review of deep learning for COVID-19 analysis and diagnosis; a survey rather than a model, and not pediatric

records.title: Use of real-time artificial intelligence in detection of abnormal image patterns in standard sonographic reference planes in screening for fetal intracranial malformations.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: real-time YOLOv3 object detection
records.clinical_problem: screening for congenital central nervous system malformation on standard neurosonographic planes
records.patient_population: 16,297 pregnancies at 18-40 weeks from two tertiary Chinese hospitals for development, a third hospital for external validation, and 166 pregnancies for prospective video testing
records.model_description: Detects ten distinct intracranial abnormality patterns during the scan itself, not afterwards, using a real-time detection architecture. The evaluation ladder is unusually complete: internal validation, external validation at a third hospital, comparison against sonologists of differing experience, and then a prospective video dataset simulating live scanning. Performance drops from internal to external, as it should, and stays useful.
records.dataset_size: 43,890 images from 16,297 pregnancies and 169 videos from 166 pregnancies
records.headline_result: micro-average AUC 0.977 internally and 0.898 on external validation across ten intracranial patterns, with prospective real-time video evaluation
records.study_design: retrospective development with external and prospective validation

records.title: Brain age prediction using fMRI network coupling in youths and associations with psychiatric symptoms.
records.exclusion_reason: brain-age prediction from functional connectivity in youth against psychiatric symptom burden; the association did not replicate in the second sample and the target is not a diagnostic imaging task

records.title: An artificial intelligence powered platform for auto-analyses of spine alignment irrespective of image quality with prospective validation.
records.model_family: hybrid model combining an HRNet landmark detector with rule-based post-processing
records.clinical_problem: automatic measurement of spine alignment in scoliosis, where existing auto-analysis is unreliable and where the image a clinician has is often a phone photo or a screenshot rather than the original radiograph
records.patient_population: 1542 consecutive patients with scoliosis at two Hong Kong clinics from December 2019 to November 2020 for development, then prospective validation in a further 337 patients; biplanar EOS radiographs recaptured with smartphones or screenshots
records.model_description: Two things set it apart. First, it is deliberately trained on degraded images - smartphone photographs and screenshots of radiographs - because that is what gets sent between clinics, and robustness to that is the difference between a research tool and a usable one. Second, rules are layered on the network's landmarks so the output can be explained and checked, rather than emerging from an opaque regression. Prospectively validated on 337 further patients, which is rare in this literature.
records.dataset_size: 1542 development patients plus 337 prospective validation patients
records.headline_result: mean landmark error 2.78 pixels posteroanterior and 5.52 lateral; mean angle error 3.18 degrees coronal and 6.32 degrees sagittal; curve detection sensitivity 95.7% and specificity 88.1%; all predicted alignments strongly correlated with ground truth (R2 > 0.97)

records.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Pediatric Skull Fractures on Plain Radiographs.
records.model_family: deep learning detection model for plain radiographs
records.clinical_problem: detecting skull fractures on plain radiographs in children with head trauma, the film that is often taken first and read by whoever is on shift
records.patient_population: children with head trauma who had both skull radiography and cranial CT: development sets of 149 and 264 from two hospitals, external test set of 95 from a third; cranial CT was the reference standard
records.model_description: One of the cleaner pediatric AI evaluations in the literature: multi-center development, a genuinely external test hospital, CT as the reference standard, and a two-session reader study with the crossed design that shows who the tool is for. The answer is the one that keeps recurring in pediatric AI - it significantly helped radiology residents and emergency physicians and did nothing measurable for the pediatric radiologist. That is an argument about staffing and coverage, not about accuracy.
records.dataset_size: 413 development cases from two hospitals, 95 external test cases from a third
records.headline_result: AUROC 0.922 internal and 0.870 external; with AI assistance AUROC rose by 0.094 for radiology residents (p = 0.012) and 0.069 for emergency physicians (p = 0.043), but by only 0.008 for the pediatric radiologist (p = 0.850)
records.study_design: retrospective multi-center model development with a crossed reader study

records.title: Deep learning fetal ultrasound video model match human observers in biometric measurements.
records.model_family: multi-task convolutional network doing spatio-temporal feature extraction and standard plane detection on ultrasound video
records.clinical_problem: fetal biometry - head circumference, biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, femur length - and the gestational age and weight estimates derived from it, in settings short of sonographers who can interpret fetal ultrasound
records.patient_population: 50 freehand fetal ultrasound video scans, compared against five experienced sonographers measuring at two time points at least two weeks apart
records.model_description: Works from video rather than from a frozen frame, so the model chooses the measuring plane as well as the caliper positions - the part of biometry that actually takes skill. The evaluation is the strongest form available short of a trial: five sonographers measured twice, weeks apart, establishing both intra- and inter-observer variability, and the model's disagreement with each expert fell inside that band. Six minutes of expert time becomes a few seconds.
records.headline_result: automated measurements comparable to five experienced sonographers, with differences within inter- and intra-observer variability and not statistically significant against any individual expert; seconds versus an average of six minutes
records.study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader repeatability study

records.title: Intelligent Segmentation Medical Assistance System for MRI Images of Osteosarcoma in Developing Countries.
records.journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
records.model_family: depthwise-separable U-shaped network with a conditional random field boundary refinement and Mean Teacher noisy-data training
records.clinical_problem: segmenting osteosarcoma on MRI and computing tumor area in settings where radiologist time is the binding constraint and outcomes are worst
records.patient_population: more than 80 000 osteosarcoma MRI images from three hospitals in China; osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor of children and adolescents
records.model_description: Explicitly engineered for a low-resource deployment rather than for a leaderboard: separable convolutions keep the model cheap to run, a Mean Teacher stage lets noisy studies be used rather than discarded, and a conditional random field cleans up boundaries that a light network gets wrong. The stated objective is a balance of speed, accuracy and cost, which is an unusual and honest framing for a segmentation paper.
records.dataset_size: more than 80 000 MRI images from three hospitals
records.headline_result: improved segmentation accuracy while holding the balance of speed and cost, tested across three hospitals

records.title: No sonographer, no radiologist: New system for automatic prenatal detection of fetal biometry, fetal presentation, and placental location.
records.model_family: U-Net segmentation of the fetal head and placenta applied to volume sweep imaging acquisitions
records.clinical_problem: obtaining fetal biometry, presentation and placental position where there is neither a sonographer to scan nor a radiologist to interpret
records.patient_population: obstetric volume sweep imaging examinations performed in Peru by an operator with no previous ultrasound experience after eight hours of training
records.model_description: The title states the design goal exactly. Both halves of the expertise requirement are removed at once: a standardized sweep protocol keyed to external body landmarks replaces the sonographer's judgment about where to put the probe, and a U-Net replaces the interpreting provider. Eight hours of operator training is the whole input. Placental location is the weak point - substantial rather than near-perfect agreement - which is the finding a deployment plan would have to build around.
records.headline_result: 100% agreement for fetal presentation (kappa 1, p<0.0001) and 76.7% for placental location (kappa 0.59); relative error 5.6% for biparietal diameter and 7.9% for head circumference; gestational age within 2 weeks of standard of care in up to 89%
records.study_design: prospective diagnostic study in an under-resourced setting

records.title: White matter microstructure in children and adolescents with ADHD.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of diffusion MRI findings in childhood ADHD; describes imaging differences but no machine-learning model

records.title: Correlation of histopathology and multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging in childhood osteosarcoma: Predicting tumor response to chemotherapy.
records.model_family: multi-feature fuzzy clustering with weighted majority ruling over conventional, diffusion-weighted and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI features
records.clinical_problem: predicting tumor necrosis - and thus response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy - in childhood osteosarcoma, a cancer whose systemic treatment has been essentially unchanged for 30 years for want of a biomarker
records.patient_population: 15 patients with newly diagnosed high-grade appendicular osteosarcoma enrolled in a single-center observational study, of whom 13 contributed usable data
records.model_description: The methodological core is the co-registration of histologic sections with the MR images, so that MRI features are learned against necrosis measured at the same physical location rather than against a whole-tumor percentage. Necrosis on the resection specimen is the current response measure and it arrives only after surgery; an imaging surrogate would arrive during treatment. Fifteen patients, so this is a proof of principle for a testable biomarker rather than a biomarker.
records.headline_result: MRI-estimated necrosis compared against pathologist estimates and deep-learning quantification of digitized histologic sections, through direct histologic-MR co-registration

records.title: Radiation Dose Reduction for 80-kVp Pediatric CT Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction: A Clinical and Phantom Study.
records.model_family: deep learning-based CT reconstruction
records.clinical_problem: how far pediatric CT dose can be cut at low tube voltage before diagnostic quality fails
records.patient_population: 65 children aged 6 years or younger (mean 25 months) undergoing contrast-enhanced 80-kVp CT, plus a phantom study
records.model_description: Compares deep-learning reconstruction against hybrid and model-based iterative reconstruction on low-tube-voltage pediatric CT, at roughly half the dose. Two radiologists scored noise, texture, streak, sharpness and overall quality, and a phantom study measured task-based detectability across six dose levels. The finding that matters: lower-dose deep-learning images scored higher than standard-dose hybrid iterative images, while lower-dose model-based iterative images scored worse.
records.dataset_size: 65 children (31 standard dose, 34 lower dose) plus phantom imaging at six dose levels
records.headline_result: size-specific dose estimate 54% lower in the reduced-dose group; lower-dose deep-learning reconstruction scored higher than standard-dose hybrid iterative reconstruction on texture, sharpness and overall quality (p < .001)
records.study_design: retrospective clinical and phantom study with reader assessment

records.title: Autonomous artificial intelligence in pediatric radiology: the use and perception of BoneXpert for bone age assessment.
records.model_family: autonomous commercial bone age system
records.clinical_problem: what actually happens when an AI tool designed to replace the radiologist is installed in a department
records.patient_population: 97 radiologists across 18 European countries already using the software, from 282 surveyed
records.model_description: The most useful deployment study in this database, and it contains no images. BoneXpert was built as an AI-replace tool; asked how they actually use it, only 18% of radiologists let it replace them, 60% still review the radiograph themselves to exclude underlying disease, and 40% have never overruled it. Reporting time fell sharply. The authors' conclusion is the general lesson: bone age rating is not the whole of reading a bone age radiograph, so a tool validated for one task cannot autonomously own the examination.
records.release_evidence: the autonomous AI system for bone age rating (BoneXpert), in clinical use in European departments
records.headline_result: radiologists taking over 2 minutes per rating fell from 86% to 21% after installation; only 18% used it to replace the radiologist, 60% still checked the radiograph themselves, and 40% never overruled it

records.title: Imaging fetal anatomy.
records.exclusion_reason: review of past, present and future techniques for imaging the developing embryo and fetus, from in utero ultrasound to micro-CT and ultra-high-field MRI; AI appears only in the future perspective

records.title: Contributions of Artificial Intelligence Reported in Obstetrics and Gynecology Journals: Systematic Review.
records.exclusion_reason: bibliometric systematic review of AI publications across obstetrics and gynecology as a discipline, including assisted reproduction and omics; not specific to fetal or pediatric imaging

records.title: Naming-related spectral responses predict neuropsychological outcome after epilepsy surgery.
records.exclusion_reason: prediction of post-surgical language decline from intracranially recorded naming-related spectral responses; the model input is intracranial EEG, not imaging

records.title: Medical Professional Enhancement Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Screening.
records.model_family: deep neural network with a visualized internal representation used as an explainable overlay
records.clinical_problem: screening for congenital heart disease on fetal cardiac ultrasound, where detection rates are low because the technique is hard to master
records.patient_population: fetal cardiac ultrasound screening read by experts, fellows and residents
records.model_description: The measured outcome is the examiner's performance, not the model's - which is the right endpoint for a screening aid and a rare one to see reported. The gain scales inversely with experience: residents improved most, fellows next, experts least, exactly the gradient you would want from a tool meant to spread a hard skill. The explainability is not a post-hoc heatmap but a purpose-built representation of the network's internals, offered as the thing that earns clinician trust.
records.headline_result: mean AUC rose from 0.966 to 0.975 for experts, 0.829 to 0.890 for fellows and 0.616 to 0.748 for residents

records.title: Subcortical segmentation of the fetal brain in 3D ultrasound using deep learning.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network trained few-shot, compared against training on many weakly labelled atlas-derived segmentations
records.clinical_problem: quantifying subcortical brain volume development from 3D fetal ultrasound, which manual segmentation makes impractical because of low soft tissue contrast, speckle and shadowing
records.patient_population: 9 manually annotated volumes for training; the trained models were then applied to 278 ultrasound volumes from a diverse healthy population
records.model_description: Two contributions worth separating. Methodologically, it settles a practical question - nine careful manual annotations beat many weak atlas-derived labels, reaching close to intra-observer variability - which changes how a group with limited annotation time should spend it. Substantively, applying the result to 278 healthy volumes produced ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for choroid plexus, ventricle horns, cavum septum pellucidum and cerebellum, which is a normative reference that did not previously exist for this modality.
records.dataset_size: 9 manually annotated training volumes; 278 volumes for the growth curves
records.headline_result: segmentation performance close to intra-observer variability from only nine manual annotations, and novel ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for four subcortical structures
records.study_design: retrospective model development and normative study

records.title: A Comprehensive Survey on the Detection, Classification, and Challenges of Neurological Disorders.
records.exclusion_reason: survey of AI for neurological disorders across imaging, signal and speech modalities and all ages; not specific to pediatric imaging

records.title: High-Grade Glioma Treatment Response Monitoring Biomarkers: A Position Statement on the Evidence Supporting the Use of Advanced MRI Techniques in the Clinic, and the Latest Bench-to-Bedside Developments. Part 1: Perfusion and Diffusion Techniques.
records.exclusion_reason: position statement on advanced MRI monitoring biomarkers in adult high-grade glioma; children are mentioned only as a group for whom arterial spin labeling avoids gadolinium

records.title: MRI Radiogenomics of Pediatric Medulloblastoma: A Multicenter Study.
records.model_family: two-stage sequential radiomics classifier selected from six candidate models
records.clinical_problem: identifying the molecular subgroup of a medulloblastoma from the preoperative MRI, which determines risk group and therapy
records.patient_population: 263 children with newly diagnosed medulloblastoma at 12 international pediatric sites, mean age 87 months
records.model_description: Extracts 1,800 texture and intensity features from preoperative T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 MRI and assigns the tumor to one of the four clinically actionable molecular subgroups, in two stages: first separating non-WNT/non-SHH tumors, then splitting WNT from SHH. A separate classifier distinguishes high-risk group 3 from group 4. If it held up prospectively it would let subgroup-directed decisions be made before surgery, and narrow who needs targeted genetic testing.
records.headline_result: microaveraged F1 88% across subgroups, 95% for WNT specifically, and AUC 98% for group 3 versus group 4

records.title: Pediatric chest radiograph interpretation: how far has artificial intelligence come? A systematic literature review.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of 55 studies of AI for pediatric chest radiograph interpretation and an inventory of 29 public chest radiograph datasets; a survey rather than a model

records.title: Using deep transfer learning to detect scoliosis and spondylolisthesis from x-ray images.
records.exclusion_reason: deep transfer learning classification of scoliosis and spondylolisthesis on spine radiographs from 338 subjects; children are mentioned as an affected group but the abstract does not state the ages of the subjects, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: Automated detection of acute appendicular skeletal fractures in pediatric patients using deep learning.
records.model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection algorithm
records.clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in children
records.patient_population: 300 radiographic examinations from patients aged 2-21 (167 boys, 133 girls, mean age 10.8 years), balanced across five body parts
records.model_description: An independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on pediatric extremity radiographs, deliberately balanced across five anatomical regions with 60 examinations each. Performance held up across body parts and fracture types with one clear exception, avulsion fractures, where sensitivity fell to 73% with a wide confidence interval. Avulsions are a characteristically pediatric injury, which makes that the finding to carry into a procurement discussion.
records.release_evidence: external validation of an existing commercial AI software program (BoneView)
records.headline_result: sensitivity per patient 91.3%, specificity 90.0%, AUC 0.93; sensitivity for avulsion fractures only 72.7%

records.title: Accounting for motion in resting-state fMRI: What part of the spectrum are we characterizing in autism spectrum disorder?
records.exclusion_reason: methodological paper on selection bias from motion-based exclusion in resting-state fMRI, using machine learning within a targeted minimum loss estimator to correct it; the model is a statistical bias correction, not an imaging model

records.title: An overview of artificial intelligence techniques for diagnosis of Schizophrenia based on magnetic resonance imaging modalities: Methods, challenges, and future works.
records.exclusion_reason: review of AI for schizophrenia diagnosis on MRI; the population is late-adolescent to adult and no pediatric imaging task is addressed

records.title: A pediatric wrist trauma X-ray dataset (GRAZPEDWRI-DX) for machine learning.
records.clinical_problem: the absence of an annotated public pediatric fracture dataset, which is what keeps most fracture AI adult-trained
records.patient_population: 6,091 children treated for wrist trauma at one pediatric surgery department between 2008 and 2018
records.model_description: A public dataset rather than a model, and arguably worth more than another classifier: 20,327 de-identified pediatric wrist radiographs across 10,643 studies, annotated by pediatric radiologists with lines, boxes and polygons marking fractures and periosteal reactions, plus age and sex. Given that children are under 1% of public medical imaging data, a dataset of this size in the commonest pediatric fracture is a substantive contribution.
records.release_evidence: this dataset is publicly available to encourage computer vision research
records.dataset_size: 20,327 images from 10,643 studies of 6,091 patients, with 74,459 tags and 67,771 labeled objects

records.title: Automated 3D reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space from motion-corrupted MRI stacks for 21-36 weeks GA range.
records.model_family: 3D CNN localisation and landmark-guided pose estimation feeding automated deformable slice-to-volume registration
records.clinical_problem: reconstructing a high-resolution 3D fetal trunk volume from motion-corrupted T2-weighted stacks, which is what makes detailed assessment of body anomalies including congenital heart defects possible
records.patient_population: T2-weighted fetal MRI datasets across the 21-36 week gestational age range
records.model_description: Extends to the trunk what had only been solved for the fetal brain. Two specific failures are targeted: existing trunk pipelines need manual input, and gradient-descent registration has too narrow a capture range for the severe motion typical at early gestational age. A 3D localisation network plus landmark-based pose estimation replaces both, and an outlier-rejection step throws out stacks ruined by motion or poor quality without a human deciding. The result lands in standard radiological space regardless of how the fetus is lying.
records.headline_result: fully automated deformable slice-to-volume reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space across 21-36 weeks, independent of fetal trunk position or stack coverage

records.title: Artificial intelligence for radiological paediatric fracture assessment: a systematic review.
records.clinical_problem: how well AI actually detects fractures in children, given that development has concentrated on adults
records.patient_population: children in the nine eligible studies, most on radiographs and most of the elbow
records.model_description: A systematic review with a pointed premise: missed fractures carry greater long-term clinical and medicolegal consequence in children than in adults, yet almost all research and commercial effort has been on adults. Only nine studies qualified. Nearly all used single-institution data and only two performed external validation, so the reported accuracies of 89 to 98 percent cannot be assumed to generalize. Its recommendation is multicentre real-world evaluation.
records.headline_result: reported AI accuracies 88.8-97.9%; only 2 of 9 studies performed external validation, and AI sensitivity exceeded human readers non-significantly in 2 of 3 comparative studies

records.title: Development and validation of machine learning models for prediction of seizure outcome after pediatric epilepsy surgery.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning prediction of seizure freedom one year after pediatric epilepsy surgery; the five selected features are clinical and investigational (number of antiseizure medications, presence of an MRI lesion, age at onset, video-EEG concordance, surgery type) rather than image-derived, so this is a clinical prediction model

records.title: Artificial intelligence and imaging: Opportunities in cardio-oncology.
records.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
records.exclusion_reason: review of AI applied to cardiovascular imaging in cardio-oncology; survivors of childhood cancer are one mentioned group and no pediatric model is evaluated

records.title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence approved for adults for the interpretation of pediatric chest radiographs.
records.model_family: commercial adult-developed lesion detection software
records.clinical_problem: whether chest AI built and approved for adults can be pointed at children's radiographs
records.patient_population: 2,273 chest radiographs from patients 18 or younger
records.model_description: Takes software developed on adults and runs it on 2,273 pediatric chest radiographs against a pediatric radiologist reference. Overall sensitivity was only 67%, and age was a significant predictor of error. Excluding cardiomegaly and children under two lifted accuracy from 87.5% to 96.9%, which locates the failure precisely: the youngest children and the finding most dependent on age-specific normal anatomy. The conclusion, that these tools need validation in younger children, is the practical one.
records.release_evidence: an AI-based lesion detection software developed for adult chest radiographs
records.headline_result: sensitivity 67.2%, specificity 91.1%, accuracy 87.5% overall; accuracy rose to 96.9% and sensitivity to 86.4% after excluding cardiomegaly and children 2 years or younger (all p < 0.001)

records.title: SynthStrip: skull-stripping for any brain image.
records.model_family: CNN trained on synthetically generated images
records.clinical_problem: removing non-brain signal (skull-stripping) as a first step in any brain MRI analysis
records.patient_population: subjects from newborn to adult, across a range of acquisitions including clinically common thick-slice fast spin-echo
records.model_description: Takes any brain MRI, of any contrast or resolution, and returns a brain mask. It is trained entirely on synthetic images whose anatomy, intensities and artifacts are deliberately pushed beyond the realistic range, so that a single model generalizes to acquisitions it never saw, including neonatal and clinical thick-slice scans that defeat conventional tools.
records.release_evidence: our method and labeled evaluation data are available at https://w3id.org/synthstrip
records.headline_result: substantial accuracy improvement over popular skull-stripping baselines with a single trained model

records.title: Deep Learning to Predict Neonatal and Infant Brain Age from Myelination on Brain MRI Scans.
records.model_family: three-dimensional regression convolutional neural network with layer-wise relevance propagation attention maps
records.clinical_problem: judging whether an infant's myelination is appropriate for age, which today means a radiologist visually inspecting T1 and T2 images against remembered milestones and comparing to gestationally corrected age
records.patient_population: 518 neonates and infants aged 0-25 months with reported normal myelination scanned at one academic center between January 1995 and June 2019 (mean gestationally corrected age 67 weeks +/- 33), with an external test set from the National Institutes of Health
records.model_description: Automates an assessment that is already part of every pediatric brain MRI report, rather than inventing a new biomarker - the output is the age the brain looks like, which is exactly what the radiologist is estimating by eye. The attention maps are the convincing part: the network attended to cerebellum, posterior white matter and basal ganglia in the youngest infants and to anterior white matter in the oldest, which is the known caudal-to-rostral, posterior-to-anterior order of myelination. Combining T1 and T2 beat either alone, and it held up on an external NIH set.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 9.8 +/- 2.3 weeks (T1), 9.1 +/- 1.9 (T2) and 7.7 +/- 1.7 (both) internally; 9.1 weeks on the external NIH test set
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Radiation Dose Optimization in Pediatric Radiology: A Systematic Review.
records.body_region: abdomen, chest, head, neck and pelvis
records.clinical_problem: how much radiation dose AI can actually save in children, and where
records.patient_population: children in the 16 reviewed studies
records.model_description: A systematic review answering a single procurement-shaped question: which AI techniques have been used for pediatric dose optimization, where, and how well. Almost all of it is deep-learning CT reconstruction, and the reported dose reductions are large. It notes that commercially available models dominate but locally built ones matched them, and that the evidence base is narrow: three modalities, small samples, and most examination types untouched.
records.release_evidence: commercially available AI models based on deep convolutional networks dominate the reviewed studies
records.headline_result: most studies reported 36-70% radiation dose reduction without loss of diagnostic information

records.title: Tracking of menstrual cycles and prediction of the fertile window via measurements of basal body temperature and heart rate as well as machine-learning algorithms.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning predicts the fertile window and menses from wearable basal body temperature and heart rate in adult women; not imaging and not a pediatric population

records.title: Proposing a CNN Method for Primary and Permanent Tooth Detection and Enumeration on Pediatric Dental Radiographs.
records.journal: The Journal of clinical pediatric dentistry
records.exclusion_reason: tooth detection and numbering on dental panoramic radiographs; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Wearable Seismocardiography-Based Assessment of Stroke Volume in Congenital Heart Disease.
records.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
records.exclusion_reason: ridge regression estimates stroke volume from wearable ECG and seismocardiogram signals in 45 patients with congenital heart disease; cardiac MRI is the reference standard rather than the model input, so the model is not an imaging model

records.title: An artificial intelligence model correlated with morphological and genetic features of blastocyst quality improves ranking of viable embryos.
records.exclusion_reason: AI ranking of blastocyst images for embryo selection in IVF; laboratory microscopy rather than diagnostic radiology

records.title: A machine-learning algorithm for diagnosis of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children and Kawasaki disease in the USA: a retrospective model development and validation study.
records.exclusion_reason: diagnosis of multisystem inflammatory syndrome versus Kawasaki disease from age, clinical signs and laboratory measurements; no imaging is used
records.study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

records.title: Assessment of an artificial intelligence aid for the detection of appendicular skeletal fractures in children and young adults by senior and junior radiologists.
records.model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection aid
records.clinical_problem: missed fractures on pediatric emergency radiographs, particularly by trainees
records.patient_population: 300 radiographs from patients aged 2 to 21, half with at least one fracture, read by three senior pediatric radiologists and five residents
records.model_description: A multi-reader study of what an AI aid does to human performance rather than of the model alone. Eight readers read 300 radiographs unaided and then again with the AI. Sensitivity rose by about 10 points overall with no meaningful loss of specificity, and the gain was largest for residents, which is the group covering nights and weekends in a pediatric emergency department.
records.release_evidence: described as an artificial intelligence aid evaluated as a reading adjunct
records.headline_result: mean reader sensitivity rose from 73.3% to 82.8% (P < 0.001) with specificity essentially unchanged; stand-alone AI sensitivity 91% and specificity 90%

records.title: Prediction of Histologic Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma Using Pretherapeutic MRI Radiomics.
records.model_family: sixteen radiomics models combining two feature selection methods (ReliefF and t test), ComBat harmonization, and two classifiers (artificial neural network and support vector machine)
records.clinical_problem: predicting histologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in osteosarcoma before treatment starts, when the current prognostic measure - percent necrosis - is only available after surgery and imaging has no predictive value
records.patient_population: 176 patients treated between January 2007 and December 2018 at three centers in France, median age 20 years (range 5-71), 107 male
records.model_description: The clinical gap is stated precisely: histologic response is among the strongest survival predictors in osteosarcoma but arrives after the surgery it might have informed. Sixteen model configurations are built and compared rather than one being reported, and ComBat harmonization is tested explicitly - a necessary step for a three-centre retrospective radiomics study where scanner differences would otherwise be learned as signal. Training and validation performance are close, which is reassuring for a radiomics model of this size.
records.headline_result: best model AUC 0.95 with 91% sensitivity and 92% specificity in training, and 0.97 / 91% / 92% in validation

records.title: Traumatic brain injury: progress and challenges in prevention, clinical care, and research.
records.exclusion_reason: Lancet Neurology Commission on traumatic brain injury care and research generally; not a study of AI applied to pediatric imaging

records.title: An analysis-ready and quality controlled resource for pediatric brain white-matter research.
records.model_family: neural network trained on expert plus community-scientist quality ratings
records.clinical_problem: quality control of diffusion MRI at a scale where no expert can look at every scan, which otherwise limits every downstream analysis of pediatric white matter
records.patient_population: 2747 diffusion MRI datasets from children and adolescents in the Healthy Brain Network study
records.model_description: Two deliverables in one paper, and the second is the interesting one. The first is a curated, preprocessed, analysis-ready pediatric diffusion MRI resource in BIDS format, openly released. The second is a way of scaling quality control: a small expert-scored subset plus a much larger set scored by community scientists trains a network that agrees with experts on held-out data, and an interpretability check confirms it keys on features that actually bear on quality. That paradigm - crowdsource the bulk, anchor with experts, learn the rest - transfers to any large pediatric imaging cohort.
records.release_evidence: preprocessed, analysis-ready data made openly available from the openly-available Healthy Brain Network study
records.headline_result: quality control highly concordant with experts on a held-out set, ROC-AUC 0.947

records.title: A mobile-optimized artificial intelligence system for gestational age and fetal malpresentation assessment.
records.model_family: mobile-optimized deep learning models over blind-sweep ultrasound, running on-device
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age and detecting fetal malpresentation where there is no trained sonographer, which is where most of the world's antenatal ultrasound gap sits
records.patient_population: blind sweep ultrasounds collected by sonographers in the USA and Zambia and by novice operators in Zambia; 406 for gestational age and 613 for malpresentation
records.model_description: Designed backwards from the deployment constraint rather than from the dataset. Six freehand sweeps replace the standard examination, so the operator needs no plane-finding skill; the model runs on an Android phone in under three seconds with no internet; and the accuracy claim is a formal non-inferiority test against standard biometry rather than a correlation. The most consequential result is that non-inferiority held when novices performed only two of the six sweep types, which is a statement about how little training the pathway actually requires.
records.dataset_size: 406 gestational age cases and 613 malpresentation cases
records.headline_result: gestational age non-inferior to standard biometry (error difference -1.4 +/- 4.5 days, 95% CI -1.8 to -0.9); malpresentation AUC-ROC 0.977 (95% CI 0.949-1.00); under 3 s on-device

records.title: Automatic autism spectrum disorder detection using artificial intelligence methods with MRI neuroimaging: A review.
records.clinical_problem: automated detection of autism spectrum disorder from structural and functional MRI
records.patient_population: children with autism across the reviewed computer-aided diagnosis literature
records.model_description: A review of computer-aided diagnosis systems for autism built on structural and functional MRI, covering both conventional machine learning and the smaller deep learning literature, with a comparison of the two and a catalogue of the obstacles each faces. Useful as an entry point to a literature that is large, heterogeneous and rarely externally validated.

records.title: Deep Learning for Improving the Effectiveness of Routine Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Diseases.
records.model_family: DenseNet201, selected after comparing four convolutional architectures
records.clinical_problem: detecting major congenital heart disease at routine prenatal ultrasound screening, where detection rates are held down by the scarcity of fetal cardiologists and the volume of scans
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images covering seven congenital heart defects - ventricular and atrial septal defect, atrioventricular septal defect, Ebstein anomaly, tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries and hypoplastic left heart syndrome - plus normal controls
records.model_description: Seven named lesions rather than a normal-versus-abnormal split, which is what a screening tool would have to distinguish to be more than a flag. Reporting the intra-patient and inter-patient splits separately is the paper's most useful discipline: the perfect intra-patient numbers are an artefact of frames from the same fetus appearing on both sides, and the inter-patient figures are the ones to read. Validated against three expert fetal cardiologists.
records.headline_result: inter-patient sensitivity 99%, specificity 97% and accuracy 98% (intra-patient 100% across the board)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with expert comparison

records.title: Machine-learning-based prediction of pre-eclampsia using first-trimester maternal characteristics and biomarkers.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.exclusion_reason: first-trimester pre-eclampsia screening from maternal characteristics, history and serum biomarkers with one Doppler index; a maternal outcome rather than a fetal imaging task

records.title: In utero exposure to cannabidiol disrupts select early-life behaviors in a sex-specific manner.
records.exclusion_reason: mouse study of in utero cannabidiol exposure using deep learning to analyze pup ultrasonic vocalizations and homing behavior; not imaging and not human

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiology: A Scoping Review.
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis, risk stratification and management of congenital heart disease in children
records.patient_population: children with congenital heart disease across the 2002-2022 literature
records.model_description: A scoping review across cardiac MRI, echocardiography, CT and electrocardiography in children, extending to postoperative outcome prediction and prenatal prediction from maternal risk factors. It is candid about why adoption lags: few appropriate algorithms, limited physician training, fear of over-mechanization, and the worry about losing the human element.

records.title: AI Estimation of Gestational Age from Blind Ultrasound Sweeps in Low-Resource Settings.
records.model_family: neural network on ultrasound cineloop sweeps
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where there is no sonographer and no high-end ultrasound machine
records.patient_population: 4,695 pregnant volunteers in North Carolina and Zambia, with separate test sets of IVF pregnancies and of sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices
records.model_description: Estimates gestational age from blind sweeps of the pregnant abdomen: the operator simply passes the probe along predefined lines without needing to find any standard plane. The model was more accurate than a trained sonographer's standard biometry, and the accuracy held when the sweeps were collected by untrained providers in Zambia using battery-powered devices. This is one of the clearest demonstrations in the corpus that AI can move an imaging capability to where the expertise is not.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.9 days for the model versus 4.7 days for standard biometry (P < 0.001); 4.9 versus 5.4 days for sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices

records.title: Toward a realistic model of speech processing in the brain with self-supervised learning
records.exclusion_reason: comparison of self-supervised speech models against adult fMRI responses; a computational neuroscience study rather than a pediatric imaging application

records.title: FDA approved Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Enabled Medical Devices: An updated landscape
records.clinical_problem: what has actually been cleared for use, through which pathway, and for whom
records.patient_population: the population covered by FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled medical devices, with pediatric representation as one axis of analysis
records.model_description: An analysis of every FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled device by clearance pathway, timeline, specialty, decision type and recall history.
