Radiology dominates, approvals surged from 2018, and most went through 510(k) on substantial equivalence, which means no new clinical trial. Two gaps are named that bear directly on children: pediatric-focused devices and trials are underrepresented, and trials are geographically concentrated in the United States.
records.release_evidence: analysis of FDA-cleared commercial medical devices
records.dataset_size: the full FDA AI/ML-enabled device list
records.headline_result: a significant surge in approvals since 2018 with clear radiology dominance, reliance on the 510(k) pathway, and underrepresentation of pediatric-focused devices and trials

records.title: Precision medicine for long-term depression outcomes using the Personalized Advantage Index approach: cognitive therapy or interpersonal psychotherapy?
records.exclusion_reason: treatment-selection modelling for adult depression from pre-treatment clinical variables; no imaging
records.study_design: secondary analysis of a randomized trial

records.title: Differentiation Between Ependymoma and Medulloblastoma in Children with Radiomics Approach.
records.model_family: radiomics with three feature selection methods and four classifiers compared
records.clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from medulloblastoma in a child, when the two look alike in age, location and symptoms
records.patient_population: 51 children (24 ependymoma, 27 medulloblastoma)
records.model_description: Extracts radiomic features from contrast-enhanced T1 and apparent diffusion coefficient maps of semi-automatically segmented tumors and classifies which of the two common posterior fossa tumors it is. Twelve combinations of feature selection and classifier were compared, which is the honest way to do this on 51 patients; the authors note explicitly that no single combination is best for every dataset.
records.headline_result: best model (logistic feature selection with random forest) reached AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.787-0.968)

records.title: Multi-Res-Attention UNet: A CNN Model for the Segmentation of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Lesions from Magnetic Resonance Images.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.exclusion_reason: focal cortical dysplasia segmentation network evaluated on 3-T FLAIR MRI; focal cortical dysplasia is described as affecting adults and children but the abstract does not state the ages of the cohort, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record
records.model_family: hybrid skip-connection fully convolutional network

records.title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology: Future opportunities.
records.clinical_problem: which parts of the pediatric imaging pathway AI could plausibly improve
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
records.model_description: Walks the pediatric patient pathway and asks, at each step, where AI has been shown feasible and where it has not, borrowing from the adult literature to propose targets. Its opening observation is the important one for this database: cancer screening AI has had enormous attention while children's imaging has been neglected, which is a statement about where development effort has gone rather than where the clinical need is.

records.title: Large-Scale Functional Brain Network Architecture Changes Associated With Trauma-Related Dissociation.
records.exclusion_reason: functional MRI in 65 adult women with post-traumatic stress disorder; childhood abuse is the exposure history, not the age at imaging

records.title: Noise reduction approach in pediatric abdominal CT combining deep learning and dual-energy technique.
records.model_family: deep learning noise reduction applied to virtual monoenergetic dual-energy reconstructions
records.clinical_problem: reducing both radiation dose and iodinated contrast load in children undergoing abdominal CT
records.patient_population: 29 pediatric patients aged 2-19 years, each with a prior standard single-energy CT for comparison
records.model_description: Combines two dose-sparing ideas that are usually studied separately: dual-energy acquisition with reduced iodine concentration, and deep-learning denoising of the resulting low-energy virtual monoenergetic images. Each alone increases noise; together they held image quality while cutting radiation by about 20% and iodine by 14%. Contrast load matters independently of dose in children with repeated imaging or impaired renal function.
records.headline_result: overall and diagnostic image quality maintained against standard single-energy CT, with 19.6% lower dose index and 14.3% lower total iodine administration

records.title: Predicting brain age with complex networks: From adolescence to adulthood.
records.exclusion_reason: brain-age prediction across ages 7 to 64 in a healthy population; a methodological neuroscience study rather than a pediatric diagnostic application

records.title: Traditional and New Methods of Bone Age Assessment-An Overview.
records.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in pediatric endocrinology, sixty years after the atlases were published
records.patient_population: children undergoing bone age assessment
records.model_description: An endocrinology-side overview of how bone age is measured now. It covers the Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse atlases, the automated programs that have been validated against them (which are precise, remove inter- and intra-rater variability and cut reading time), and the radiation-free alternatives using ultrasound or MRI that are the least-developed part of this field.

records.title: Radiogenomics of neuroblastoma in pediatric patients: CT-based radiomics signature in predicting MYCN amplification.
records.model_family: radiomics signature combined with clinical factors in a nomogram
records.clinical_problem: predicting MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which determines risk group and therapy
records.patient_population: 78 children with neuroblastoma (55 training, 23 test)
records.model_description: A second, independent CT radiomics attempt at MYCN status in neuroblastoma, on a smaller cohort than the other in this database. It reports that both pre- and post-contrast phases contribute, and that adding clinical factors to the radiomics signature clearly beats a clinical model alone. Two independent groups reaching similar conclusions on this question is worth more than either result on its own.
records.headline_result: combined clinical-radiomics nomogram AUC 0.95 in training and 0.91 in testing, against 0.82 and 0.70 for the clinical model alone

records.title: CA-Net: Comprehensive Attention Convolutional Neural Networks for Explainable Medical Image Segmentation.
records.model_family: CNN with joint spatial, channel and scale attention
records.body_region: placenta and fetal brain (and skin lesions, non-radiologic)
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta and fetal brain on fetal MRI
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses dermoscopic skin lesion images
records.model_description: Takes a fetal MRI slice and returns a segmentation of the placenta or fetal brain, using three kinds of attention so the network weighs the right location, the right feature channels and the right scale at once. The attention maps can be displayed, which is the paper's explainability claim. It is about fifteen times smaller than a comparable state-of-the-art segmentation network.
records.release_evidence: our code is available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/CA-Net
records.headline_result: Dice improved over U-Net from 84.79% to 87.08% for the placenta and 93.20% to 95.88% for the fetal brain

records.title: Technology trends and applications of deep learning in ultrasonography: image quality enhancement, diagnostic support, and improving workflow efficiency.
records.exclusion_reason: review of deep learning applications in ultrasonography across breast, thyroid, heart, kidney, liver and fetal head; no model developed and not pediatric-specific

records.title: Integration of brain and behavior measures for identification of data-driven groups cutting across children with ASD, ADHD, or OCD.
records.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
records.model_family: similarity network fusion across imaging and behavioral measures
records.clinical_problem: whether the diagnostic boundaries between autism, ADHD and OCD correspond to anything in the brain
records.patient_population: 176 children aged 6-16 with autism, ADHD or OCD from the POND network, all scanned on the same 3T scanner
records.model_description: Fuses cortical thickness, subcortical volume, white matter anisotropy and behavioral measures into a single similarity structure, then finds groups that cut across the three diagnoses. The four resulting transdiagnostic groups differed in everyday adaptive functioning, which the DSM categories did not capture as well. Scanning all children on one scanner removes the usual site confound.
records.headline_result: four transdiagnostic groups driven mainly by cortical thickness in socio-emotional and attention networks plus inattention symptoms; groups remained stable across resampling and differed significantly in adaptive functioning

records.title: Deep learning and medical image processing for coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic: A survey.
records.exclusion_reason: survey of deep learning for COVID-19 imaging in a general population; pediatric imaging appears only as a passing example

records.title: Improving Image Quality and Reducing Radiation Dose for Pediatric CT by Using Deep Learning Reconstruction.
records.model_family: deep-learning CT reconstruction algorithm
records.clinical_problem: keeping diagnostic image quality on pediatric CT while cutting radiation dose
records.patient_population: children undergoing clinical CT (19 patients, mean age 11 years)
records.model_description: Reconstructs the CT image from the raw projection data with a trained network in place of filtered back projection or iterative reconstruction, removing noise without the waxy texture model-based iterative reconstruction introduces. Assessed both by a mathematical observer model across object sizes and contrasts and by three pediatric radiologists scoring edge definition, noise and conspicuity of low-contrast structures.
records.release_evidence: the abstract does not say whether the algorithm is a vendor product or research software
records.headline_result: object detectability improved 51% over filtered back projection, 18% over statistical iterative and 11% over model-based iterative reconstruction; radiologists preferred it (7.0 vs 6.2, 6.2 and 4.6); 52% greater dose reduction than statistical iterative reconstruction
records.study_design: retrospective single-center image-quality study with reader assessment

records.title: Identification of suicidality in adolescent major depressive disorder patients using sMRI: A machine learning approach.
records.model_family: support vector machine with recursive feature elimination on FreeSurfer cortical measures
records.clinical_problem: separating adolescents with depression who have attempted suicide from those with ideation only
records.patient_population: 66 adolescents and young adults with major depressive disorder
records.model_description: Takes structural MRI cortical thickness and volume measures and classifies whether a depressed adolescent has attempted suicide or has ideation without attempt. The top-ranked features were orbitofrontal and cingulate thickness. The clinical framing is risk stratification for prevention, though the design is cross-sectional so it separates groups rather than predicting a future attempt.
records.headline_result: 78.6% cross-validated balanced accuracy (sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 84.0%, positive predictive value 88.2%)

records.title: Artificial intelligence for automatic cerebral ventricle segmentation and volume calculation: a clinical tool for the evaluation of pediatric hydrocephalus.
records.model_family: encoder-decoder convolutional neural network
records.clinical_problem: tracking ventricular size objectively over time in children with hydrocephalus, which currently drives shunt decisions by eye
records.patient_population: 200 children with obstructive hydrocephalus from four pediatric hospitals plus 199 controls, with external testing at a fifth hospital
records.model_description: Takes a T2-weighted MRI and returns the ventricles outlined and their volume in about a second and a half. Built deliberately for clinical use rather than research: trained across four pediatric hospitals, tested at a fifth, and benchmarked against FreeSurfer, which it beat on both accuracy and speed. Serial volumes rather than subjective impression are what would change hydrocephalus management.
records.dataset_size: 399 children across four hospitals, plus an external dataset from a fifth
records.headline_result: Dice 0.901 overall (0.946 in hydrocephalus), 0.926 on external data from a fifth hospital, more accurate than FreeSurfer at 1.48 seconds per scan
records.study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation

records.title: Deep learning prediction of proton and photon dose distributions for paediatric abdominal tumours.
records.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
records.model_family: 3D patch-based U-net networks, one per modality
records.clinical_problem: choosing between proton and photon radiotherapy for a child, which currently requires planning both
records.patient_population: 80 children with neuroblastoma or Wilms tumour
records.model_description: Predicts what the proton and the photon dose distribution would look like for a specific child's anatomy, without running either planning process. Two radiation oncologists then chose a modality from the predicted organ-at-risk dose difference and reached the same decision as from the fully planned distributions in 18 of 20 patients. The intended use is explicit: to identify the better technique where proton planning expertise or capacity is not available.
records.dataset_size: 80 children (60 for training with 5-fold cross-validation, 20 for inference)
records.headline_result: dose-volume histogram differences within 6% of planned distributions; identical modality selection in 18 of 20 patients
records.study_design: retrospective single-center technical validation with clinician assessment

records.title: Neuroimaging in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
records.exclusion_reason: review of neuroimaging in ADHD concluding it is still far from clinical use; prediction work is noted as a trend but no model is presented

records.title: A Deep Attentive Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Cortical Plate Segmentation in Fetal MRI.
records.model_family: fully convolutional network with deep attentive modules, mixed kernel convolutions, deep supervision and residual connections
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal cortical plate, the measurement that quantitative studies of cortical folding and brain maturation depend on and that is otherwise refined by hand
records.patient_population: reconstructed fetal brain MRI of fetuses scanned at 16 to 39 weeks gestation (mean 28.6 +/- 5.3)
records.model_description: A segmentation network built around the specific difficulty of this structure: the cortical plate is thin relative to the resolution of reconstructed fetal MRI, partial volume is severe, and its shape changes continuously across the second and third trimesters. Attention modules with mixed kernel sizes are the response. Under a minute per brain, which is what makes population-scale studies of cortical folding practical.
records.headline_result: average Dice 0.87, Hausdorff distance 0.96 mm and symmetric surface difference 0.28 mm, outperforming several state-of-the-art deep models and a multi-atlas method
records.study_design: retrospective model development with expert evaluation

records.title: MRI-based 3D models of the hip joint enables radiation-free computer-assisted planning of periacetabular osteotomy for treatment of hip dysplasia using deep learning for automatic segmentation.
records.exclusion_reason: deep learning segmentation of MRI-based 3D hip models for planning periacetabular osteotomy in 26 symptomatic patients described as of childbearing age; the conditions are developmental but the imaged patients are young adults, not children

records.title: Comparison of different machine learning approaches to predict dental age using Demirjian's staging approach.
records.exclusion_reason: dental age estimation from orthopantomograms; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: A deep learning framework for 18F-FDG PET imaging diagnosis in pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.
records.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
records.model_family: symmetricity-driven pair-of-cube Siamese convolutional neural network over 386 symmetry features
records.clinical_problem: localizing the epileptic focus on 18F-FDG PET in children with temporal lobe epilepsy, where the focus may be either hypo- or hyper-metabolic with no clear boundary and misdiagnosis is common
records.patient_population: 201 pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy and 24 age-matched controls who underwent 18F-FDG PET-CT
records.model_description: The architecture encodes the way a nuclear medicine physician actually reads these studies - by comparing the two hemispheres - as a Siamese network over paired cubes, and then reports the metabolic abnormality of the predicted focus as an asymmetry index. Comparison is against the three things it would replace: visual assessment, SPM, and a divergence-based logistic regression. Dice around 0.5 sounds modest until read against expert visual assessment at 0.31 to 0.44 on the same cases.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.51 for focus localization versus 0.24 for SPM (P < 0.01) and 0.31-0.44 for visual assessment; classification AUC 0.93 versus 0.72 for logistic regression

records.title: Retrospective motion artifact correction of structural MRI images using deep learning improves the quality of cortical surface reconstructions.
records.exclusion_reason: retrospective motion-artifact correction developed and validated on adult datasets; infant and pediatric subjects are named only as a potential future application

records.title: Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation for Automatic Head Circumference Biometry Using Deeply Supervised Attention-Gated V-Net.
records.model_family: V-Net with attention gates, deep supervision and a multi-scale loss
records.clinical_problem: measuring head circumference from a fetal ultrasound image automatically
records.patient_population: fetuses across trimesters in the public HC18 challenge dataset (355 test images)
records.model_description: Segments the fetal skull on a 2D ultrasound image, then fits an ellipse to it and reports head circumference. Attention gates and deep supervision are what lift it above plain U-Net and V-Net on this task, which is hard because the appearance of the fetal head changes markedly between trimesters. Benchmarked on a public challenge, so the numbers are directly comparable with other entries.
records.release_evidence: the code of DAG V-Net will be made available publicly on https://github.com/xiaojinmao-code/
records.dataset_size: HC18 challenge training set with augmentation; 355 test images
records.headline_result: Dice 97.93%, head circumference absolute difference 1.77 ± 1.69 mm, Hausdorff distance 1.29 ± 0.79 mm; fifth place in the HC18 challenge
records.study_design: technical development on a public benchmark

records.title: The interaction between language and working memory: a systematic review of fMRI studies in the past two decades.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of fMRI studies of working memory and language, explicitly excluding children; no machine-learning model

records.title: Multi-Site Infant Brain Segmentation Algorithms: The iSeg-2019 Challenge.
records.model_family: 30 competing deep-learning segmentation methods, 8 reviewed in detail
records.clinical_problem: segmenting 6-month infant brain MRI, and whether any method survives being moved to another site's scanner
records.patient_population: 6-month-old infants; training from UNC, testing from UNC/UMN, Stanford and Emory with different protocols and scanners
records.model_description: A challenge report rather than a single model. Thirty teams segmented 6-month infant brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and CSF, at the age when the two tissues are nearly isointense and conventional tools fail. The design deliberately puts the test data at different institutions from the training data, and the conclusion is the useful one: multi-site consistency remains unsolved, so a model that works on one scanner should not be assumed to work on another.
records.headline_result: top methods reviewed across whole brain, regions of interest and gyral landmarks; multi-site consistency identified as still an open issue

records.title: Development of a computed tomography-based radiomics nomogram for prediction of transarterial chemoembolization refractoriness in hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.exclusion_reason: CT radiomics nomogram for chemoembolization refractoriness in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma

records.title: Evidence for similar structural brain anomalies in youth and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a machine learning analysis.
records.model_family: deep neural network classification models on structural MRI
records.clinical_problem: whether the structural brain signature of ADHD in children is the same one seen in adults, tested by asking a model trained on one age group to classify the other
records.patient_population: children and adults with ADHD and controls, drawn from ENIGMA-ADHD consortium samples
records.model_description: A study that uses classification accuracy as a hypothesis test rather than as a product claim. The interesting result is the cross-age transfer: a model trained only on adults still separated children with ADHD from controls, which is evidence that the anatomy the network keys on is continuous from childhood into adulthood. Prediction was stronger in children than adults, consistent with the ENIGMA effect sizes.
records.headline_result: structural MRI significantly separated ADHD from control in both children and adults, and the adult-trained model significantly predicted ADHD in the child sample

records.title: Artificial intelligence enables whole-body positron emission tomography scans with minimal radiation exposure.
records.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
records.model_family: convolutional neural network taking paired ultra-low-dose PET and MRI input
records.clinical_problem: cutting the radiation burden of repeated staging PET scans in children with cancer
records.patient_population: 33 children and young adults aged 3-30 with lymphoma undergoing whole-body FDG PET/MRI
records.model_description: Takes a simulated 6.25% dose PET scan together with the MRI acquired at the same time and outputs an image that behaves like a standard-dose PET. What makes this credible is that it checks the quantitative measure clinicians act on: SUVmax, which noise inflates at ultra-low dose, was restored to standard-dose values, and reader confidence agreed with the standard scans far better than with the low-dose ones.
records.dataset_size: 33 children and young adults with lymphoma
records.headline_result: reader agreement with standard clinical scans kappa 0.942 for AI-reconstructed images versus 0.650 for 6.25% dose images; SUVmax restored to standard-dose values
records.study_design: retrospective single-center study with reader assessment

records.title: Automatic quality assessment for 2D fetal sonographic standard plane based on multitask learning.
records.model_family: multitask scheme of three convolutional networks - feature extraction, class prediction and region proposal
records.clinical_problem: quality control of 2D fetal sonographic standard planes, the labor-intensive check that biometry and anomaly diagnosis depend on and that currently needs a professional sonographer
records.patient_population: fetal head, abdominal and heart standard-plane images
records.model_description: Operationalizes the criterion sonographers actually apply - every essential anatomical structure present, complete and clearly bounded - by having the network identify each structure, judge whether it meets standard, and say where it is. Quality control rather than measurement, which is the step upstream of everything else and the one most automation skips. Under a second per image.
records.headline_result: quality assessment of a fetal sonographic image in under a second, with segmentation and diagnosis competitive with state-of-the-art methods

records.title: An algorithm for using deep learning convolutional neural networks with three dimensional depth sensor imaging in scoliosis detection.
records.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
records.model_family: convolutional neural network on three-dimensional depth sensor images of the back
records.clinical_problem: screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis without radiation, by predicting the Cobb angle from a surface scan rather than from a radiograph
records.patient_population: 160 subjects suspected to have adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, from a consecutive prospectively collected series at five scoliosis centers in Japan
records.model_description: Existing scoliosis screening methods - forward bend test, scoliometer - detect asymmetry but predict the Cobb angle poorly, and that is the specific gap this fills: a depth sensor plus a network that outputs a number on the same scale clinicians decide with. The reported accuracy is framed at the two thresholds that matter, 10 degrees for calling it scoliosis and 20 degrees for considering a brace, which is more useful than a bare correlation. Five centers and ten repeats of five-fold cross-validation.
records.headline_result: correlation 0.91 with the actual Cobb angle, mean absolute error 4.0 degrees and RMSE 5.4 degrees; 94% accuracy at the 10-degree threshold and 89% at 20 degrees
records.study_design: retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter series

records.title: Knowledge representation and learning of operator clinical workflow from full-length routine fetal ultrasound scan videos.
records.model_family: deep learning temporal video segmentation followed by automated workflow description
records.clinical_problem: characterizing how sonographers actually perform a routine anomaly scan, so that scanning skill, scan time and machine interfaces can be studied at scale
records.patient_population: full-length routine second-trimester fetal ultrasound scans, over 200 hours of recordings
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model at all, and that is the point - it treats the scan itself as the object of study. The network temporally segments a full-length recording into semantically meaningful segments, turning an unwatchable archive of 200 hours into a structured description of operator behavior. The stated uses are training sonographers, optimizing scan times and designing better machine interfaces, which is the non-interpretive side of imaging AI that pediatric and fetal services rarely have data on.
records.dataset_size: more than 200 hours of full-length routine scan video
records.headline_result: first fully-automatic framework to describe operator clinical workflow from full-length routine second-trimester scan video

records.title: Modality alignment contrastive learning for severity assessment of COVID-19 from lung ultrasound and clinical information.
records.exclusion_reason: COVID-19 severity assessment from lung ultrasound in an adult patient cohort; pregnant women and children are named only as a potential future application

records.title: Artificial intelligence system for automatic deciduous tooth detection and numbering in panoramic radiographs.
records.exclusion_reason: dental panoramic radiography for tooth charting; dental imaging is excluded from this database's scope

records.title: Learning to map 2D ultrasound images into 3D space with minimal human annotation.
records.model_family: convolutional network with a learned pairwise attention module, trained self-supervised by inverting a slice-sampling process
records.clinical_problem: locating where a 2D fetal neurosonography image sits in 3D atlas space, the alignment step that standard plane finding and any 3D interpretation depend on
records.patient_population: 2D slices sampled from 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks gestational age, then real 2D transthalamic plane images and freehand scan video
records.model_description: The annotation problem is dissolved rather than solved: instead of labeling each 2D scan with its 3D position, slices are sampled from volumes and the network is trained to invert the sampling, so supervision is free. It takes a set of images rather than one and learns which pairs to weight, so accuracy improves as more images from the same scan are given - useful, since a real examination produces a stream, not a single frame. It transfers to real standard-plane images and to freehand video.
records.dataset_size: 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks, plus real 2D images and freehand video
records.headline_result: outperforms the baseline by up to 23% on Euclidean distance, plane angle and normalized cross correlation as the number of input images grows, and matches human annotation on real transthalamic plane images

records.title: Machine Learning-Based Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics for Prediction of H3K27M Mutation in Midline Gliomas.
records.model_family: extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) over 651 radiomic features per MRI sequence, with feature selection
records.clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status in midline gliomas non-invasively, a molecular marker with prognostic weight that conventional MRI features do not distinguish
records.patient_population: 109 patients from three academic centers, 60 of them pediatric (55%); 50 H3K27M-mutant and 59 wild-type
records.model_description: A radiogenomics model for a tumor - diffuse midline glioma - where tissue is often not obtainable and the mutation defines the entity. The motivation is stated as a negative result from the prior literature: enhancement, necrosis and edema rates vary and none separates mutant from wild-type, so the signal, if there is one, is in texture rather than in anything a radiologist reports. Multi-institutional, majority pediatric, but a single random split of 109 patients and test performance below training, so the estimate is fragile.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.791 training and 0.737 test; test accuracy 72.7%, precision 76.5%, recall 72.2%, F1 74.3%

records.title: Fundamentals of the Development of Connectivity in the Human Fetal Brain in Late Gestation: From 24 Weeks Gestational Age to Term.
records.journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology
records.exclusion_reason: histological and MRI characterization of fetal connectivity development; descriptive neuropathology with no machine-learning model

records.title: Individual variation underlying brain age estimates in typical development.
records.exclusion_reason: methodological study of what drives brain-age prediction error in typically developing children; a normal-development question with no clinical target

records.title: Prediction of tumor response via a pretreatment MRI radiomics-based nomogram in HCC treated with TACE.
records.exclusion_reason: MRI radiomics for chemoembolization response in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma

records.title: Multimodal brain predictors of current weight and weight gain in children enrolled in the ABCD study ®.
records.model_family: cross-validated elastic-net regression on multimodal imaging features
records.clinical_problem: identifying which 9-10 year olds will gain weight pathologically over the following year
records.patient_population: children aged 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study
records.model_description: Uses structural, diffusion, resting-state and task-based MRI to model current body mass index and, separately, to predict pathological weight gain a year later. Structural features generalized to held-out data and predicted future pathological gain; functional and reward-task measures did not. The practical reading is that the cheap, routinely acquired structural sequence carried the signal and the elaborate functional paradigms did not.
records.headline_result: structural features explained 27% of held-out variance in body mass index and predicted pathological weight gain with area under the curve 0.83 in both training and test sets

records.title: Increased Brain Age Gap Estimate (BrainAGE) in Young Adults After Premature Birth.
records.exclusion_reason: brain-age gap estimation from structural MRI in 101 premature-born young adults versus 111 full-term controls; a brain-age association study in adults, consistent with the other brain-age papers screened out here

records.title: Automated Segmentation of Abdominal Skeletal Muscle on Pediatric CT Scans Using Deep Learning.
records.model_family: paired U-Net models for level localization and muscle segmentation
records.clinical_problem: measuring skeletal muscle mass on CT, a marker of nutritional status and sarcopenia, which requires finding the L3 level and outlining muscle by hand
records.patient_population: 370 patients sampled uniformly from 0 to 18 years and across both sexes
records.model_description: Two problems in one pipeline: locating the L3 vertebral level on the sagittal reformat, then segmenting muscle on the corresponding axial slice. Sampling uniformly across ages from birth to 18 is the design choice that makes it pediatric rather than adult-with-children-included, since body habitus changes completely over that range. Level localization landed within the slice thickness.
records.headline_result: L3 localization error 3.23 ± 2.61 mm, within the reconstructed slice thickness; muscle segmentation Dice 0.93 ± 0.03

records.title: MRI-based radiomics for prognosis of pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: an international study.
records.model_family: LASSO Cox regression on wavelet-filtered radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: prognostication in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, a uniformly fatal childhood tumor that is rarely biopsied
records.patient_population: 177 treatment-naive children with diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma from an international cohort, split into training and independent testing sets
records.model_description: Predicts overall survival from texture features of the routine T1-post-contrast and T2 images at diagnosis, before any treatment. It beats a clinical-only model built from age and sex, and holds up in an independent test set, though the concordance drops from 0.70 to 0.59 when it does. For a tumor where biopsy is often avoided and MRI is the only longitudinal measure, an objective imaging prognostic is worth having even at that accuracy.
records.headline_result: concordance 0.68 for radiomics versus 0.57 for clinical variables alone in training; 0.59 in the independent testing dataset (P = .02)

records.title: An ensemble of neural networks provides expert-level prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease.
records.model_family: ensemble of neural networks with segmentation models
records.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease on screening ultrasound
records.patient_population: fetuses at 18 to 24 weeks undergoing screening ultrasound or echocardiography
records.model_description: Takes a whole fetal ultrasound survey, picks out the five recommended cardiac views, and classifies the heart as normal or complex congenital heart disease, while separate segmentation models compute standard cardiothoracic measurements. It addresses a specific failure of practice: the five screening views can detect 90% of complex disease, but real-world sensitivity is nearer 30%. Performance held up on outside-hospital and lower-quality images.
records.dataset_size: 107,823 training images from 1,326 echocardiograms and screening ultrasounds; internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys and over 4.4 million images
records.headline_result: AUC 0.99, sensitivity 95%, specificity 96%, negative predictive value 100%; sensitivity comparable to clinicians

records.title: Using Machine Learning to Predict the Diagnosis, Management and Severity of Pediatric Appendicitis.
records.model_family: random forest, gradient boosting and logistic regression compared
records.clinical_problem: three separate decisions in suspected pediatric appendicitis: is it appendicitis, does it need surgery, and is it complicated
records.patient_population: 430 children and adolescents aged 0-18 with suspected appendicitis
records.model_description: Combines history, examination, laboratory values and abdominal ultrasound findings to predict diagnosis, management and severity at once, which no earlier model had done. The authors also identified small subsets of 6 to 18 predictors that performed as well as all 38, and deployed the result as a free online tool. Severity, the target that would justify antibiotics instead of surgery, remains the weakest of the three.
records.release_evidence: deployed as an open access easy-to-use online tool (the Appendicitis Prediction Tool)
records.headline_result: area under the precision-recall curve 0.94 for diagnosis, 0.92 for management and 0.70 for severity

records.title: A Radiomics Nomogram for Preoperative Prediction of Early Recurrence of Small Hepatocellular Carcinoma After Surgical Resection or Radiofrequency Ablation.
records.exclusion_reason: radiomics nomogram predicting early recurrence of small hepatocellular carcinoma in 111 adults after resection or radiofrequency ablation; not a pediatric population

records.title: Time-Dependent Deep Image Prior for Dynamic MRI.
records.model_family: unsupervised deep image prior with a learned temporal manifold
records.clinical_problem: reconstructing a moving fetal heart from sparsely sampled dynamic MRI without cardiac gating
records.patient_population: fetuses in retrospective and real fetal cardiac MRI datasets
records.model_description: Reconstructs a dynamic MRI series by fitting a network to that one patient's measurements, with no prior training and no other data. For fetal cardiac imaging this matters because there is no reliable heartbeat signal to gate on, and this method needs none: a low-dimensional manifold encodes the temporal variation and a convolutional network generates the image series consistent with the acquired k-space.
records.headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art methods quantitatively and qualitatively on retrospective and real fetal cardiac datasets

records.title: A Transfer Learning-Based Active Learning Framework for Brain Tumor Classification.
records.exclusion_reason: transfer learning with active learning for low- versus high-grade glioma classification on MRI; children are named among those affected by brain tumors but the abstract does not state the ages of the 203 training and 66 test patients, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: CT-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning Predicts MYCN Amplification in Pediatric Abdominal Neuroblastoma.
records.model_family: radiomics with four classifiers compared, combined into a nomogram
records.clinical_problem: identifying MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which defines the high-risk group and currently requires tissue
records.patient_population: 172 children with abdominal neuroblastoma, 47 MYCN-amplified and 125 not
records.model_description: Extracts radiomic features from three-phase CT and predicts whether the tumor is MYCN-amplified, then folds the signature into a nomogram with clinicopathological and radiographic variables. If it held up prospectively it would let risk stratification start from the staging CT rather than waiting on genetics, which matters most where molecular testing is slow or unavailable.
records.headline_result: training AUC 0.940 for logistic and support vector machine models, 0.927 for random forest and 0.780 for Bayes

records.title: Free-breathing Accelerated Cardiac MRI Using Deep Learning: Validation in Children and Young Adults.
records.model_family: unrolled deep-learning reconstruction with separable 3D convolutions and data consistency steps
records.clinical_problem: getting ventricular volumes and mass in children without repeated breath-holds
records.patient_population: 50 children and young adults aged 5-30 (mean 16 years) undergoing cardiac MRI at a children's hospital, prospectively scanned with both sequences
records.model_description: Reconstructs a 12-fold accelerated free-breathing cine cardiac MRI, so a child gets ventricular volumetry in about a minute of free breathing instead of three minutes of repeated breath-holds. The honest result is a trade: image quality scored slightly lower than the reference sequence, but the volumetric measurements two radiologists derived from it agreed closely, which is what the examination is actually for.
records.dataset_size: trained on 10 adult volunteers; prospectively validated in 50 children and young adults
records.headline_result: acquisition time 0.9 versus 3.0 minutes (P < .001); image quality 3.8 versus 4.3 on a five-point scale; intraclass correlation 0.76-0.97 for all measurements

records.title: Performance evaluation of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in "double low" chest CTA in children: a feasibility study.
records.model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction algorithm, high setting (DLIR-H)
records.clinical_problem: cutting both radiation and iodinated contrast dose in pediatric chest CT angiography, where iterative reconstruction runs out of headroom at low dose and 100 kVp gives too little enhancement at low contrast dose
records.patient_population: 46 children (mean age 5.9 +/- 4.2 years) scanned at 70 kVp with 0.8-1.2 ml/kg contrast, versus 46 age-matched controls at 100 kVp with 1.3-1.8 ml/kg
records.model_description: The clearest pediatric statement of what deep learning reconstruction actually buys: it is spent on lowering two doses at once. Dropping to 70 kVp raises vascular enhancement but also noise, and DLIR absorbs the noise, so the child receives 11 percent less radiation and 24 percent less contrast and the images come out quieter and better enhanced than the standard protocol. A vendor algorithm evaluated in clinical practice rather than a research model.
records.release_evidence: a vendor deep learning image reconstruction algorithm running on the clinical CT scanner, evaluated against the scanner's adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V
records.dataset_size: 46 children in the study group and 46 age-matched controls
records.headline_result: dose-length-product down 11.2% (p = 0.01) and contrast dose down 24% (p < 0.001), with higher aortic enhancement (416.5 vs 342.0 HU) and lower noise (15.1 vs 18.6 HU), both p < 0.001
records.study_design: prospective feasibility study with two-reader qualitative scoring

records.title: Medical imaging deep learning with differential privacy.
records.model_family: differentially private stochastic gradient descent framework for PyTorch
records.clinical_problem: training diagnostic models on children's images without exposing individual patients
records.patient_population: children in the public pediatric pneumonia chest radiograph dataset, plus an adult liver segmentation benchmark
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model but the plumbing beneath one: an open-source framework that trains networks under formal differential privacy guarantees, so that what the model learns cannot be traced back to an individual child. Demonstrated on pediatric pneumonia classification and liver segmentation, with the finding that rigorous privacy costs some classification accuracy but very little segmentation accuracy. Relevant to any children's hospital weighing data sharing against consent.
records.release_evidence: deepee is presented as a free-and-open-source framework for use with PyTorch
records.dataset_size: the pediatric pneumonia dataset and the Medical Segmentation Decathlon liver dataset
records.headline_result: acceptable classification and excellent segmentation performance under formal privacy guarantees, with favorable memory and compute against other frameworks

records.title: Crowdsourcing assessment of maternal blood multi-omics for predicting gestational age and preterm birth.
records.exclusion_reason: prediction of gestational age and preterm birth from maternal blood transcriptomics and proteomics; no imaging

records.title: Application of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in head CT imaging for children to improve image quality and lesion detection.
records.model_family: deep learning image reconstruction compared against filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction
records.clinical_problem: seeing small intracranial lesions on a low-dose pediatric head CT at thin slice thickness
records.patient_population: 50 children undergoing low-dose axial head CT with age-dependent tube current
records.model_description: Tests the specific claim that matters for thin-slice head CT: only the deep-learning reconstruction produced diagnostically usable 0.625 mm images, and those images had the same noise as conventional 5 mm images while showing more lesions (69 against 65). The authors translate that into a dose implication of roughly 85% if current image quality and slice thickness were the target.
records.release_evidence: compares vendor reconstruction options available on the scanner
records.headline_result: 0.625 mm deep-learning images matched 5 mm iterative images on noise and quality while detecting 69 versus 65 lesions, implying up to 85% potential dose reduction

records.title: Improving the image quality of pediatric chest CT angiography with low radiation dose and contrast volume using deep learning image reconstruction.
records.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
records.model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction, high setting (DLIR-H)
records.clinical_problem: keeping thin-slice pediatric chest CT angiography diagnostic at low radiation dose and low contrast volume, where iterative reconstruction over-smooths and loses arterial margins
records.patient_population: 33 children scanned at 70 kVp with automatic tube current modulation and 0.8-1.2 mL/kg contrast
records.model_description: The complement to the same group's larger comparison study: here the comparator is not a standard-dose protocol but the two iterative reconstruction strengths at the same low dose, which isolates what the network adds. The finding is qualitative rather than numerical - 100% ASIR-V matched DLIR on measured noise but produced over-smoothed artery margins, and only DLIR-H was acceptable on all three subjective criteria. Noise numbers alone would have missed that.
records.release_evidence: a vendor deep learning image reconstruction algorithm on the clinical CT scanner, compared against the scanner's ASIR-V
records.headline_result: aortic noise 19.24 +/- 5.77 HU with DLIR-H versus 29.45 +/- 7.59 HU with 50% ASIR-V (p<0.001), at CTDIvol 1.37 +/- 0.29 mGy and 25.43 +/- 13.32 mL contrast; only DLIR-H acceptable on all three qualitative criteria
records.study_design: retrospective image quality study with two-reader consensus scoring

records.title: Application of machine learning to predict the outcome of pediatric traumatic brain injury.
records.journal: Chinese journal of traumatology = Zhonghua chuang shang za zhi
records.model_family: supervised classifiers - support vector machines, neural networks, random forest, logistic regression, naive Bayes and k-nearest neighbour
records.clinical_problem: predicting functional outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, from the vital signs, Glasgow coma scale and intracranial injury characteristics available on admission
records.patient_population: 828 children admitted with traumatic brain injury to a trauma center in southern Thailand between January 2009 and July 2020, all of whom had a brain CT; median age 72 months
records.model_description: A prognostic model built on the features a trauma team already has, including the characteristics of the intracranial injuries read off the CT - a head CT was an inclusion requirement. Outcome is the King's Outcome Scale for Childhood Head Injury dichotomized into favourable and unfavourable, which keeps the target clinically legible. Six algorithms are compared on the same 70/30 split rather than one being tuned and reported.
records.headline_result: machine learning models trained on admission clinical and CT injury characteristics predicted dichotomized functional outcome in the held-out 30%

records.title: Illness duration and symptom profile in symptomatic UK school-aged children tested for SARS-CoV-2.
records.exclusion_reason: app-based symptom epidemiology in children with SARS-CoV-2; no imaging and no model

records.title: Automatic airway segmentation from computed tomography using robust and efficient 3-D convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: low-memory 3D U-Net
records.clinical_problem: extracting the airway tree from chest CT, which quantitative assessment of cystic fibrosis lung disease depends on
records.patient_population: children including those with cystic fibrosis, adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from a lung cancer screening trial, and the public EXACT'09 dataset
records.model_description: Segments the airway tree from a chest CT in a single pass over large 3D patches, often the whole lungs at once, which keeps the method simple and fast. Validated deliberately across three very different datasets, one of them pediatric cystic fibrosis, to show it does not depend on the disease or acquisition it was tuned on. Generalization across datasets is the claim, not just accuracy on one.
records.dataset_size: three datasets including a pediatric cystic fibrosis cohort and the public EXACT'09 set
records.headline_result: highly complete airway trees with few false positives across all three datasets; second highest sensitivity among methods reporting good specificity on EXACT'09

records.title: Prediction of hand-wrist maturation stages based on cervical vertebrae images using artificial intelligence.
records.model_family: ensemble of eight machine learning models over cervical vertebrae morphometric ratios plus age and sex
records.clinical_problem: estimating hand-wrist skeletal maturation stage from the lateral cephalogram already taken for orthodontics, so that treatment timing can be judged without a second radiograph of the hand
records.patient_population: 499 paired hand-wrist radiographs and lateral cephalograms from 455 orthodontic patients aged 6-18 years, collected at two university hospitals and a paediatric dental clinic
records.model_description: Radiation arithmetic rather than accuracy chasing: the growth information is inferred from a film the patient is already getting, which removes the hand-wrist radiograph from the pathway entirely. Features are explicit and interpretable - width-height, width-perpendicular-height and concavity ratios from 13 cervical vertebra landmarks - and adding chronological age and sex improved prediction, which is worth noting since those are free.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.90 Fishman stages (round MAE 0.87, RMSE 1.20) under five-fold cross-validation

records.title: Deep learning-based parameter estimation in fetal diffusion-weighted MRI.

records.model_description: The contribution is the training data, not the network. Reliable fetal diffusion ground truth does not exist, so the authors estimate accurate parameter maps from high-quality newborn scans and then degrade them to match the fetal measurement scheme and noise distribution - manufacturing a fetal training set out of neonatal data. This is a reusable pattern for any pediatric imaging problem where the population of interest cannot be imaged well enough to label.
records.dataset_size: 100 fetal scans for accuracy, 20 for precision, 20 for expert quality assessment

records.clinical_problem: the repetitive parts of obstetric ultrasound: positioning, structure identification, gestational age, and real-time quality assurance
records.patient_population: pregnancies across gestation
records.model_description: A review that frames AI in obstetric ultrasound around repetition rather than diagnosis: the tasks worth automating are the ones done identically many times per scan. records.title: Quantification of Liver Fat Content with CT and MRI: State of the Art.

records.title: Multimodal MR Images-Based Diagnosis of Early Adolescent Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Using Multiple Kernel Learning.
records.model_family: Boruta feature selection with multiple kernel learning fusing structural MRI, functional MRI and diffusion tensor features, classified by a support vector machine
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in early adolescence, where current criteria rest on behavior analysis that is subjective and inconsistent especially in children
records.patient_population: comorbidity-free children with ADHD and covariable-matched healthy children aged 9-10 from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) study
records.model_description: Fusion at the kernel level rather than by concatenating features, which is the point of the paper - it is compared directly against early feature fusion and against each modality alone, and wins. The cohort design is unusually clean for this literature: comorbidity-free cases, covariable-matched controls, a narrow 9-10 age band, drawn from ABCD. The resulting AUC of 0.698 is the sober number that clean design produces, and it is a useful calibration against the higher figures reported on less controlled samples.
records.dataset_size: ABCD subjects aged 9-10, size not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: AUC 0.698 and accuracy 64.3%, significantly better than early feature fusion or any single modality
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public cohort

records.title: Deep Learning-based Reconstruction for Lower-Dose Pediatric CT: Technical Principles, Image Characteristics, and Clinical Implementations.

records.model_family: convolutional neural network reconstruction engines
records.clinical_problem: getting diagnostic image quality out of low-dose CT in the population where dose matters most
records.patient_population: children undergoing CT for a range of clinical indications
records.model_description: A RadioGraphics review of deep-learning CT reconstruction for children: how the engines are trained on paired low-dose and high-dose data to tell true attenuation from noise, how the resulting images look and behave differently from filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction, and what dose reduction is achievable in practice. Written for a department deciding whether to adopt what is already a purchasable scanner option.
records.release_evidence: deep learning-based reconstruction has been introduced to overcome the limitations of the FBP and IR approaches and is currently available clinically

records.title: Comparison of intracranial injury predictability between machine learning algorithms and the nomogram in pediatric traumatic brain injury.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning predicts whether a head CT will show intracranial injury in children with traumatic brain injury, from 14 clinical parameters; the imaging finding is the label rather than the input, so no images or image-derived features are analyzed

records.title: DenResCov-19: A deep transfer learning network for robust automatic classification of COVID-19, pneumonia, and tuberculosis from X-rays.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.exclusion_reason: DenResCov-19 classifies COVID-19, pneumonia, tuberculosis and healthy chest radiographs by joining DenseNet-121 and ResNet-50; childhood pneumonia mortality is cited as motivation but the abstract does not state that the imaged patients are children, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: Application of deep learning upon spinal radiographs to predict progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis at first clinic visit.
records.model_family: self-attentive capsule network with two-stage transfer learning, on a region of interest centered at the curve apex
records.clinical_problem: telling at the first clinic visit which mild adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curves will progress, the prediction that decides who is braced and who is watched
records.patient_population: skeletally immature patients (Risser <= 2) with 11-30 degree curves presenting between October 2015 and April 2020: 328 for training and cross-validation, 110 for independent testing on biplanar EOS, plus 52 on standard PA radiographs for cross-platform validation
records.model_description: Prior work showed three-dimensional morphology predicts progression but needed biplanar equipment and slow software reconstruction; this puts the same prediction on the plain standing PA radiograph every clinic already takes. The 3D reconstruction is used only to establish which parameters matter - apical rotation and torsion - and then discarded from the deployed pathway. The separate 52-patient cross-platform cohort on standard radiographs is the part that makes it portable beyond an EOS centre.
records.headline_result: accuracy 76.6%, sensitivity 75.2%, specificity 80.2% for progressive versus non-progressive curves, outperforming conventional CNNs and a clinical parameter logistic regression
records.study_design: retrospective cohort model development with cross-platform validation

records.title: Impact of Age and Sex on COVID-19 Severity Assessed From Radiologic and Clinical Findings.
records.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
records.exclusion_reason: COVID-19 severity by age and sex in an adult hospital cohort; children are mentioned only as a population other studies have focused on

records.title: A Deep-Learning Aided Diagnostic System in Assessing Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Pediatric Pelvic Radiographs.
records.model_family: three-stage pipeline: Mask R-CNN pelvic bone segmentation, HRNet landmark localization, then measurement and classification
records.clinical_problem: measuring and classifying developmental dysplasia of the hip on pediatric pelvic radiographs, where the acetabular index and centre-edge angle are drawn by hand and observers disagree
records.patient_population: 1265 pediatric pelvic radiographs for training and 133 from two other medical institutions for validation, with three orthopedic surgeons as comparators
records.model_description: The decomposition matches how the measurement is actually made - find the ilium, pubis, ischium and femoral heads, then place the landmarks, then compute the angles - which makes each stage checkable. The result that matters clinically is not accuracy but variance: intraclass consistency across surgeons was 0.79-0.98 while the model's was 1.00, because a deterministic model measuring the same film twice cannot disagree with itself. It also matched an intermediate surgeon on Tonnis and IHDI grading, in less time.
records.headline_result: Tonnis and IHDI classification accuracy 0.86-0.95 for both hips; no statistically significant difference from surgeons on the numeric indices; intraclass consistency 1.00 for the model versus 0.79-0.98 among surgeons, and significantly faster
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and observer comparison

records.title: MONAIfbs: MONAI-based fetal brain MRI deep learning segmentation

records.model_description: Replaces a two-step localise-then-segment pipeline with a single well-trained network, on the argument that the two-step design fails irrecoverably when localisation fails. It reduced outliers as well as improving average accuracy, which matters more here: super-resolution reconstruction is only automatic if the mask never needs a human. Built on MONAI, so it drops into existing fetal pipelines.
records.release_evidence: presented as a tool built on the open MONAI framework
records.headline_result: single-step dynamic UNet outperformed the published two-step approach, including when that approach was retrained on the same expanded dataset, and reduced the number of outliers

records.title: Illness characteristics of COVID-19 in children infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant

records.title: A transfer learning method with deep residual network for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis.

records.clinical_problem: diagnosis of childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs

records.model_description: Takes a pediatric chest radiograph and returns a pneumonia classification, with dilated convolutions chosen so that going deeper does not throw away the spatial detail that locates the inflammatory area. Initialized from weights learned on large datasets in the same field because the pediatric data alone is too small. The authors argue it copes better with low-resolution images and partially obscured consolidation than earlier methods.
records.headline_result: recall 96.7% and F1 score 92.7% on the test set

records.title: Recent Development in Three and Four Dimension Fetal Echocardiography.

records.title: Atypical Functional Connectivity in Tourette Syndrome Differs Between Children and Adults.
records.model_family: multivariate classification on whole-brain functional connectivity
records.clinical_problem: whether Tourette syndrome has an imaging signature, and whether it is the same signature in children as in adults
records.patient_population: 202 children and adults with Tourette syndrome and control subjects
records.model_description: Classifies Tourette syndrome from functional connectivity separately in children and in adults, then asks whether either classifier transfers to the other age group. It does not, which is the finding: the connections that distinguish the disorder are age-specific. For anyone building pediatric models from adult data, this is a clean demonstration of why that assumption fails in a developmental disorder.
records.headline_result: successful classification in children and adults separately, with no generalization across age groups

records.title: Data-driven identification of subtypes of executive function across typical development, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorders.

records.title: Development and validation of a machine-learning model for prediction of shoulder dystocia.

records.model_description: Uses sonographic fetal biometry, adjusted for gestational age at delivery, together with obstetric history to predict shoulder dystocia, and validates on a cohort from a different country and health system. It beat the current paradigm of estimated fetal weight plus maternal diabetes. Adjusted estimated fetal weight and abdominal circumference were the strongest imaging contributors, which is a check that the model is using the anatomy one would expect.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.793 versus 0.745 for adjusted estimated fetal weight combined with diabetes (P = 1e-16)

records.title: The Use of Lung Ultrasound to Monitor the Antibiotic Response of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Children: A Preliminary Hypothesis.
records.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
records.exclusion_reason: case series of six children describing lung ultrasound findings during antibiotic treatment of community-acquired pneumonia; no machine learning

records.title: A Generic Quality Control Framework for Fetal Ultrasound Cardiac Four-Chamber Planes.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: three-network pipeline: basic CNN, deeper multi-task CNN, and an aggregated residual visual block detector
records.clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal cardiac four-chamber view is adequate to diagnose from
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing cardiac screening ultrasound
records.model_description: Scores the quality of a fetal four-chamber view in three steps: is this actually a four-chamber plane, are the gain and zoom right, and are the key anatomical structures visible. The three outputs combine into one quantitative score. It runs at 101 frames per second, which is fast enough to give the sonographer feedback while the probe is still on the abdomen.
records.dataset_size: an institutional fetal ultrasound dataset; size not stated
records.headline_result: mean average precision 93.52% at 101 frames per second

records.title: An automated framework for localization, segmentation and super-resolution reconstruction of fetal brain MRI.
records.model_family: two-stage CNN localization and segmentation plus outlier-robust super-resolution
records.clinical_problem: producing a usable high-resolution fetal brain volume from motion-corrupted stacks, including brains malformed by open spina bifida
records.patient_population: fetuses with normal brains and with varying ventriculomegaly associated with open spina bifida
records.model_description: A four-stage pipeline that takes the motion-corrupted 2D slice stacks of a fetal brain MRI and returns a high-resolution volume in standard anatomical space with no user input. One network finds the brain, a second segments it finely, then a super-resolution step reconstructs the volume. It removes the manual brain-masking step that has kept fetal volume reconstruction out of routine practice.
records.headline_result: each stage outperformed state-of-the-art methods on segmentation and reconstruction, including expert-reader quality assessment

records.title: Modular segregation of task-dependent brain networks contributes to the development of executive function in children.
records.exclusion_reason: graph analysis of task-dependent network segregation and executive function in typically developing children; no machine-learning model and no clinical target

records.title: Deep learning, reusable and problem-based architectures for detection of consolidation on chest X-ray images.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
records.model_family: problem-based CNN architecture with transfer learning and custom preprocessing
records.clinical_problem: detecting consolidation on a child's chest radiograph
records.patient_population: children in the pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with a separate dataset used to test generalization
records.model_description: Argues that networks designed to win on ImageNet are the wrong shape for radiographs, and designs an architecture around the problem instead, with preprocessing chosen to preserve the information that consolidation lives in. It checks its own reasoning with an occlusion test showing which region drove each decision, and tests generalization on a second dataset rather than a held-out split of the same one.
records.dataset_size: the pediatric chest X-ray dataset plus an external validation dataset
records.headline_result: 94.67% accuracy for consolidation detection, above the previously published architectures on the same dataset

records.title: Using a Dual-Input Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Detection of Pediatric Supracondylar Fracture on Conventional Radiography.
records.model_family: dual-input CNN merging two ResNet branches
records.clinical_problem: detecting supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children on conventional radiographs
records.patient_population: children undergoing elbow radiography; 1,266 AP and lateral pairs for development, 258 for temporal testing and 95 from a second hospital
records.model_description: Reads the anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs together, as a radiologist does, by merging two networks rather than judging each view alone. Tested twice on data the model had never seen: a later year at the same hospital and a different hospital entirely. Its errors are asymmetric in a clinically useful direction, with very high negative predictive value and lower specificity, meaning it over-calls rather than misses.
records.dataset_size: 1,266 radiograph pairs for development; 258 temporal and 95 geographic external test pairs
records.headline_result: AUC 0.985 (temporal) and 0.992 (geographic) external test sets, comparable to human readers; geographic sensitivity 100%, specificity 86.1%, negative predictive value 100%
records.study_design: retrospective development with temporal and geographic external validation and reader study

records.title: Invited Review: Factors associated with atypical brain development in preterm infants: insights from magnetic resonance imaging.

records.title: Neuroimaging in Schizophrenia.
