records.title: Deep Learning for Lesion Detection, Progression, and Prediction of Musculoskeletal Disease.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.clinical_problem: where deep learning stands for musculoskeletal lesion detection, progression and prediction, including pediatric bone age
records.patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A review that sorts musculoskeletal deep learning by modality and by how close each application is to the clinic. Its judgment is that pediatric bone age and fracture detection on radiographs perform well enough to be nearly ready for practice, while CT and especially MRI applications remain harder because the abnormality has to be tracked across slices and contrasts. It closes by insisting on prospective multi-institution evaluation before deployment.

records.title: Deep CNN ensembles and suggestive annotations for infant brain MRI segmentation.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: ensemble of semi-dense 3D fully convolutional networks
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the 6-month infant brain, where gray and white matter are nearly isointense
records.patient_population: 6-month-old infants in the public MICCAI iSEG-2017 challenge data
records.model_description: An ensemble of networks segmenting infant brain tissue from paired T1 and T2 images. The useful property is that where the ensemble members disagree, the segmentation is usually wrong, so the disagreement map tells a human where to look and correct. The architecture uses an order of magnitude fewer parameters than a 3D U-Net, which matters for anyone deploying this on ordinary hardware.
records.headline_result: ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams; ensemble disagreement highly correlated with segmentation error
records.study_design: technical development on a public challenge

records.title: A Multidimensional Neural Maturation Index Reveals Reproducible Developmental Patterns in Children and Adolescents.
records.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
records.exclusion_reason: neural maturation index built from brain-age prediction in typically developing children; a developmental neuroscience measure rather than a diagnostic imaging application

records.title: Using deep-learning algorithms to classify fetal brain ultrasound images as normal or abnormal.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: deep-learning segmentation, classification and localization models
records.clinical_problem: recognizing an abnormal fetal brain on standard axial screening planes
records.patient_population: images from 10,251 normal and 2,529 abnormal pregnancies, with abnormality confirmed by neonatal ultrasound, follow-up or autopsy
records.model_description: Takes a standard axial fetal brain ultrasound image, segments the skull outline, classifies the brain as normal or abnormal, and overlays a heat map indicating where the abnormality is. Trained on a large hospital archive with outcomes confirmed after birth rather than by the reporting sonographer, and split at case rather than image level, which is the methodologically careful choice.
records.dataset_size: 15,372 normal and 14,047 abnormal images from 12,780 pregnancies
records.headline_result: classification accuracy 96.3%, sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 95.9%, AUC 0.989; lesions localized precisely in 61.6% of abnormal images and closely in a further 24.6%

records.title: Machine Learning in Fetal Cardiology: What to Expect.
records.clinical_problem: assessing fetal cardiac structure and function when the heart is small, moving, and often scanned by someone without fetal echocardiography training
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography
records.model_description: A short review for fetal cardiologists of where machine learning can help: improving the acquired image, extracting measurements and segmentations automatically, and supporting the prenatal diagnosis of cardiac remodeling and structural abnormality. Written as an orientation to the technology rather than an evaluation of specific models.

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for World Health Organization-defined chest radiograph primary-endpoint pneumonia in children.
records.model_family: pixel-level texture classification on multi-scale Gaussian derivative features
records.clinical_problem: identifying WHO-defined primary-endpoint pneumonia on a child's chest radiograph, the definition used in vaccine efficacy and epidemiological studies
records.patient_population: 858 interpretable pediatric chest radiographs, 39% with primary-endpoint pneumonia by radiologist consensus
records.model_description: Targets a specific and consequential definition rather than pneumonia in general: the WHO primary-endpoint criterion is what vaccine trials are scored against, and it depends on three radiologists agreeing. Automating it would make large epidemiological studies tractable and remove reader variability from vaccine efficacy estimates. Three radiologists independently set the reference, and the harder task of separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate is reported separately.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.850 against radiologist consensus (sensitivity 76%, specificity 80%); AUC 0.810 separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate

records.title: Deep Learning Techniques for Automatic Detection of Embryonic Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
records.model_family: four-stage framework: transfer learning, deep feature extraction, feature reduction and classification, with feature fusion across pretrained networks
records.clinical_problem: detecting embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders on prenatal MRI, where up to three in a thousand pregnancies carry a brain defect and earlier detection changes counseling
records.patient_population: embryonic MRI images across various gestational ages
records.model_description: The argument is against the handcrafted-feature pipelines that preceded it: enhancement, segmentation and feature engineering each introduce choices, and a deep network learns from the raw image instead. Feature fusion across several pretrained backbones stands in for the training data that prenatal MRI cohorts do not have. Comparison is against prior work on embryonic images rather than a held-out external set, so the performance claim is relative.
records.headline_result: identified embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders from MRI across a range of gestational ages, performing competitively with prior work on embryonic images

records.title: Prediction of Pulmonary to Systemic Flow Ratio in Patients With Congenital Heart Disease Using Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Chest Radiographs.
records.model_family: transfer-learned convolutional network regressing a continuous value from the chest radiograph
records.clinical_problem: quantifying pulmonary blood flow in congenital heart disease from the chest radiograph, which today is read subjectively and qualitatively and whose gold standard is an invasive catheterization
records.patient_population: 1031 cardiac catheterizations in 657 patients at a tertiary center from January 2005 to April 2019 (median age 3.4 years, IQR 1.2-8.6), with 78 patients / 100 catheterizations held out; mean Fick-derived pulmonary to systemic flow ratio 1.43 (SD 0.95)
records.model_description: Turns a qualitative impression - does the pulmonary vasculature look plethoric - into a number on the same scale as the catheter measurement, with the Fick-derived ratio from a simultaneous catheterization as ground truth. The comparison against three certified pediatric cardiologists reading the same films is what establishes the claim, and the clinically salient operating point (a ratio of 2.0 or more, the shunt magnitude that prompts intervention) is reported separately. A non-invasive stand-in for part of what catheterization is done to answer.
records.dataset_size: 1031 catheterizations in 657 patients; 100 held out for evaluation
records.headline_result: prediction of the pulmonary to systemic flow ratio from chest radiographs evaluated by intraclass correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, with the diagnostic concordance rate compared against three certified pediatric cardiologists
records.study_design: retrospective observational study with expert comparison

records.title: DW-Net: A cascaded convolutional neural network for apical four-chamber view segmentation in fetal echocardiography.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: dilated convolutional chain followed by a W-Net refinement stage
records.clinical_problem: outlining the seven key structures of the apical four-chamber view, from which congenital heart disease is judged
records.patient_population: 895 apical four-chamber views from fetal echocardiography
records.model_description: Segments seven anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, contending with speckle, chambers that look alike, and boundaries that simply are not visible in places. A dilated convolution chain localizes the chambers across scales and a second stage sharpens the boundaries. The output is intended as the input to automated cardiac indices rather than as a diagnosis in itself.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.827, pixel accuracy 0.933, AUC 0.990, substantially above established segmentation methods

records.title: Prediction of fetal weight at varying gestational age in the absence of ultrasound examination using ensemble learning.
records.exclusion_reason: predicts fetal weight from clinical variables precisely in the absence of an ultrasound examination; not an imaging model

records.title: Artificial intelligence in bone age assessment: accuracy and efficiency of a novel fully automated algorithm compared to the Greulich-Pyle method.
records.model_family: fully automated AI bone age software
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment against the Greulich-Pyle standard, in both accuracy and reading time
records.patient_population: 514 patients undergoing hand radiography for bone age
records.model_description: Compares a commercial-style automated bone age program against three blinded radiologists applying Greulich-Pyle, with a two-expert consensus as reference. The software was more accurate than the individual readers, not merely comparable, and cut reading time by 87%. Performance did not differ by sex. The design is the useful part: blinded readers, a consensus reference, and time measured alongside accuracy.
records.release_evidence: described as a novel AI software version; commercial availability not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: mean absolute deviation from reference 0.34 years for the software versus 0.79 years for the readers (p < 0.001); reading time reduced by 87%

records.title: DeepFMRI: End-to-end deep learning for functional connectivity and classification of ADHD using fMRI.
records.model_family: end-to-end deep network (feature extractor, connectivity network, classifier)
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD, which currently rests entirely on behavioral assessment
records.patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset, contributed by several imaging sites
records.model_description: Takes preprocessed resting-state fMRI time series and outputs an ADHD diagnosis, learning the functional connectivity representation as part of the network rather than computing it beforehand. Because connectivity is learned end to end, the model can be interrogated for which regions carried the decision; here the frontal lobe dominated. Trained and tested on a public multi-site dataset, so the numbers are directly comparable with prior work.
records.headline_result: 73.1% accuracy at the New York University site (specificity 91.6%, sensitivity 65.5%), above prior state of the art
records.study_design: technical development on a public benchmark

records.title: Towards a new 3D classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
records.model_family: fuzzy c-means clustering over ten 3D parameters measured on biplanar radiograph reconstructions
records.clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis in three dimensions, since the classifications surgeons plan from are two-dimensional and do not describe the deformity they are actually operating on
records.patient_population: patients from a multicenter adolescent idiopathic scoliosis database, all with biplanar radiographs and 3D reconstruction of the entire spine; cluster sizes 11 to 290
records.model_description: Unsupervised, and deliberately so - the point is to let the data propose subgroups rather than test an existing scheme. Eleven clusters emerged from ten 3D parameters, and the validation step is the one that matters for a taxonomy: four experienced spine surgeons from the SRS 3D Scoliosis Committee reviewed representative cases and unanimously agreed each cluster was a group current classifications do not name. Whether these subgroups predict surgical outcome is the unanswered question.
records.headline_result: eleven statistically distinct 3D subgroups, all judged by four spine surgeons to be undefined in current classifications

records.title: MRI Techniques to Decrease Imaging Times in Children.
records.journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
records.clinical_problem: shortening pediatric MRI enough to reduce or avoid sedation and general anesthesia
records.patient_population: children undergoing MRI
records.model_description: A RadioGraphics review of the commercially available ways to shorten a pediatric MRI (parallel imaging, simultaneous multislice, radial sampling, compressed sensing, automated protocol selection) and the ones still under investigation, including AI-based reconstruction and prospective motion correction. It is the practical counterpart to the model papers: it says which of these a department can buy today.
records.release_evidence: the reviewed acceleration techniques are described as commercially available products in clinical use

records.title: Distinguishing between paediatric brain tumour types using multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: A multi-site study.
records.model_family: machine learning classifiers on combined diffusion and perfusion features
records.clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of the three common childhood brain tumour types, which is a genuine radiological challenge
records.patient_population: children with brain tumours imaged at multiple centres
records.model_description: Most quantitative work in this area is single-centre and single-modality; this combines diffusion and perfusion imaging across sites. It also takes features from the whole brain as well as the tumour, and finds both contribute, which is a useful observation for a field that segments the lesion and discards everything else.
records.dataset_size: a multi-centre paediatric brain tumour cohort
records.headline_result: combining diffusion and perfusion features from tumour and whole brain gave the optimal classifier at over 80% predictive precision

records.title: Using Deep Learning Algorithms to Grade Hydronephrosis Severity: Toward a Clinical Adjunct.
records.model_family: five-layer convolutional neural network
records.clinical_problem: grading hydronephrosis severity on renal ultrasound, currently a subjective five-point judgment
records.patient_population: 673 patients aged 0 to 116 months (mean 16.5 months) with 2,420 sagittal renal ultrasound images across all five Society for Fetal Urology grades
records.model_description: Assigns a Society for Fetal Urology grade to a renal ultrasound image. The reported numbers are refreshingly candid: it places 94% of images correctly or within one grade, but only 51% exactly right on the five-way task, and the clinically decisive distinctions (low versus high grade, and grade II versus III) reach 78% and 71%. The authors frame it as a decision and teaching aid rather than a grader.
records.headline_result: 94% of images correct or within one grade on the five-way task (51% exactly correct); 78% accuracy for low versus high grade and 71% for grade II versus III

The paper is honest about the adult-to-pediatric transfer: fuzzy segmentation metrics dropped when the network trained on adults was applied to children, and thresholds had to be re-optimized. Measurement error against radiography was nonetheless within 2.2 degrees.
records.dataset_size: eight adult volunteers for training, eight pediatric patients for testing
records.headline_result: maximum error 2.2 degrees against radiographic scoliosis measurement, with each measurement taking under one minute; segmentation metrics fell when translating from adults to children

records.title: Predicting motor outcome in preterm infants from very early brain diffusion MRI using a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
records.model_family: patch-based convolutional neural network on fractional anisotropy maps
records.clinical_problem: identifying preterm infants headed for neuromotor delay early enough to refer them for intervention
records.patient_population: 77 infants born under 31 weeks gestation, imaged at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age with motor outcome at 2 years corrected age
records.model_description: Predicts abnormal motor outcome at two years from diffusion MRI acquired before term, which is earlier than most preterm prediction work and therefore closer to when intervention could start. Classification is done on image patches and aggregated with a tuned threshold, and heat maps show which brain locations drove the abnormal predictions. Accuracy is moderate and the confidence intervals are wide on 77 infants.
records.dataset_size: 77 very preterm infants (48 normal, 29 abnormal outcome)
records.headline_result: sensitivity 70%, specificity 74%, AUC 0.72 for abnormal motor outcome at 2 years from MRI acquired at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age

records.title: Neonatal Brain Microstructure and Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Early Language Development in Children Born Very Preterm.
records.model_family: multivariate logistic models with leave-one-out cross-validation and exhaustive feature selection over diffusion tensor metrics
records.clinical_problem: identifying which very-low-birth-weight preterm infants are heading for language delay, early enough to intervene while neuroplasticity is greatest
records.patient_population: 102 very-low-birth-weight neonates (birthweight <= 1500 g, gestational age <= 32 weeks) recruited 2010-2011, of whom 92 returned for Bayley-III assessment at 18-22 months adjusted age
records.model_description: Near-term diffusion imaging used as a prognostic instrument rather than a descriptive one. Exhaustive feature selection narrows to three brain regions, which keeps the model small enough to interpret and to replicate. Separate models for composite, expressive and receptive language, with the strongest performance on expressive and receptive - and a side finding that cerebellar asymmetry tracked lower receptive scores. Nearly a third of the cohort scored below 85, so the outcome is common enough for the prediction to matter.
records.headline_result: sensitivity and specificity of 89%/86% for composite, 100%/90% for expressive and 100%/90% for receptive language risk

records.title: Deep Learning Measurement of Leg Length Discrepancy in Children Based on Radiographs.
records.model_family: segmentation network followed by geometric calculation
records.clinical_problem: measuring leg length discrepancy, a task the paper describes as time consuming but cognitively simple
records.patient_population: 179 children aged 5-19 (mean 12 years) imaged for leg length discrepancy
records.model_description: Segments the femurs and tibias on a full-length radiograph and computes each bone's length and the discrepancy between sides. The case it makes is not diagnostic accuracy but time: agreement with the radiology report was essentially perfect and the measurement took one second against 96 seconds by hand. This is the shape of the pediatric AI application most likely to pay for itself, an exact, repetitive measurement rather than a judgment call.
records.headline_result: correlation 0.99 with radiologist measurements (mean absolute error 0.45 cm for individual bones, 0.51 cm for discrepancy); 1 second versus 96 seconds per study

records.title: Ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma: Differentiation using radiomics approach based on machine learning.
records.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
records.model_family: radiomics with Kruskal-Wallis feature selection and a support vector machine
records.clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery, two posterior fossa tumors with different management that overlap on conventional MRI
records.patient_population: 135 MRI slices from children with posterior fossa tumors, split into training and validation sets
records.model_description: A conventional radiomics pipeline whose most useful output is the feature ablation: Gabor, texture and wavelet features were compared head to head, and texture features alone matched the full 300-feature set. Small and slice-level rather than patient-level, so the headline accuracy should be read as a feasibility signal rather than a performance estimate.
records.headline_result: accuracy 0.878, sensitivity 0.929, specificity 0.800, AUC 0.865 on the selected feature set, with no significant loss versus the full feature set

records.title: Automated abnormality classification of chest radiographs using deep convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: deep CNN, pretrained on natural images and on adult radiographs
records.clinical_problem: flagging abnormal chest radiographs for worklist triage, and pneumonia in children specifically
records.patient_population: adult cohorts for pretraining, then fine-tuned on pediatric patients for the pneumonia task
records.model_description: Sorts frontal chest radiographs into normal and abnormal so that abnormal studies can be pushed up the worklist. The pediatric relevance is in the transfer step: a model pretrained on adult cohorts and fine-tuned on children reached higher performance for pneumonia than either alone, which is the practical recipe for a children's hospital with a smaller archive.
records.dataset_size: about 8,500 images for the pretraining benefit analysis; cohort sizes not stated
records.headline_result: AUC 0.982 for normal versus abnormal, 0.944 on an external dataset, and 0.985 for normal versus pneumonia after fine-tuning on children

records.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in urology-Current use and future directions: An iTRUE study.
records.exclusion_reason: review of AI across urology; pediatric urology is one subsection and the applications are mostly genomic, cystoscopic or outcome prediction rather than pediatric radiologic imaging

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for fetal brain ultrasound images using deep convolutional neural networks.
records.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
records.model_family: deep convolutional networks: segmentation of the craniocerebral region, then four-class classification, then class activation mapping for localization
records.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of five common fetal brain abnormalities on standard neurosonographic planes, where missed malformations change counseling and management
records.patient_population: real-world clinical fetal brain ultrasound images at the transventricular and transcerebellar standard planes
records.model_description: A three-stage design that gets weakly-supervised localization for free: the classifier is trained only on image-level labels, and lesions are then localized by class activation mapping rather than by any drawn box. That keeps the annotation burden low, and the numbers show the cost - classification is strong while localization overlap is modest. Positioned as support for junior operators, whose false negatives on fetal brain anomalies are the stated target.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.942 for craniocerebral segmentation, average F1 0.96 for classification, average mean IOU 0.497 for lesion localization

records.title: Healthy versus pathological learning transferability in shoulder muscle MRI segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: deep convolutional encoder-decoders with encoders pre-trained on ImageNet
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the four rotator cuff muscles on MRI in children with obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, so that muscle volume - and from it force - can be estimated without hours of manual tracing
records.patient_population: 24 shoulder examinations in children with unilateral obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, evaluated leave-one-out
records.model_description: A study framed around the two constraints that define pediatric musculoskeletal AI: very little annotated data, and pathological anatomy that looks nothing like the healthy training examples. It answers the transferability question directly by comparing learning schemes, and the winner combines healthy and pathological annotated data with ImageNet pre-training rather than choosing between them. Supraspinatus, the smallest and most atrophied muscle, is where it degrades.
records.headline_result: Dice 82.4% deltoid, 82.0% infraspinatus, 71.0% supraspinatus and 82.8% subscapularis, with surface estimation errors below 83 mm2 except supraspinatus at 134.6 mm2

records.title: Efficient Pneumonia Detection in Chest Xray Images Using Deep Transfer Learning.
records.model_family: weighted ensemble of ResNet18, Xception, InceptionV3, DenseNet121 and MobileNetV3
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia diagnosis on pediatric chest radiographs
records.patient_population: children in the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center pneumonia dataset
records.model_description: Combines the predictions of five transfer-learned networks with learned weights rather than trusting any single architecture, and reports both accuracy and AUC on held-out data from the public Guangzhou pediatric dataset. The very high headline numbers should be read with that dataset's known limitations in mind: it is a single-center collection with a strong case mix, and the model has not been tested anywhere else.
records.dataset_size: the public Guangzhou pediatric pneumonia dataset
records.headline_result: 98.43% test accuracy and AUC 99.76 on unseen data from the same dataset
records.study_design: technical development on a public dataset

records.title: Evaluation of deep convolutional neural networks for automatic classification of common maternal fetal ultrasound planes.
records.model_family: several state-of-the-art CNN classifiers compared
records.clinical_problem: labelling which anatomical plane a routine maternal-fetal screening ultrasound image shows
records.patient_population: 1,792 patients undergoing routine maternal-fetal screening ultrasound at two hospitals, imaged by several operators and machines
records.model_description: Classifies a screening ultrasound image into one of six categories (fetal abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix, other), and then subdivides brain images into the three standard brain planes. The point of the study is realism: the images come from two hospitals, several operators and several machines, and the models are benchmarked against the research technicians who do this task daily.
records.release_evidence: the dataset is stated to be made publicly available; nothing is said about the models
records.headline_result: computational models performed similarly to human operators on common plane classification; fine-grained brain-plane categorization remained harder

records.title: Achieving accurate estimates of fetal gestational age and personalised predictions of fetal growth based on data from an international prospective cohort study: a population-based machine learning study.
records.model_family: machine-learning regression on serial fetal biometry
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy accurately in the second and third trimesters, and forecasting how a given fetus will grow
records.patient_population: healthy, well-nourished participants in the multicentre INTERGROWTH-21st study, with generalization tested in the more heterogeneous INTERBIO-21st cohort
records.model_description: Estimates gestational age from ultrasound biometry measured across a ten-week window, and separately forecasts a specific fetus's growth trajectory six weeks ahead. The methodological move that makes it credible is the reference standard: accuracy is judged against the exactly known intervals between a woman's own scan visits rather than her recalled last menstrual period, which is itself unreliable. Generalization was checked in a different, more heterogeneous population.
records.headline_result: gestational age between 20 and 30 weeks estimated to within 3 days with 95% confidence, a prediction interval 3-5 times narrower than previous algorithms; 6-week growth forecasts accurate to within 7 days

records.title: Deep white matter analysis (DeepWMA): Fast and consistent tractography segmentation.
records.model_family: CNN classifier on a 2D multi-channel fiber descriptor (FiberMap)
records.clinical_problem: identifying named white matter tracts consistently enough to quantify them across very different subjects
records.patient_population: 597 diffusion MRI scans from six independently acquired populations spanning 1 day to 82 years, including neonates and patients with brain tumors
records.model_description: Sorts the individual streamlines of a whole-brain tractogram into 54 named deep white matter tracts by classifying each fiber from an encoding of its spatial trajectory. The claim that matters clinically is consistency across subjects who look nothing alike: it identified over 99% of tracts across all subjects, including day-old neonates and brains distorted by space-occupying tumors, where registration-based methods break down.
records.dataset_size: 1 million labeled fiber samples for training; 597 diffusion MRI scans for testing
records.headline_result: 90.99% fiber classification accuracy in training; over 99% of tracts successfully identified across all test subjects including neonates and tumor patients

records.title: Deep Predictive Motion Tracking in Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Application to Fetal Imaging.
records.model_family: recurrent neural network with spatial and temporal encoder-decoders, predicting motion parameters from sequences of acquired slices
records.clinical_problem: fetal motion during MRI, which today is handled by an operator watching slices go by and re-acquiring stacks - operator-dependent, expensive in scanner time, and hard for a pregnant woman to tolerate
records.patient_population: fetal MRI acquisitions, with held-out test sets including fetuses scanned at different ages and motion trajectories recorded from volunteers
records.model_description: Predicts where the fetus will be, not just where it was, which is what a system has to do if it is going to steer the next slice rather than fix the last one. The framing of the problem is unusually concrete about cost - scanner time, operator dependence, and the tolerability of a long scan for the mother - and the target is a navigation system rather than a better image. Prediction error is naturally larger than estimation error, and the paper reports both.
records.headline_result: real-time performance with average errors of 3.5 degrees for motion estimation and 8 degrees for prediction, outperforming alternative techniques

records.title: Deep learning-based synthetic CT generation for paediatric brain MR-only photon and proton radiotherapy.
records.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
records.model_family: three 2D conditional generative adversarial networks combined across orthogonal planes
records.clinical_problem: planning photon and proton radiotherapy from MRI alone, so a child does not need a separate planning CT
records.patient_population: 60 pediatric patients with brain tumors undergoing radiotherapy, deliberately imaged with heterogeneous MRI protocols
records.model_description: Generates a synthetic CT from a T1-weighted MRI so that radiotherapy dose can be calculated without acquiring a planning CT, sparing the child that dose. Three networks work on the three orthogonal planes and their median is combined; the spread between them doubles as an uncertainty map, which flags the body contour and air cavities as the places to distrust. Trained on deliberately heterogeneous protocols, which is what a real pediatric department has.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 61 ± 14 HU; dose difference -0.1 ± 0.3% (photon) and 0.1 ± 0.4% (proton) with gamma 2%/2mm pass rates of 99.5% and 99.2%

records.title: Deep learning-enabled MRI-only photon and proton therapy treatment planning for paediatric abdominal tumours.
records.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
records.model_family: U-Net-like network generating synthetic CT from T1- and T2-weighted MRI
records.clinical_problem: planning radiotherapy for a child from MRI alone, sparing the planning CT dose
records.patient_population: 66 children with Wilms tumour or neuroblastoma (mean age 4 years) who had MRI and CT on the same day
records.model_description: Converts MRI intensities to CT Hounsfield units so that radiotherapy dose can be computed without a planning CT. Dose distributions calculated on the synthetic CT matched those from the real CT to within half a percent on average for both volumetric-modulated arc therapy and pencil-beam proton scanning, with gamma pass rates above 96%. For a small child this removes a CT and, with it, a dose and often a separate anesthetic.
records.dataset_size: 66 children with paired same-day MRI and CT
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 57 ± 12 HU; average dose differences below 0.5% with gamma pass rates above 99% (photon) and 96% (proton)

records.title: Diagnosis of common pulmonary diseases in children by X-ray images and deep learning.
records.model_family: YOLOv3 lung field cropping followed by multi-class classification, comparing one-versus-one, one-versus-all and a single CNN classifier
records.clinical_problem: screening children's chest radiographs for the common lower respiratory problems - bronchiolitis or bronchitis, bronchopneumonia or interstitial pneumonitis, lobar pneumonia and pneumothorax - in settings where acute lower respiratory infection is the leading cause of child death
records.patient_population: chest radiographs of children with common pulmonary diseases
records.model_description: Deliberately broader than the single-disease pediatric models that preceded it: four disease categories plus normal, rather than pneumonia versus not. The honest conclusion in the abstract is the useful one - the scheme is strong at the normal-versus-abnormal decision and much weaker at telling the specific diseases apart, with per-class accuracies between 72% and 86%. That is the profile of a triage tool, and the authors say so.
records.headline_result: 92.47% accuracy for abnormal versus normal; per-class accuracy 71.94% bronchiolitis/bronchitis, 72.19% bronchopneumonia, 85.42% lobar pneumonia, 85.71% pneumothorax and 80.00% normal

records.title: Clinical application of artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis using anteroposterior pelvic radiographs in children with developmental dysplasia of the hip.
records.model_family: deep learning classification with acetabular index measurement
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip on a pelvic radiograph, where the normal anatomy changes so much with age that reading is genuinely hard
records.patient_population: 10,219 anteroposterior pelvic radiographs; the 1,138-patient test set had a mean age of 1.5 years and was 79% female
records.model_description: Classifies a pelvic radiograph as dislocated or not and measures the acetabular index, trained on over ten thousand radiographs labelled to a uniform standard. The size of the training set is what distinguishes it, and the reported agreement limits for acetabular index are wider in dislocated hips than normal ones, which is where measurement matters most.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.975 with sensitivity 95.5% and specificity 99.5% for hip dislocation; acetabular index agreement -3.27 to 2.94 degrees in non-dislocated and -7.36 to 5.36 degrees in dislocated hips

records.title: Image Segmentation of the Ventricular Septum in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Videos Based on Deep Learning Using Time-Series Information.
records.model_family: U-net with temporal and section-specific calibration
records.clinical_problem: delineating the ventricular septum during fetal cardiac screening, a small structure that changes shape with every heartbeat
records.patient_population: 615 annotated frames from 421 normal fetal cardiac ultrasound videos of 211 screened pregnant women
records.model_description: General-purpose segmentation networks fail badly on the fetal ventricular septum: DeepLab v3+ scored a mean intersection over union of 0.02 and U-net 0.15 on this task. This method crops to the relevant region, segments, then calibrates the output using the video's time-series information and the known section, reaching 0.55. The gap between those numbers is the honest measure of how hard small moving fetal structures are.
records.dataset_size: 615 annotated frames from 421 videos of 211 women
records.headline_result: mean intersection over union 0.554 versus 0.152 for U-net and 0.022 for DeepLab v3+

records.title: Training confounder-free deep learning models for medical applications.
records.model_family: end-to-end confounder-invariant feature learning (adversarial fair-learning scheme)
records.clinical_problem: stopping a model from learning a confounder instead of the disease, demonstrated partly on bone age from children's hand radiographs
records.patient_population: adolescents in the NCANDA alcohol and neurodevelopment cohort, children undergoing hand radiography, and adults with HIV
records.model_description: A training method rather than a clinical model: it forces the learned features to be statistically independent of a named confounder (age, sex, scanner) while still predicting the outcome, borrowing from fair machine learning. Demonstrated on three tasks including bone age from pediatric hand radiographs and sex differences in adolescent brain MRI. Directly relevant to any children's hospital worried that a model has learned the scanner or the referring pathway rather than the disease.
records.release_evidence: the code is available at https://github.com/qingyuzhao/br-net
records.headline_result: accurate prediction with reduced confounder-associated bias across all three tasks; figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: Fully‑automated deep‑learning segmentation of pediatric cardiovascular magnetic resonance of patients with complex congenital heart diseases.
records.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

records.patient_population: pediatric subjects with complex congenital heart disease
records.model_description: Addresses the defining constraint of pediatric AI head on: there is not enough annotated pediatric cardiac MRI, and certainly not in complex congenital disease, so a generative network synthesizes additional images with matching chamber labels to enlarge the training set. The resulting segmentation network is benchmarked against U-Net and against cvi42, the software actually used in clinics. The authors made the pediatric congenital dataset public, which is rarer still.
records.release_evidence: the pediatric congenital heart disease dataset was made publicly available
records.dataset_size: a cohort of pediatric subjects with complex congenital heart disease
records.headline_result: outperformed U-Net and the clinically used cvi42 software on Dice, Jaccard, Hausdorff distance and clinical volumetric indices

records.title: Automated quantification of baseline imaging PET metrics on FDG PET/CT images of pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma patients.

The per-feature agreement is the useful part of the results - SUVmax and total lesion glycolysis are essentially solved, volume is slightly underestimated, and the disease-spread metric is not yet reliable.

records.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence

records.title: Mapping the asynchrony of cortical maturation in the infant brain: A MRI multi-parametric clustering approach.
records.exclusion_reason: multi-parametric clustering to describe normal cortical maturation in healthy infants; a developmental neuroscience description rather than a diagnostic model

records.title: Deep Generative Adversarial Neural Networks for Compressive Sensing MRI.
records.model_family: least-squares GAN with a deep residual generator
records.clinical_problem: shortening contrast-enhanced MRI in children by reconstructing undersampled data
records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing contrast-enhanced abdominal MRI
records.model_description: Takes an aliased image from undersampled k-space and returns a diagnostic-quality reconstruction in milliseconds. A generative adversarial network learns what real high-quality MR images look like, so the output keeps fine texture instead of the waxy appearance that pixel-wise losses produce. Trained and evaluated on a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MRI dataset with expert radiologist ratings.
records.dataset_size: a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MR dataset; size not stated
records.headline_result: expert radiologists rated it higher in fine texture detail than wavelet, dictionary-learning and pixel-wise deep learning reconstructions, at two orders of magnitude faster reconstruction

records.title: Towards Automated Semantic Segmentation in Prenatal Volumetric Ultrasound.
records.model_family: 3D fully convolutional network with a multi-directional recurrent refinement network
records.clinical_problem: getting reliable biometry out of 3D prenatal ultrasound, which is hard to interpret and therefore little used
records.patient_population: pregnant women undergoing volumetric prenatal ultrasound
records.model_description: Segments the fetus, gestational sac and placenta simultaneously in a 3D ultrasound volume. A convolutional network makes the initial dense labeling and a recurrent network sweeping in several directions fixes the boundaries, which is where ultrasound segmentation usually fails because contrast is poor and edges are ambiguous. The measurements agreed with experts and were reproducible across scanning variation.
records.dataset_size: large in-house datasets; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: superior segmentation performance with decent agreement with expert measurements and high reproducibility against scanning variation

records.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation of bone age radiographs improves accuracy and decreases variability.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network
records.clinical_problem: whether AI assistance makes pediatric radiologists better at bone age, not whether AI alone beats them
records.patient_population: 280 age- and sex-matched bone age radiographs from children aged 5 to 18
records.model_description: The model itself is a bone age network the group had already published; the contribution here is the comparison design. Six subspecialty pediatric radiologists read the same 280 cases, then three read them again with the model's estimate in front of them. Every reader improved, and inter-reader variability fell. The conclusion — AI plus radiologist beats either alone — is the argument for deploying these tools as an adjunct rather than a replacement.
records.headline_result: AI alone 68.2% accurate versus 63.6% for the six-reader mean; pooled root mean squared error fell from 0.661 to 0.508 years with AI assistance, and every individual reader improved

records.title: Real-Time Deep Pose Estimation With Geodesic Loss for Image-to-Template Rigid Registration.
records.model_family: regression CNN predicting angle-axis rotation and translation, trained with geodesic loss
records.clinical_problem: aligning fetal brain images acquired in arbitrary orientations to a standard atlas, the step that motion-robust reconstruction depends on
records.patient_population: fetuses scanned in utero across a wide gestational age range, with generalization tested on newborns
records.model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented fetal brain sits in a canonical space directly from the image, in under 100 milliseconds, replacing an iterative optimization that has a narrow capture range. Trained on T2-weighted fetal scans, it generalized to T1-weighted newborn scans once image contrast was transferred with a conditional GAN, which is a useful demonstration that a model can be moved across contrasts without retraining from scratch.
records.headline_result: 3D pose estimation with a wide capture range in under 100 ms, generalizing to newborn scans of a different contrast

records.title: Remapping the cognitive and neural profiles of children who struggle at school.
records.exclusion_reason: unsupervised clustering of cognitive assessment scores in struggling learners; MRI is used to describe the resulting groups, not as model input

records.title: Fetal brain growth portrayed by a spatiotemporal diffusion tensor MRI atlas computed from in utero images.
records.model_family: kernel regression in age with diffeomorphic tensor-to-tensor registration
records.clinical_problem: having a normative reference for fetal white matter development against which an individual fetus can be compared
records.patient_population: 67 healthy fetuses scanned once each between 21 and 39 weeks gestational age
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model but the normative resource one needs before building any: the first diffusion tensor atlas of the fetal brain built from in utero images, computed by regressing motion-corrected individual tensors against gestational age. It makes group studies and computer-aided diagnosis from fetal diffusion imaging possible, which the authors note had not previously been feasible because individual in utero reconstructions are too noisy.
records.headline_result: the atlas reproduced the known sequence of limbic, projection and association fiber development between 21 and 39 weeks

records.title: Structural and functional neuroimaging in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
records.exclusion_reason: review of structural and functional imaging findings in ADHD; states explicitly that no neural biomarker exists for diagnosis and builds no model

records.title: Regression Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Pediatric Bone Age Assessment From Hand Radiograph.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: regression CNN with an attention module and dynamic attention loss
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
records.patient_population: children in two large hand radiograph datasets
records.model_description: Regresses bone age directly from the radiograph, with an attention module that first learns where the growth-relevant regions are and a loss that weights the hard cases more heavily during training. The attention idea addresses the specific failure mode of bone age networks, which is that most of the image is irrelevant and the informative epiphyses are small.
records.dataset_size: two large datasets; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: average discrepancy of 5.2-5.3 months between clinical and automatic bone age on two large datasets

records.title: Curved planar reformatting and convolutional neural network-based segmentation of the small bowel for visualization and quantitative assessment of pediatric Crohn's disease from MRI.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.model_family: convolutional neural network segmentation of lumen, wall and background, combined with curved planar reformatting
records.clinical_problem: seeing and quantifying disease burden in pediatric Crohn disease on contrast-enhanced small bowel MRI, where following the bowel means scrolling back and forth through a 3D volume
records.patient_population: 23 pediatric patients with Crohn disease imaged at 1.5 T with a T1-weighted postcontrast VIBE sequence
records.model_description: The segmentation is a means, not the end. Curved planar reformatting straightens the bowel so its whole length is visible at once, and the CNN supplies the lumen and wall boundaries that reformatting needs - together turning a scroll-through into a set of markers. The markers are then tested for what a radiologist would want: whether they separate active from inactive segments and stricturing from non-stricturing, and whether they reproduce. Wall segmentation is more reliable than lumen.
records.headline_result: Dice 75 +/- 18% lumen, 81 +/- 8% wall, 97 +/- 2% background; wall thickness at minimum radius (P = 0.0013) and median relative contrast enhancement (P = 0.0033) separated active from non-active segments

records.title: Artificial intelligence and amniotic fluid multiomics: prediction of perinatal outcome in asymptomatic women with short cervix.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.exclusion_reason: prediction of perinatal outcome from amniotic fluid metabolomics and proteomics; sonographic cervical length is one covariate rather than the imaging input

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on ultrasound imaging data by integrating texture image features and deep transfer learning image features.
records.model_family: support vector machine on transfer-learned deep features combined with conventional texture features
records.clinical_problem: identifying congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract on the ultrasound children already receive
records.patient_population: 50 children with congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract and 50 controls, imaged during routine care
records.model_description: Combines features learned by a pretrained network with hand-computed texture features and shows the combination beats either alone, which is the useful methodological finding on a 100-child dataset where a deep model alone would overfit. Uses images from routine clinical care rather than a curated research acquisition.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.92, 0.88 and 0.92 for left, right and bilateral abnormal kidney scans, significantly better than either feature set alone (p < 0.001)

records.title: Comparative effectiveness of convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for radiology text report classification.
records.model_family: CNN with GloVe embeddings, and a domain-phrase attention hierarchical recurrent network
records.clinical_problem: extracting whether a CT report says there is a pulmonary embolus, at scale and across institutions
records.patient_population: adult and pediatric patients whose thoracic CT reports were collected from four healthcare centers
records.model_description: Reads a free-text thoracic CT report and decides whether it describes a pulmonary embolus. The recurrent model builds up word, sentence and document representations and weights domain-specific phrases through an attention mechanism. The finding that matters for a children's hospital is the transfer: models trained on adult reports classified pediatric reports at the same F1 of 0.99, which is not what happens with image models.
records.dataset_size: over 7,370 thoracic CT reports from four centers
records.headline_result: F1 0.99 for pulmonary embolus in adults and 0.99 in the pediatric population, beating the rule-based PEFinder on multi-institutional test sets

records.title: The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge.
records.model_family: convolutional neural networks (105 submitted entries)
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment
records.patient_population: children whose hand radiographs make up a curated 14,236-image challenge dataset
records.model_description: Not one model but a public competition: RSNA released a curated set of 14,236 pediatric hand radiographs with reference bone ages and invited teams to submit algorithms, scored on mean absolute distance in months. Almost every entry used convolutional neural networks. The paper reports what a coordinated community effort achieved and is the reference point later bone-age papers compare against.
records.release_evidence: the data set was made available to registered challenge participants; the abstract says nothing about releasing the models
records.headline_result: best five entries achieved mean absolute distance of 4.2 to 4.5 months

records.title: Using an artificial neural network to predict traumatic brain injury.
records.model_family: artificial neural network over radiologist-interpreted CT findings
records.clinical_problem: ruling in clinically relevant traumatic brain injury in children so that the rest can be discharged on an evidence-based basis rather than admitted for observation
records.patient_population: 12 902 children from the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network traumatic brain injury dataset
records.model_description: Built on PECARN, the dataset that produced the clinical decision rule pediatric emergency medicine already uses, and aimed at the same decision - who can safely go home. The inputs are the radiologist's CT findings rather than the pixels, so this is decision support layered on the report rather than image analysis. Sensitivity above 99% is the operating point the problem demands, since the cost of a missed clinically relevant injury is not symmetric with the cost of an observation stay.
records.headline_result: prediction of clinically relevant traumatic brain injury with greater than 99% sensitivity and AUC 0.99
records.study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multi-center cohort

records.title: Functional connectivity changes associated with fMRI neurofeedback of right inferior frontal cortex in adolescents with ADHD.
records.exclusion_reason: real-time fMRI neurofeedback as a treatment in adolescents with ADHD; an intervention study, not an AI model

records.title: Automated Fetal Head Detection and Circumference Estimation from Free-Hand Ultrasound Sweeps Using Deep Learning in Resource-Limited Countries.
records.model_family: VGG-inspired detection network followed by a U-net measurement network
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age where there is no sonographer, using a sweep protocol any health worker can learn in a day
records.patient_population: 183 pregnant women at St. Luke's Hospital, Wolisso, Ethiopia
records.model_description: Works from sweeps acquired with a fixed protocol that requires no knowledge of ultrasound, and which will usually not contain the standard plane at all. One network finds the frames containing the fetal head, a second measures head circumference in those frames, and gestational age follows from the Hadlock curve. Validated against standard-plane measurements taken by an experienced sonographer on the same women.
records.headline_result: most automatically estimated gestational ages fell within the 2.5th to 97.5th centile interval of the Hadlock curve relative to reference measurements

records.title: Protocol for a transdiagnostic study of children with problems of attention, learning and memory (CALM).
records.exclusion_reason: study protocol for a transdiagnostic cohort of struggling learners; machine learning is planned rather than performed and MRI is optional

records.title: Unbiased age-specific structural brain atlases for Chinese pediatric population.
records.model_family: unbiased template construction algorithm
records.clinical_problem: whether a pediatric brain atlas built on one population is valid for children of another
records.patient_population: 328 cognitively normal Chinese children aged 6-12, with two independent validation datasets of 114 and 71 children
records.model_description: A set of age-specific brain templates built from Chinese children, made because the widely used NIH pediatric atlases are derived from Caucasian children. The comparison found substantial anatomical differences in frontal and parietal regions, and using the matched atlas gave significantly better tissue segmentation and brain-age prediction in Chinese children. It is a concrete demonstration that population mismatch in a reference dataset degrades downstream results.
records.release_evidence: released on the NITRC website at https://www.nitrc.org/projects/chn-pd
records.dataset_size: 328 children for atlas construction; 185 children across two validation datasets
records.headline_result: significantly higher accuracy than the NIH pediatric atlases for both brain-age prediction and tissue segmentation in Chinese children

records.title: Transient states of network connectivity are atypical in autism: A dynamic functional connectivity study.
records.exclusion_reason: group comparison of dynamic functional connectivity states in autism; clustering is used descriptively and no predictive model is built

records.title: A review on lung boundary detection in chest X-rays.
records.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
records.clinical_problem: isolating the lungs on a chest radiograph, the step every downstream chest analysis depends on
records.patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed studies, with particular attention to pediatric and deformed-lung cases
records.model_description: A review of lung segmentation on chest radiographs from 2006 to 2017, classifying methods into rule-based, pixel-classification, model-based, hybrid and deep-learning families. Its finding for a children's hospital is a gap: almost all published algorithms are validated on adult posteroanterior films of healthy-looking lungs, while pediatric films are noisier, obstructed by whoever is holding the child, and anatomically different by developmental stage.
records.headline_result: hybrid and deep-learning methods reached inter-observer-level segmentation performance, at the cost of long training and high computational complexity

records.title: Prenatal lead exposure impacts cross-hemispheric and long-range connectivity in the human fetal brain.
records.exclusion_reason: association between prenatal lead exposure and fetal functional connectivity; no machine-learning model

records.title: Sensory over-responsivity: parent report, direct assessment measures, and neural architecture.
records.exclusion_reason: group comparison of white matter anisotropy by sensory over-responsivity phenotype; no machine-learning model

records.title: Evaluation of an improved tool for non-invasive prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity based on fully automated fetal lung ultrasound analysis.
records.model_family: deep learning lung delineation feeding quantitative texture analysis
records.clinical_problem: predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity from ultrasound instead of amniocentesis
records.patient_population: 790 fetal lung ultrasound images obtained between 24 and 39 weeks gestation
records.model_description: The successor version of the commercial fetal lung maturity tool, with the manual lung outlining replaced by deep learning. The comparison that makes the paper worth reading is three-way: fully automated, the same texture analysis with manual delineation, and gestational age alone. Automation cost essentially nothing in accuracy (91.5% versus 90.3%) while both beat gestational age alone (75.6%) decisively.
records.release_evidence: quantusFLM version 3.0, a commercial software tool
records.headline_result: sensitivity 71.0%, specificity 94.7%, accuracy 91.5% fully automated, against 90.3% with manual delineation and 75.6% using gestational age alone

records.title: Evaluating reinforcement learning agents for anatomical landmark detection.
records.model_family: deep Q-network reinforcement learning agents with multi-scale hierarchical search
records.body_region: fetal head, adult brain and heart
records.clinical_problem: finding anatomical landmarks automatically, the step that biometry and registration depend on
records.patient_population: fetuses in a fetal head ultrasound dataset, alongside adult brain and cardiac MRI datasets
records.model_description: Rather than scanning the whole image, an agent starts somewhere and learns to walk toward the landmark, treating the 3D scan as an environment to navigate. Searching coarse-to-fine with hierarchical step sizes speeds this up four- to fivefold and copes with the large fields of view and noisy backgrounds where fixed-scale agents fail. Evaluated on fetal head ultrasound among three datasets.
records.dataset_size: three medical imaging datasets; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: surpassed state-of-the-art supervised and reinforcement-learning landmark methods; hierarchical steps sped up search 4-5 times

records.title: Amygdala-prefrontal cortex white matter tracts are widespread, variable and implicated in amygdala modulation in adolescents.
records.exclusion_reason: developmental neuroscience: probabilistic tractography maps amygdala-prefrontal tracts in 142 adolescents and a machine-learning regression relates that connectivity to amygdala reactivity; no diagnostic or clinical imaging model

records.title: Attention gated networks: Learning to leverage salient regions in medical images.
records.model_family: attention-gated CNN module for VGG / U-Net
records.clinical_problem: identifying the correct standard views during fetal ultrasound screening
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing mid-pregnancy screening ultrasound; the segmentation experiments use adult abdominal CT
records.model_description: A drop-in module that makes a standard CNN learn where to look, suppressing irrelevant image regions without a separate organ-localization step. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, where it reduced false positives, and on multi-organ abdominal CT segmentation. It is a general architecture contribution rather than a clinical product.
records.release_evidence: the source code for the proposed AG models is publicly available
records.dataset_size: two large 3D CT abdominal datasets plus a fetal ultrasound screening set; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: consistent improvement in prediction performance over the base architectures across datasets and training sizes

records.title: Improving preterm newborn identification in low-resource settings with machine learning.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning identifies preterm newborns from maternal and newborn clinical characteristics in a low-resource setting; early pregnancy ultrasound is the gold standard the model is scored against, not an input, and no images are analyzed

records.title: White matter connectomes at birth accurately predict cognitive abilities at age 2.
records.model_family: deep learning classifier on white matter connectomes
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive ability at age 2 from the brain's wiring at birth
records.patient_population: 75 full-term infants scanned at birth and 37 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
records.model_description: Builds a white matter connectome from diffusion MRI acquired at birth and classifies whether that child will score above or below the median on cognitive testing at two years, then predicts the individual score. Trained on full-term infants and evaluated separately on preterm infants, which is the transfer that matters clinically. Frontal lobe connections and their links to the rest of the brain carried the classification.
records.headline_result: 89.5% accuracy in full-term and 83.8% in preterm infants for the 2-year cognitive group; predicted and actual scores correlated at r = 0.98 and 0.96

records.title: Decision Fusion-Based Fetal Ultrasound Image Plane Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: two fine-tuned convolutional feature extractors - one on the whole image, one on discriminant cropped regions - whose classification decisions are fused
records.clinical_problem: labeling which fetal structure a 2D ultrasound image shows, across 14 structures, so that large retrospective archives can be mined for indicators of abnormal development
records.patient_population: 4074 2-D fetal ultrasound images (3109 training, 965 test)
records.model_description: The diagnosis of the problem is precise: crops confuse structures that look alike, such as kidney and abdomen, while the whole image lacks the local detail to say which structure is where. Fusing decisions from both, without a prior on where to look, is the contribution, and localization falls out of the same machinery. The high mean accuracy alongside much lower precision and recall reflects 14 unbalanced classes. Its stated purpose is retrospective archive mining rather than live scanning.
records.headline_result: mean accuracy 97.05%, precision 76.47%, recall 75.41%, Cohen kappa 0.72; 92% mean accuracy on images without scanner overlays

records.title: Objective Detection of Eloquent Axonal Pathways to Minimize Postoperative Deficits in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery using Diffusion Tractography and Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: deep CNN on diffusion tractography streamlines with focal and center losses and a soft attention mechanism
records.clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter pathways before pediatric epilepsy surgery, so that resection spares motor, language, auditory and visual function
records.patient_population: streamlines from 70 healthy children and 70 children with focal epilepsy, labeled by functional MRI and electrical stimulation mapping
records.model_description: Aimed at the specific inadequacy of the current tools: electrical stimulation mapping is invasive and maps cortex, fMRI needs task cooperation from a child, and neither shows the fibers connecting eloquent areas. The network classifies individual tractography streamlines, with focal and center losses chosen for an extremely unbalanced label distribution and soft attention for interpretability. Ground truth comes from the invasive standard it would reduce.
records.release_evidence: the abstract states the implementation will be released at a GitHub repository
records.headline_result: 73-100% accuracy for objective detection of functionally important pathways, outperforming existing streamline classification models

records.title: Intrinsic Functional Brain Connectivity Predicts Onset of Major Depression Disorder in Adolescence: A Pilot Study.
records.model_family: classifier built on resting-state functional connectivity features
records.clinical_problem: identifying, before any episode occurs, which children at familial risk for major depression will develop it in adolescence
records.patient_population: never-depressed children aged 8-14 with familial risk for major depressive disorder and age-matched controls without familial risk, reassessed by diagnostic interview 3-4 years later
records.model_description: A prognostic rather than diagnostic model, and the design carries the weight: imaging at baseline in children who had never been depressed, diagnosis established 3-4 years later, and the classifier built independently of the group differences the paper also reports. Its comparator is the right one - baseline clinical rating scales - and connectivity beat them. A pilot, with the sample size that word implies.
records.dataset_size: pilot cohort, size not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: classification of converters versus non-converters from baseline connectivity reached high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, superior to classification from baseline clinical rating scales

records.title: A radiomics-based nomogram for the preoperative prediction of posthepatectomy liver failure in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.exclusion_reason: CT radiomics nomogram for post-hepatectomy liver failure in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma

records.title: Fully automated radiological analysis of spinal disorders and deformities: a deep learning approach.
records.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
records.model_family: fully convolutional network with a differentiable spatial-to-numerical layer
records.clinical_problem: measuring spinal deformity parameters (Cobb angle, kyphosis, lordosis, pelvic incidence) on biplanar radiographs
records.patient_population: 493 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, adult deformity and spinal stenosis
records.model_description: Takes biplanar spine radiographs and returns the 78 anatomical landmarks (endplate centers, hip joint centers, S1 endplate margins) from which the standard deformity angles are then computed. It is designed to cope with a wide range of conditions and fields of view. The authors are candid that although the predicted spine shape looks convincing and correlates strongly with ground truth, the standard errors on individual angles are large.
records.dataset_size: 493 spines for training, 50 patients for quantitative comparison
records.headline_result: all parameters strongly correlated with ground truth, but standard errors from 2.7 degrees (pelvic tilt) to 11.5 degrees (L1-L5 lordosis)

records.title: Techniques for minimizing sedation in pediatric MRI.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.clinical_problem: avoiding sedation and general anesthesia for MRI in infants and young children
records.patient_population: infants and young children undergoing MRI
records.model_description: A review of every lever available for getting a diagnostic MRI in a small child awake: environment, child life specialists, feed-and-bundle, distraction, noise reduction, and the technical routes to shorter scans, of which artificial intelligence is one. Useful as the framing document for why faster reconstruction matters in a children's hospital, rather than as a source of model performance figures.

records.title: Resting-state neural network disturbances that underpin the emergence of emotional symptoms in adolescent girls: resting-state fMRI study.
records.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
records.exclusion_reason: longitudinal resting-state fMRI study of dynamic functional network connectivity in 88 adolescent girls, correlated with later emotional symptoms; group comparison and correlation, no machine learning model

records.title: Sex differences in functional connectivity during fetal brain development.
records.exclusion_reason: descriptive study of sex differences in normal fetal functional connectivity; no model is trained and no clinical question is asked

records.title: Machine learning concepts, concerns and opportunities for a pediatric radiologist.
records.exclusion_reason: educational review of machine learning concepts and implementation challenges written for pediatric radiologists; no model developed or evaluated

records.title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Based on Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: convolutional neural networks with transfer learning and classifier combination, both mixture-of-experts and simple Bayes
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children from resting-state functional MRI, before behavioral symptoms are established enough for interview and observation to settle it
records.patient_population: children aged 5 to 10 years from the ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets
records.model_description: Two constraints are handled at once: small medical datasets and the need to hold the age window narrow. The age restriction to 5-10 years is a deliberate cost - it shrinks an already small dataset - taken because a diagnostic aid is only useful before the clinical diagnosis is obvious. Combining classifiers and transferring features stand in for the data that does not exist. Accuracy in the low-to-mid 70s is representative of what ABIDE supports, and is a reminder of how far this is from clinical use.
records.dataset_size: ABIDE I and ABIDE II subjects aged 5-10
records.headline_result: ABIDE I accuracy 0.7273, sensitivity 0.712, specificity 0.7348; ABIDE II accuracy 0.700, sensitivity 0.582, specificity 0.804
records.study_design: retrospective model development on public datasets

records.title: Childhood Trauma in Schizophrenia: Current Findings and Research Perspectives.
records.exclusion_reason: review of childhood trauma in schizophrenia; imaging findings are described but no AI model is involved

records.title: Artificial intelligence and the analysis of multi-platform metabolomics data for the detection of intrauterine growth restriction.
records.exclusion_reason: prediction of intrauterine growth restriction from cord blood metabolomics; no imaging

records.title: Toward Automated 3D Spine Reconstruction from Biplanar Radiographs Using CNN for Statistical Spine Model Fitting.
records.model_family: CNN landmark detection driving a statistical shape model
records.clinical_problem: getting 3D spinal measurements from biplanar radiographs, which currently needs so much manual supervision that it stays out of routine practice
records.patient_population: 68 biplanar radiographs of asymptomatic subjects and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
records.model_description: Fits a realistic statistical shape model of the spine to a pair of biplanar radiographs by having networks find the controlling anatomical landmarks, iteratively and coarse-to-fine. Reconstruction takes under a minute against the semi-automated methods it replaces, and 89% of its measurements fell inside the experts' own confidence intervals. The stated aim is dissemination: 3D measurement exists but nobody has time to do it by hand.
records.headline_result: landmark errors 1.6-2.3 mm; absolute error 2.8-4.7 degrees for spinal and 1-2.1 degrees for pelvic parameters; 89% of measurements inside expert confidence intervals
records.study_design: retrospective validation against multi-expert ground truth

records.title: Abdominal ultrasound should become part of standard care for early diagnosis and management of necrotising enterocolitis: a narrative review.
records.journal: Archives of disease in childhood. Fetal and neonatal edition
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review arguing abdominal ultrasound should be standard care in necrotising enterocolitis; computer-aided detection and AI are named only as a future amplifier, no model

records.title: The Protective Effects of Supportive Parenting on the Relationship Between Adolescent Poverty and Resting-State Functional Brain Connectivity During Adulthood.
records.exclusion_reason: resting-state connectivity in 25-year-olds against adolescent poverty history; the imaging is of adults and there is no model

records.title: Automatic evaluation of fetal head biometry from ultrasound images using machine learning.
records.model_family: deep learning pipeline with a plane acceptance check followed by head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation
records.clinical_problem: automating head circumference and biparietal diameter on fetal ultrasound, the biometry used to assign gestational age and flag central nervous system pathology
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images: 102 labeled for training, 70 for validation
records.model_description: Biometry with a gatekeeper. The pipeline first decides whether the plane is acceptable and only then measures, which is the right ordering for a measurement that is meaningless off-plane and the part most automated biometry skips. Small dataset, and the reported success rates are plane-level rather than millimetre agreement, so it reads as feasibility.
records.headline_result: 91.43% success for head circumference and 100% for biparietal diameter, with 87.14% accuracy on the plane acceptance check

records.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Liver Stiffness Using Clinical and T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic Data.
records.model_family: support vector machine on clinical plus T2-weighted radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: estimating liver stiffness without MR elastography, which not every center has
records.patient_population: 225 children and young adults (mean age 14.1 years) internally and 84 (mean age 13.7) in an external cohort, with known or suspected liver disease
records.model_description: Classifies liver stiffness above or below 3 kPa from routine T2-weighted images plus clinical data, using elastography as the reference. The point is substitution: if ordinary sequences carry enough signal, centers without elastography could still stratify fibrosis risk. Clinical and radiomic features together beat either alone, and the model held up in an independent external cohort with a modest drop.
records.headline_result: internal AUC 0.84 combining clinical and radiomic features (0.77 clinical, 0.70 radiomic alone); external AUC 0.80 with accuracy 75.0%

records.title: Cortical abnormalities in youth at clinical high-risk for psychosis: Findings from the NAPLS2 cohort.
records.exclusion_reason: cortical morphometry group comparison in clinical high-risk youth; the machine-learning brain-age model it refers to is from a prior report and no model is developed here

records.title: The Future of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography: Advanced Analytics and Clinical Insights.
records.exclusion_reason: review of the future of cardiovascular CT; AI and radiomics are one of several forward-looking sections and no pediatric model is evaluated

records.title: Automatic brain tissue segmentation in fetal MRI using convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: two sequential CNNs with synthetic intensity-inhomogeneity augmentation
records.clinical_problem: volumetric and morphologic assessment of the fetal brain, which requires tissue-level segmentation
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing MRI
records.model_description: One network extracts the intracranial volume, a second divides it into seven tissue classes: cerebellum, basal ganglia and thalami, ventricular CSF, white matter, brain stem, cortical gray matter and extracerebral CSF.
