The trick is in the training: rather than correcting the intensity inhomogeneity that fetal motion causes, artificial gradients are added to clean slices so the network learns to tolerate the artifact, which removes a preprocessing step entirely.
records.headline_result: average Dice rose from 0.77 to 0.88 and mean surface distance fell from 0.78 mm to 0.37 mm when training data included simulated inhomogeneity

records.title: Role of deep learning in infant brain MRI analysis.
records.exclusion_reason: review comparing existing deep learning methods for infant brain tissue segmentation and presymptomatic disease prediction; surveys and discusses open issues rather than developing a model

records.title: Association of Prepubertal and Postpubertal Exposure to Childhood Maltreatment With Adult Amygdala Function.
records.exclusion_reason: functional MRI in young adults (mean age 23 years); childhood refers to retrospectively reported maltreatment, not the age at imaging

records.title: Bone age assessment with various machine learning techniques: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
records.clinical_problem: the state of machine learning for bone age assessment
records.patient_population: children and subadults in the 26 studies reviewed, mostly from the United States and Western Europe
records.model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 bone age studies using machine learning. Its value is in the gaps it names: the field works almost entirely on hand and wrist radiographs and has barely explored radiation-free alternatives such as MRI, few studies address ethnic differences, the samples cluster around the medico-legal age of 18, and socioeconomic influences on skeletal maturation are untouched.

records.title: Self-supervised learning for medical image analysis using image context restoration.
records.model_family: self-supervised pretraining by context restoration
records.clinical_problem: getting usable models when few images are labelled, demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with 2D ultrasound; further experiments use abdominal CT and brain tumor MRI
records.model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model: patches of an unlabelled image are swapped and the network learns to restore the original, which teaches it semantic features without any annotation. The pretrained weights are then fine-tuned for a downstream task. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, abdominal organ localization on CT and brain tumor segmentation on MRI.
records.headline_result: improved models in all three downstream tasks; magnitudes not stated in the abstract

records.title: Computed tomography-based predictive nomogram for differentiating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children.
records.model_family: LASSO-selected radiomic signatures from two anatomical regions, combined with a clinical factor in a predictive nomogram
records.clinical_problem: separating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children on chest CT, a distinction that changes treatment entirely and that experienced radiologists get wrong often enough to matter
records.patient_population: 53 children with clinically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis and 62 with community-acquired pneumonia, split 3:1 into primary (n=86) and validation (n=29) cohorts
records.model_description: Two separate radiomic signatures rather than one, extracted from the consolidation and from the lymph nodes, which mirrors how the two diseases actually differ and lets the model use nodal texture that no visual score captures. Duration of fever is the only clinical variable added. The comparator that gives the result its weight is a senior radiologist reading the same scans, who scored 0.79 against the nomogram's 0.97 - though on 29 validation patients.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.971 (95% CI 0.912-1) versus 0.791 for a senior radiologist's clinical judgment and 0.832 for the clinical factor alone

records.title: Automated age estimation from MRI volumes of the hand.
records.model_family: random forests and deep convolutional neural networks on 3D hand MRI, with several image-input simplifications compared
records.clinical_problem: estimating age in children and adolescents without ionizing radiation, for both clinical and forensic use
records.patient_population: 328 hand MR images of children and adolescents; the best method was then adapted to 2D and applied to a public hand radiograph dataset
records.model_description: The MRI answer to bone age. Three problems with radiographic staging are addressed at once - radiation, the absence of MRI-specific staging systems, and examiner subjectivity - by regressing age directly from 3D volumes and skipping staging entirely. The paper is unusually careful about what is being estimated, separating biological age estimation from chronological age approximation, and it validates by porting the method to 2D radiographs where it matches published automatic methods.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.37 +/- 0.51 years for biological age in subjects 18 or younger
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation

records.title: Altered Functional Connectivity in Children With Low-Function Autism Spectrum Disorders.
records.exclusion_reason: group comparison of independent-component functional networks in children with autism; descriptive rather than predictive, with no model

records.title: Experience during adolescence shapes brain development: From synapses and networks to normal and pathological behavior.
records.exclusion_reason: symposium review of experience-dependent plasticity in adolescence; no machine-learning model

records.title: Multi-task learning for quality assessment of fetal head ultrasound images.
records.model_family: multi-task faster region-based CNN with shared convolutional trunk
records.clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal head ultrasound image is good enough to measure from, before anyone measures from it
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
records.model_description: Detects the key anatomical structures of the fetal head, checks whether the image magnification is appropriate, and scores the plane against clinical protocol, all from one network with a shared feature trunk and task-specific heads. It returns a verdict in under half a second, which is fast enough to be useful during the scan rather than after it. Prior clinical rules are folded in to hold down false detections.
records.dataset_size: an institutional dataset; size not stated
records.headline_result: quality assessment of an ultrasound plane in under half a second, comparable with state-of-the-art methods

records.title: Fetal Brain Abnormality Classification from MRI Images of Different Gestational Age.
records.model_family: classical classifiers - diagonal quadratic discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbour, random forest, naive Bayes and RBF networks - plus bagging and AdaBoost ensembles of them
records.clinical_problem: classifying fetal brain abnormalities on MRI before birth, across a wide span of gestational ages rather than at one fixed age
records.patient_population: fetuses of widespread gestational ages imaged with brain MRI
records.model_description: Pre-deep-learning in method but pointed in framing: most work on early brain abnormality classification had been done on newborns and premature infants, and this pushes the same question back before birth and across gestational ages rather than at a single one. Handcrafted features with a bank of classical classifiers and ensembles compared against their base models; k-nearest neighbour won.
records.headline_result: highest accuracy and AUC around 95% using the k-nearest neighbour classifier

records.title: Diagnosis and classification of pediatric acute appendicitis by artificial intelligence methods: An investigator-independent approach.
records.model_family: machine-learning classifier on a routine biomarker signature
records.clinical_problem: deciding whether a child with abdominal pain has appendicitis, and whether it is complicated
records.patient_population: 590 children and adolescents aged 0-17 with suspected appendicitis at a Berlin hospital (473 histologically confirmed, 117 negative)
records.model_description: Combines the appendiceal diameter measured on ultrasound with the full blood count and C-reactive protein, all of which are obtained routinely anyway, and returns a diagnosis of appendicitis. The framing is investigator-independent: no expert interpretation is needed. Discrimination of appendicitis from no appendicitis is good; separating complicated from uncomplicated inflammation, the decision that would actually change management toward antibiotics, is not.
records.dataset_size: 590 patients, with at most 35% used for discovery and training
records.headline_result: 90% accuracy for appendicitis (93% sensitivity, 67% specificity); only 51% accuracy for identifying complicated inflammation

records.title: Development of a Plasma Screening Panel for Pediatric Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Using Metabolomics.
records.exclusion_reason: plasma metabolomics screening panel for pediatric fatty liver disease; imaging is part of the reference standard, not the model input

records.title: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation with test-time augmentation for medical image segmentation with convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: test-time augmentation for CNN segmentation uncertainty
records.clinical_problem: knowing when to distrust an automated fetal brain segmentation
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; brain tumor MRI is used as a second test case
records.model_description: A way of putting an uncertainty estimate on a segmentation: the same image is transformed several ways at test time and the spread of the resulting segmentations is treated as image-based uncertainty, formalized as Monte Carlo sampling over an image acquisition model. Applied to fetal brain and brain tumor MRI, it flags overconfident wrong predictions better than dropout-based model uncertainty alone.
records.headline_result: better uncertainty estimation than test-time dropout alone, and higher accuracy than single-prediction segmentation

records.title: Deep Learning for Chest Radiograph Diagnosis in the Emergency Department.
records.exclusion_reason: emergency department chest radiographs in adults (mean age 53 years); not a pediatric population
records.release_evidence: chest radiographs were analyzed with a commercially available deep-learning algorithm

records.title: Development and validation of deep learning algorithms for scoliosis screening using back images.
records.model_family: deep learning image classifiers
records.clinical_problem: screening adolescents for idiopathic scoliosis without radiographs and without unnecessary referrals
records.patient_population: adolescents undergoing scoliosis screening
records.model_description: The input is an unclothed photograph of the back, not a radiograph, which is the point: current school screening has such low positive predictive value that it sends many children for radiographs they did not need. The algorithms detect scoliosis, flag curves of 20 degrees or more, and grade severity, with the aim of triaging who actually needs imaging and of following untreated cases without repeated radiation.
records.headline_result: accuracy superior to human specialists for detecting scoliosis, for detecting curves of 20 degrees or more, and for severity grading

records.title: Effects of Music Training on Inhibitory Control and Associated Neural Networks in School-Aged Children: A Longitudinal Study.
records.exclusion_reason: longitudinal study of music training and inhibitory control in children; no machine-learning model and no clinical imaging task

records.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric and adult congenital cardiac MRI: an unmet clinical need.
records.exclusion_reason: review of deep learning applied to cardiac MRI in pediatric and adult congenital heart disease, from acquisition to analysis; no model developed

records.title: Non-contact physiological monitoring of preterm infants in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
records.exclusion_reason: camera-based contactless heart and respiratory rate monitoring in the neonatal intensive care unit; a vital-signs sensing task, not diagnostic imaging

records.title: Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation for Measuring Biometric Parameters Using Multi-Task Deep Learning.
records.journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
records.model_family: multi-task CNN optimizing segmentation Dice and ellipse parameters jointly
records.clinical_problem: head circumference measurement for fetal growth assessment and gestational age estimation
records.patient_population: fetuses across all trimesters in an ultrasound dataset
records.model_description: Trains segmentation and ellipse fitting together in one loss rather than segmenting first and fitting afterwards, so the network optimizes for the measurement that will actually be reported. Evaluated across trimesters, which matters because the fetal head looks very different early and late in pregnancy.
records.headline_result: segmentation and head circumference measurements matched radiologist annotations, comparable to the state of the art

records.title: Implementation and Validation of a Three-dimensional Cardiac Motion Estimation Network.
records.model_family: unsupervised convolutional network taking two 3D volumes and outputting a motion field, regularized by the Frobenius norm of the field's Jacobian
records.clinical_problem: estimating three-dimensional deformable cardiac motion from 2D cine MR images, the measurement that strain and function analyses rest on
records.patient_population: trained and tested on 150 cardiac MRI patients, then validated on a synthetic set (n = 100) and a pediatric set (n = 33)
records.model_description: A registration network that learns motion without labels: two volumes in, a smooth displacement field out. Its interest for pediatrics is the validation design rather than the architecture, since the pediatric cohort is a held-out generalization test on hearts the network never trained on. It matched or beat five established non-rigid registration methods on every dataset.
records.headline_result: median Dice 0.77 on the pediatric data, higher than or similar to all five comparison registration methods; 0.85 on synthetic data versus 0.67-0.84 for the alternatives
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

records.title: Improving Automated Pediatric Bone Age Estimation Using Ensembles of Models from the 2017 RSNA Machine Learning Challenge.
records.model_name: 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge ensembles
records.model_family: ensembles of up to 10 of the 48 challenge submissions
records.clinical_problem: automated skeletal age estimation from hand radiographs, and how much accuracy is left on the table by using a single model
records.patient_population: 12 611 pediatric hand radiographs for development and a 200-radiograph test set labeled by the weighted average of six pediatric radiologist ratings
records.model_description: A post-hoc study of the RSNA challenge that asks a question the leaderboard could not: what happens when you combine the entries. The useful finding is counter-intuitive and directly actionable for anyone assembling a clinical bone-age system - combining four less-correlated models beat combining the eight top scorers, so model diversity bought more than individual accuracy did.
records.dataset_size: 48 challenge submissions; 12 611 training radiographs; 200 test radiographs
records.headline_result: single-model generalization error 4.55 months versus 3.79 months for the best four-model ensemble; naively combining the top eight models reached only 3.93 months
records.study_design: secondary analysis of a public challenge

records.title: Spherical U-Net on Cortical Surfaces: Methods and Applications.
records.journal: Information processing in medical imaging : proceedings of the ... conference
records.model_family: convolution, pooling and transposed convolution defined on the spherical manifold
records.clinical_problem: parcellating the infant cortical surface and predicting how its attributes will develop
records.patient_population: infants
records.model_description: Standard convolutions assume a regular grid, which a cortical surface mesh is not: vertex counts and local connectivity vary between and within subjects. This defines the convolution on the sphere instead, so a U-Net can operate natively on cortical surfaces. Applied to infant cortical parcellation and to predicting how cortical attribute maps will develop, both of which are prerequisites for detecting abnormal early brain growth.
records.headline_result: competitive accuracy and computational efficiency against state-of-the-art methods on infant cortical parcellation and attribute map prediction

records.title: Fetal Pose Estimation in Volumetric MRI using a 3D Convolution Neural Network.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.model_family: 3D convolutional neural network detecting fetal keypoint landmarks per volume frame
records.clinical_problem: fetal motion during MRI, which forces single-shot acquisition with poor signal-to-noise and diagnostic contrast and often ruins the study - and about which surprisingly little is quantitatively known
records.patient_population: low-spatial-resolution, high-temporal-resolution MRI volumes of the gravid abdomen acquired over 10-30 minute durations
records.model_description: Estimates the fetus's pose - its actual posture - in every frame, which converts a long low-resolution acquisition into a kinematic record. Two things follow that a motion-correction method alone would not give: fetal movement becomes something measurable in health and disease, and the movement statistics can train models that anticipate motion rather than correct it afterwards. A MICCAI paper, and the conference venue is where much of this methods work lives.
records.headline_result: average error 4.47 mm and 96.4% accuracy at a 10 mm threshold for fetal landmark localization

records.title: Automated deep learning design for medical image classification by health-care professionals with no coding experience: a feasibility study.
records.model_family: neural architecture search via Google Cloud AutoML
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs, as one of five diagnostic classification tasks
records.patient_population: children in the Guangzhou pediatric chest radiograph dataset, alongside adult chest radiographs and three non-radiologic datasets
records.model_description: The subject is not a model but a question: can clinicians with no coding experience build a usable image classifier? Five public datasets, including pediatric chest radiographs, were fed to a commercial automated architecture-search service and the resulting classifiers evaluated. Binary tasks did well; multi-class tasks were uneven, and external validation on an unseen skin dataset collapsed, which is the paper's cautionary finding.
records.headline_result: binary tasks: sensitivity 73.3-97.0%, specificity 67-100%, AUPRC 0.87-1.00; external validation on the Edinburgh skin dataset fell to AUPRC 0.47

records.title: Binomial Classification of Pediatric Elbow Fractures Using a Deep Learning Multiview Approach Emulating Radiologist Decision Making.
records.model_family: convolutional network feeding a recurrent network across views
records.clinical_problem: identifying acute traumatic abnormality on pediatric elbow radiographs, where skeletal immaturity changes the normal appearance with age
records.patient_population: 21,456 elbow radiographic studies from a dedicated children's hospital over four years; mean age 7.2 years, 43% girls
records.model_description: Rather than judging each radiograph alone, the model reads the whole three-view series and reaches one decision, which is how a radiologist actually works. Labels came from the reports of a four-year archive at one children's hospital. The published error breakdown is worth reading: it missed 1 of 241 supracondylar and 1 of 88 lateral condylar fractures, but 15 of 77 effusions without fracture, which is the harder and more subtle call.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.95, accuracy 88%, sensitivity 91%, specificity 84%

records.title: Structural neuroimaging biomarkers for obsessive-compulsive disorder in the ENIGMA-OCD consortium: medication matters
records.model_family: multivariate classification on standardized cortical and subcortical measures
records.clinical_problem: whether structural MRI can distinguish an individual with obsessive-compulsive disorder from a healthy control, which no diagnostic biomarker currently does
records.patient_population: 2,304 patients and 2,068 controls across 46 datasets, spanning adult and pediatric (<18) samples
records.model_description: A large negative result, and the most useful kind. Across 46 sites, classification of obsessive-compulsive disorder from structural MRI was poor within the pooled sample and fell to chance when models were validated on data from sites they had never seen. Good performance appeared only within medication-defined subgroups, which is a warning that an apparent imaging biomarker can be a treatment marker. Anyone quoting single-site classification accuracies in a developmental disorder should read this first.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.57-0.62 on the pooled sample and no better than chance (0.51-0.54) on completely new sites; above 0.8 only within medication-stratified subgroups

records.title: Treatment effect of methylphenidate on intrinsic functional brain network in medication-naïve ADHD children: A multivariate analysis.
records.exclusion_reason: study of methylphenidate's effect on resting-state networks in ADHD; the random forest is used to explain variance in symptom change rather than as a diagnostic or prognostic model

records.title: Combining Disrupted and Discriminative Topological Properties of Functional Connectivity Networks as Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Accurate Diagnosis of Early Tourette Syndrome Children.
records.model_family: graph-theoretic network features with a similarity network fusion classifier
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing Tourette syndrome in children, which currently rests on qualitative description of symptoms
records.patient_population: 29 drug-naive children with Tourette syndrome and 37 healthy children
records.model_description: Builds whole-brain functional connectivity networks and uses their topological properties, rather than individual connections, as classification features. Drug-naive patients avoid the usual medication confound. The discriminative regions extended beyond sensorimotor circuits into visual, default-mode and language areas. Sample size is small, so the accuracy should be read as promising rather than established.
records.headline_result: 88.79% classification accuracy from network topological properties

records.title: A Deep Convolutional Neural Network-Based Framework for Automatic Fetal Facial Standard Plane Recognition.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: 16-layer deep CNN with global average pooling and transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: acquiring the fetal facial standard plane, the precondition for any subsequent facial measurement or diagnosis
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
records.model_description: Recognizes whether an ultrasound image is a fetal facial standard plane, a task that defeated hand-crafted features because these planes vary greatly among themselves while resembling many non-standard planes. Global average pooling in place of a large fully connected layer cuts parameters sharply, which is the practical response to having limited training data.
records.headline_result: outperformed traditional hand-crafted feature approaches; figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: In vivo placental MRI shape and textural features predict fetal growth restriction and postnatal outcome.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.model_family: machine learning on placental shape and texture features
records.clinical_problem: identifying fetal growth restriction and estimating birth weight before delivery
records.patient_population: 80 pregnancies between 18 and 39 weeks: 46 healthy and 34 with fetal growth restriction
records.model_description: Characterizes the placenta rather than the fetus, on the reasoning that placental function is what constrains growth. Shape features (volume, thickness, elongation) are combined with first-order and co-occurrence texture measures from 3D T2-weighted MRI to identify growth-restricted pregnancies and estimate birth weight, in both healthy and affected fetuses.
records.headline_result: 86% accuracy, 77% precision and 86% recall for identifying fetal growth restriction; birth weight error 0.3% in healthy and -2.6% in growth-restricted fetuses

records.title: Radiomics in paediatric neuro-oncology: A multicentre study on MRI texture analysis.
records.model_family: support vector machine on 3D texture features
records.clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of childhood brain tumors, which despite advances in MRI has not reached routine practice
records.patient_population: children with brain tumors imaged at multiple UK centres
records.model_description: The question this asks is the one most single-centre radiomics papers do not: does a texture classifier trained at one hospital work at another. It answers it by rigorous pairwise testing between centres, finding AUCs of 76-86% on unseen sites and that similar texture features are enhanced by images from different hospitals. It also examines class imbalance, which is unavoidable when some childhood tumor types are much rarer than others.
records.dataset_size: a multicentre clinical MRI cohort; size not stated
records.headline_result: AUC 76-86% across pairwise cross-centre testing, indicating transferable tumour texture information

records.title: Whole brain white matter connectivity analysis using machine learning: An application to autism.
records.model_family: data-driven fiber clustering with a machine-learning classifier on cluster diffusion features
records.clinical_problem: identifying which white matter connections are altered in autism, and whether that can classify individual children
records.patient_population: 149 children: 70 with autism spectrum disorder and 79 typically developing controls
records.model_description: Clusters whole-brain tractography into anatomically meaningful fiber groups, describes each cluster by its diffusion properties, and uses those as features to classify a child as autistic or not. Because the features are named tracts rather than voxels, the model says which connections carried the decision: corpus callosum, arcuate and uncinate fasciculi, aslant tract, and cerebellar and brainstem connections, with the crossing-fiber tensor most affected.
records.headline_result: 78.33% cross-validated classification accuracy

records.title: Performance of a Deep-Learning Neural Network Model in Assessing Skeletal Maturity on Pediatric Hand Radiographs.
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural network
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in the workup of endocrine and metabolic disorders
records.patient_population: children undergoing clinical hand radiography at two children's hospitals
records.model_description: Takes a hand radiograph and returns an estimated bone age. Trained on 14,036 clinical hand radiographs and their reports from two children's hospitals, then compared against the mean of the clinical report and three additional reviewers on a 200-examination test set, and against a published automated model on the public Digital Hand Atlas.
records.dataset_size: 14,036 clinical hand radiographs for training and validation; 200-examination and 913-examination test sets
records.headline_result: mean difference from reviewers 0 years; root mean square 0.63 years and mean absolute difference 0.50 years
records.study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic accuracy with reader comparison

records.title: Cortical activity in fine-motor tasks in children with Developmental Coordination Disorder: A preliminary fNIRS study.
records.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
records.exclusion_reason: functional near-infrared spectroscopy comparison of cortical activation during fine-motor tasks in six children with developmental coordination disorder and six controls; not radiological imaging and no machine learning

records.title: Psychoradiologic Utility of MR Imaging for Diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Radiomics Analysis.
records.model_family: random forest on shape and diffusion radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and separation of its inattentive and combined subtypes
records.patient_population: 83 newly diagnosed, never-treated children with ADHD aged 7-14 and 87 age- and sex-matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, extracts gray-matter shape and white-matter diffusion features, selects the ones with real discriminative power inside cross-validation loops, and classifies a child as having ADHD or not, and then which subtype. Notably, total brain and tissue volumes did not differ between groups, so whatever signal exists is in shape rather than size.
records.headline_result: 73.7% accuracy for ADHD versus control, 80.1% for inattentive versus combined subtype

records.title: Machine Learning for Fetal Growth Prediction.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning predicts estimated fetal weight from clinical and demographic variables available at birth rather than from images; ultrasound supplies the reference standard, not the model input

records.title: Subtyping cognitive profiles in Autism Spectrum Disorder using a Functional Random Forest algorithm.
records.model_family: random forest plus community detection on the resulting proximity matrix
records.clinical_problem: whether autism spectrum disorder contains distinct cognitive subtypes with different brain signatures
records.patient_population: 47 children with autism and 58 typically developing children aged 9-13
records.model_description: First classifies a child as autistic or typically developing from seven cognitive tasks, then reuses the forest's internal proximity between subjects to cluster them into subgroups, and finally asks whether those data-driven subgroups differ in resting-state functional connectivity. The clinical interest is in subtyping a heterogeneous diagnosis rather than in the classification accuracy, which is moderate.
records.headline_result: 72.7% classification accuracy (specificity 80.7%, sensitivity 63.1%); three autism and four typically developing subgroups identified

records.title: Differential effects of childhood neglect and abuse during sensitive exposure periods on male and female hippocampus.
records.exclusion_reason: MRI of adults aged 18-25; childhood refers to retrospectively reported maltreatment exposure, not the age at imaging

records.title: Abnormal fronto-striatal activation as a marker of threshold and subthreshold Bulimia Nervosa.
records.model_family: multi-voxel pattern analysis classifier over task fMRI conflict-related activation
records.clinical_problem: whether the fronto-striatal disturbance of bulimia nervosa is present early, when the clinical picture is still subthreshold and the diagnosis is least certain
records.patient_population: two samples of adolescents with bulimia nervosa spectrum symptoms differing in severity, illness duration and age, compared with healthy adolescents, scanned during a Simon task
records.model_description: The design does something most classification studies do not: the classifier trained to separate fully symptomatic patients from healthy adolescents is then applied to the subthreshold group, and it transfers. That cross-severity generalization is a stronger claim than in-sample accuracy, because it says the same circuit disturbance is present before the disorder is, which is what would make it a risk marker rather than a consequence.
records.dataset_size: two adolescent patient samples plus healthy controls, sizes not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: both threshold and subthreshold bulimia adolescents were accurately discriminated from healthy adolescents, and patterns learned from the severe group generalized to the subthreshold group
records.study_design: retrospective analysis of task fMRI cohorts

records.title: Neural preservation underlies speech improvement from auditory deprivation in young cochlear implant recipients.
records.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
records.model_family: machine-learning classifiers on regional neuroanatomical density and spatial pattern similarity
records.clinical_problem: predicting which deaf children will gain speech perception from a cochlear implant, before the operation
records.patient_population: children implanted before 3.5 years of age, compared against age-matched normally hearing children
records.model_description: Takes presurgical brain MRI from a cochlear implant candidate and predicts how much that individual child's speech perception will improve after implantation. The method first identifies which anatomical networks auditory deprivation has and has not affected; the predictive signal came from the unaffected regions, particularly auditory association and cognitive areas, suggesting what is preserved matters more than what is lost.
records.headline_result: highest classification accuracy, specificity and sensitivity came from brain regions unaffected by auditory deprivation

records.title: Association of Heritable Cognitive Ability and Psychopathology With White Matter Properties in Children and Adolescents.
records.exclusion_reason: cross-sectional association between diffusion metrics and dimensional cognition and psychopathology scores in a developmental cohort; no diagnostic or prognostic model is built

records.title: MABAL: a Novel Deep-Learning Architecture for Machine-Assisted Bone Age Labeling.
records.model_family: custom convolutional network trained from scratch
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment, which is tedious and time consuming for the radiologist
records.patient_population: 10,289 skeletal age examinations, 8,909 from one institution's archive and 1,383 from the public Digital Hand Atlas
records.model_description: Argues, and demonstrates, that a network designed and trained from scratch for the specific task can beat transfer learning from natural images, given a large enough institutional dataset. Training is split into four cohorts by sex and age band, which reflects how Greulich and Pyle is applied in practice. Testing uses 20 radiographs per one-year age cohort rather than a random split, so performance is visible across the age range instead of averaged over it.
records.dataset_size: 10,289 training images across four sex and age cohorts
records.headline_result: reported to outperform existing proposed bone age algorithms; figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: Strategies for prediction and mitigation of radiation-induced liver toxicity.
records.exclusion_reason: review of radiation-induced liver disease and stereotactic radiotherapy in adults; machine-learning predictive models are named as a future direction

records.title: Identifying Medical Diagnoses and Treatable Diseases by Image-Based Deep Learning.
records.model_family: Inception-v3 transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia on chest radiographs, and bacterial vs viral origin
records.patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia; the primary cohort is adults with retinal OCT
records.model_description: A transfer-learning framework that takes a single image and returns a diagnostic label, with an occlusion map highlighting the regions that drove the decision. It was developed on retinal OCT images and then retrained on pediatric chest radiographs to separate normal from pneumonia and bacterial from viral pneumonia. The paper's argument is that a general transfer-learning recipe needs far less labelled data than training from scratch.
records.dataset_size: not stated in the abstract for the chest radiograph cohort
records.headline_result: performance comparable to human experts on the retinal task; the pediatric chest radiograph result is not quantified in the abstract
records.study_design: retrospective technical development with expert comparison

records.title: Randomised controlled trial of simvastatin treatment for autism in young children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (SANTA).
records.exclusion_reason: randomized controlled drug trial in neurofibromatosis type 1; machine-learning classification is a secondary analysis of trial imaging endpoints rather than a diagnostic model

records.title: Fully-automated alignment of 3D fetal brain ultrasound to a canonical reference space using multi-task learning.
records.model_family: multi-task fully convolutional network
records.clinical_problem: putting 3D fetal neurosonography volumes into a common reference frame despite arbitrary fetal position
records.patient_population: 140 fetal ultrasound volumes, gestational age 26.0 ± 4.4 weeks
records.model_description: Localizes the fetal brain, segments its structures, and aligns the volume to a reference coordinate system, all from one network with shared features and task-specific outputs. The coordinate system is defined anatomically from the skull boundary, eye sockets and head pose predicted from intracranial structures, which is what makes alignment robust to how the fetus happens to be lying.
records.headline_result: high brain overlap and low eye localization error on co-alignment, independent of gestational age or head size

records.title: Sulcal Polymorphisms of the IFC and ACC Contribute to Inhibitory Control Variability in Children and Adults.
records.exclusion_reason: anatomical MRI study relating sulcal pattern asymmetry of the cingulate and inferior frontal cortex to inhibitory control scores; no machine learning model

records.title: Predicting Treatment Response to Intra-arterial Therapies for Hepatocellular Carcinoma with the Use of Supervised Machine Learning-An Artificial Intelligence Concept.
records.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning for chemoembolization response in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma (mean age 62 years)

records.title: Combination of rs-fMRI and sMRI Data to Discriminate Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Using Deep Belief Network.
records.model_family: deep belief network on combined functional and structural features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children, where early diagnosis changes what intervention is possible
records.patient_population: 185 children aged 5-10 from the ABIDE I and II datasets (116 with autism, 69 controls)
records.model_description: Combines resting-state functional MRI with gray and white matter measures over anatomically labelled regions and learns a joint representation with a deep belief network, on the argument that earlier work used only shallow hand-computed features. Deliberately restricted to 5-10 year olds because that is where diagnosis matters. The accuracy is modest and the specificity is poor, which the numbers make plain.
records.headline_result: 65.56% accuracy (sensitivity 84%, specificity 33%, F1 74.76%) by 10-fold cross-validation
records.study_design: technical development on a public dataset

records.title: Early prediction of cognitive deficits in very preterm infants using functional connectome data in an artificial neural network framework.
records.model_family: stacked sparse autoencoder for feature selection with a support vector machine classifier
records.clinical_problem: identifying at term-equivalent age which very preterm infants will have cognitive deficits at 2 years
records.patient_population: 28 infants born at 23-31 weeks without brain injury, scanned at term-equivalent age; features pretrained on 884 subjects from a public database
records.model_description: Learns a compressed representation of the functional connectome without labels, using a large public dataset, then uses that representation to predict 2-year cognitive outcome in a small preterm cohort. The transfer step is the point: neonatal cohorts are too small to train a deep model directly. Frontal lobe and somatosensory regions contributed most. The authors present it explicitly as proof of concept given the sample size.
records.dataset_size: 884 subjects for unsupervised pretraining; 28 very preterm infants for prediction
records.headline_result: 70.6% accuracy and AUC 0.76 for cognitive deficit at 2 years corrected age

records.title: Interactive Medical Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning With Image-Specific Fine Tuning.
records.model_family: CNN with image-specific fine tuning inside a bounding-box and scribble pipeline
records.clinical_problem: outlining fetal organs on MRI when only some organ classes were annotated for training
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses brain tumor MRI
records.model_description: The radiologist draws a bounding box, and optionally scribbles, and the network segments the structure inside it, fine-tuning itself on that specific image before producing the final contour. Because it adapts per image, it can outline organ classes that were never annotated during training. Demonstrated on fetal MRI organs and on brain tumor MRI.
records.headline_result: more robust than state-of-the-art CNNs on unseen object classes, with fewer user interactions and less user time than traditional interactive segmentation

records.title: Use of Machine Learning to Determine Deviance in Neuroanatomical Maturity Associated With Future Psychosis in Youths at Clinically High Risk.
records.model_family: supervised machine-learning brain-age regression on T1-weighted MRI
records.clinical_problem: identifying which clinically high-risk adolescents will convert to psychosis
records.patient_population: 953 healthy children aged 3-21 for model development; 275 clinically high-risk individuals (39 of whom developed psychosis) and 109 controls aged 12-21 for application
records.model_description: A model trained on structural MRI of healthy children to predict chronological age; the gap between that predicted age and the child's real age is then read as a measure of deviant neuroanatomical maturation. Applied to clinically high-risk adolescents, a larger gap was associated with higher risk of developing psychosis, but only in the younger part of the range.
records.dataset_size: 953 healthy children for training; 384 subjects for external validation and application
records.headline_result: clinically high-risk individuals showed a mean 0.64-year gap between predicted and chronological age versus controls (P = .008); greater deviation was associated with psychosis risk (P = .01)

records.title: Automatic Estimation of Fetal Abdominal Circumference From Ultrasound Images.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: convolutional network classifying anatomical landmarks, followed by a Hough transform to fit the circumference
records.clinical_problem: automating abdominal circumference measurement, the hardest of the standard fetal biometry parameters because the abdomen has low and non-uniform contrast against its surroundings and an irregular outline
records.patient_population: clinical ultrasound data from 56 pregnant women, with two experts providing acceptance judgments
records.model_description: Built around how the sonographer decides rather than around end-to-end regression: the network is trained to recognize the three landmarks that define an acceptable abdominal plane - stomach bubble, amniotic fluid and umbilical vein - and only then does a Hough transform fit the circle. That keeps the training requirement small and the failures interpretable. The paper names its failure modes plainly, which is unusual: an oversized fetus, absent amniotic fluid, or a distorted abdominal outline.
records.headline_result: agreement of 0.809 and 0.771 with two experts, against 0.905 agreement between the two experts themselves; stable even on images degraded by shadowing
records.study_design: retrospective model development with expert acceptance check

records.title: 3-D Reconstruction in Canonical Co-Ordinate Space From Arbitrarily Oriented 2-D Images.
records.model_family: CNN regression predicting rigid transformations to a learned canonical atlas
records.clinical_problem: initializing slice-to-volume registration for fetal MRI, where heavy in-utero motion breaks optimization-based methods
records.patient_population: fetuses at around 20 weeks gestation, including heavily moving cases, plus simulated data
records.model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented 2D slice belongs in a canonical 3D atlas space from intensity alone, with no initialization. Conventional registration has a narrow capture range and needs a good starting estimate, which a heavily moving fetus does not provide; this removes that dependency and slots into a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline. It runs fast enough for real-time use.
records.dataset_size: simulated MRI plus real fetal MRI data
records.headline_result: average spatial prediction error 7 mm on simulated data, with qualitatively improved reconstructions for heavily moving fetuses at around 20 weeks

records.title: Fetal health status prediction based on maternal clinical history using machine learning techniques.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
records.exclusion_reason: nine classifiers predict fetal congenital anomaly status from maternal questionnaire and clinical history; ultrasound is context for the problem, not model input, and no images are analyzed

records.title: Artificial intelligence assistance for fetal head biometry: Assessment of automated measurement software.
records.model_family: commercial automated plane identification and measurement software
records.clinical_problem: finding the transthalamic plane and measuring biparietal diameter and head circumference from a 3D volume rather than by hand
records.patient_population: 30 fetuses at 17-30 weeks gestation, each with two 3D volumes and a conventional 2D image
records.model_description: Extracts the standard measurement plane out of an acquired 3D volume and measures it, removing the operator's plane selection from the equation. Agreement with two experienced sonographers was good, and the confidence intervals quantify what automation costs: about 4 mm on biparietal diameter and 11 mm on head circumference against manual 2D measurement, which is the number to weigh against the reproducibility gain.
records.release_evidence: artificial intelligence software (Smartplanes)
records.headline_result: intra- and interobserver ICC above 0.98; 95% confidence intervals 4 mm for biparietal diameter and 11 mm for head circumference between automated 3D and manual 2D measurement

records.title: Predicting early recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma with texture analysis of preoperative MRI: a radiomics study.
records.exclusion_reason: MRI texture analysis to predict hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence in adults (mean age 67 years)

records.title: Heritability of the human connectome: A connectotyping study.
records.exclusion_reason: heritability of resting-state connectivity patterns in healthy siblings; a neuroscience question, not a diagnostic imaging application

records.title: Predicting Survival Using Pretreatment CT for Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treated With Transarterial Chemoembolization: Comparison of Models Using Radiomics.
records.exclusion_reason: CT radiomics for survival after chemoembolization in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma

records.title: Extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid in high-risk and normal-risk children with autism aged 2-4 years: a case-control study.
records.model_family: previously validated machine-learning classifier on CSF volume, brain volume, age and sex
records.clinical_problem: whether extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid volume is an imaging marker of autism beyond infancy
records.patient_population: 159 children aged 2-4 with autism spectrum disorder (both simplex and multiplex families) and 77 with typical development
records.model_description: Applies a classifier previously validated in infants to an independent cohort of 2-4 year olds, using extra-axial CSF volume together with brain volume, age and sex to separate children with autism from typically developing controls. The substantive finding is replication: the CSF excess is present in an independent sample, persists beyond infancy, and is the same in children with and without a family history.
records.headline_result: 15.1% more extra-axial CSF in the autism group after adjustment (p = 0.007, Cohen's d 0.39)

records.title: Detection of Traumatic Pediatric Elbow Joint Effusion Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural networks of varying depth and architecture, some ImageNet-pretrained and some randomly initialized
records.clinical_problem: detecting traumatic joint effusion on lateral elbow radiographs, the indirect sign that often stands in for an occult pediatric fracture
records.patient_population: 882 children presenting to the emergency department with upper extremity trauma, 901 lateral elbow radiographs
records.model_description: A direct test of whether a small pediatric dataset is enough. Fewer than 700 training radiographs, transfer learning from ImageNet, and a hyperparameter search on 115 validation images produced a classifier that reads elbow effusion at roughly 91 percent sensitivity and specificity. The clinical framing matters more than the numbers: effusion is the finding that tells the emergency physician to treat a child as fractured when no fracture line is visible.
records.headline_result: test-set AUC 0.943, sensitivity 0.909, specificity 0.906

records.title: Characterization of coronary artery pathological formations from OCT imaging using deep learning.
records.model_family: deep features from three pre-trained convolutional networks combined by majority voting
records.clinical_problem: characterizing the intracoronary tissue changes caused by Kawasaki disease on optical coherence tomography, so that coronary involvement can be classified without expert manual interpretation of every cross-section
records.patient_population: 33 retrospective pullbacks of intracoronary cross-sectional OCT images from pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease
records.model_description: An unusual corner of pediatric imaging AI: intravascular OCT in the coronary arteries of children with Kawasaki disease, where the pathological formations differ from adult atherosclerosis and no reader has seen many of them. Rather than train from scratch on 33 cases, the authors take deep features from three ImageNet-pretrained networks and vote - the standard small-data recipe, applied to a disease that will never have a large dataset.
records.headline_result: accuracy, sensitivity and specificity up to 0.99 +/- 0.01 per tissue class with the majority voting scheme

records.title: Machine-learning analysis outperforms conventional statistical models and CT classification systems in predicting 6-month outcomes in pediatric patients sustaining traumatic brain injury.
records.model_family: artificial neural network
records.clinical_problem: predicting six-month outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, where adult CT grading systems are the only tools available
records.patient_population: 565 children under 18 who sustained traumatic brain injury and had a head CT within 24 hours
records.model_description: Predicts whether a child will have a favorable Glasgow Outcome Scale score six months after traumatic brain injury, from the admission head CT and clinical record. The comparison is the point: the established adult CT grading systems (Helsinki, Rotterdam, Marshall) were first evaluated on this pediatric cohort and found only moderately predictive, and the pediatric-specific network substantially outperformed all three.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.946 ± 0.042 versus 0.781-0.838 for the Helsinki, Rotterdam and Marshall CT scores

records.title: Automatic segmentation of OCT retinal boundaries using recurrent neural networks and graph search.
records.exclusion_reason: retinal optical coherence tomography layer segmentation; ophthalmic imaging is outside radiology as scoped for this database

records.title: Automatic classification of pediatric pneumonia based on lung ultrasound pattern recognition.
records.model_family: neural network on brightness-distribution feature vectors
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing childhood pneumonia where there is no radiologist and no radiography, using lung ultrasound
records.patient_population: 21 children under 5 in Lima, Peru (15 with clinically and radiographically confirmed pneumonia, 6 without lung disease)
records.model_description: Strips out skin, fat and muscle from a lung ultrasound frame, divides the remaining image into rectangular segments, and classifies the brightness pattern of each as consolidated or normal lung. The motivation is explicitly resource-constrained: lung ultrasound detects pneumonia well but needs a trained interpreter, and this removes that requirement. The cohort is very small, which the accuracy figures should be read against.
records.dataset_size: 60 lung ultrasound frames from 21 children; 3,055 feature vectors
records.headline_result: 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity for pneumonia infiltrates

records.title: Deep Learning Based Attenuation Correction of PET/MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumor Patients: Evaluation in a Clinical Setting.
records.model_family: deep learning for MR-derived attenuation correction
records.clinical_problem: quantitatively accurate FET-PET/MRI in children without a CT for attenuation correction, and without a second sedation
records.patient_population: 79 pediatric brain tumor examinations, 36 with active tumor volume above 1 mL analyzed
records.model_description: Generates the attenuation map that PET reconstruction needs directly from MRI, so a child having simultaneous FET-PET/MRI does not need a CT and does not need a second sedation for a sequential scan. Compared against a CT-derived reference and against a non-learned MR-based method on the clinical metrics that actually drive decisions, tumor-to-background activity ratios.
records.headline_result: the only method with all patients inside predefined clinical limits; tumor-to-background difference from CT-based reference -0.1% (95% CI -0.8 to 0.5) versus 5.9% for Dixon-based correction

records.title: DeepSSM: A Deep Learning Framework for Statistical Shape Modeling from Raw Images.
records.journal: Shape in medical imaging : International Workshop, ShapeMI 2018, held in conjunction with MICCAI 2018, Granada, Spain, September 20, 2018 : proceedings. ShapeMI (Workshop) (2018 : Granada, Spain)
records.model_family: convolutional neural network that localizes the structure, establishes correspondences and regresses PCA loadings in a point distribution model, trained with a shape-statistics data augmentation scheme
records.clinical_problem: building statistical shape models straight from raw images, replacing a registration-segmentation-correspondence pipeline that needs parameter tuning, manual delineation and quality control at every step
records.patient_population: three applications, the first of which is pediatric cranial CT for characterizing metopic craniosynostosis; the others are adult femur CT and left atrium MRI
records.model_description: A MICCAI-workshop method paper whose lead application is pediatric: metopic craniosynostosis is a shape diagnosis, and statistical shape modeling is how shape is quantified, but the conventional pipeline is too hand-operated to run at scale. The augmentation trick is the enabling piece - 40-50 processed scans with known shape parameters are resampled into thousands of plausible training images, which is how a deep network gets trained on a surgical cohort's worth of data.
records.dataset_size: 40-50 processed CT/MRI scans per application, augmented into thousands of training images
records.headline_result: accurate low-dimensional shape representations produced directly from unseen 3D images with essentially no parameter tuning or user assistance

records.title: Visualization and Interpretation of Convolutional Neural Network Predictions in Detecting Pneumonia in Pediatric Chest Radiographs.
records.model_family: customized VGG16 with visualization of class-relevant regions
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children, and separating bacterial from viral pneumonia
records.patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia
records.model_description: Classifies a pediatric chest radiograph as normal or pneumonia and then as bacterial or viral, and, unusually for this literature, spends most of its effort on showing where the model looked. It introduces a way of localizing the region that drives predictions across all images of a class rather than one image at a time, on the argument that an unexplained black box is unusable for screening decisions.
records.headline_result: 96.2% accuracy detecting pneumonia and 93.6% distinguishing bacterial from viral

records.title: Altered structural connectivity in ADHD: a network based analysis.
records.exclusion_reason: graph-theoretic comparison of structural connectomes in boys with ADHD; no machine-learning model is trained

records.title: Neural Predictors of Initiating Alcohol Use During Adolescence.
records.model_family: random forest classification
records.clinical_problem: identifying adolescents at risk of initiating heavy alcohol use before they start
records.patient_population: 137 healthy substance-naive adolescents aged 12-14, followed annually to age 18
records.model_description: Takes structural and functional MRI together with demographic and neuropsychological measures from a substance-naive 12-14 year old and predicts whether that adolescent will have initiated moderate to heavy drinking by 18. The model is used as a variable-importance tool rather than a deployed classifier: its output is the ranked list of 34 contributing predictors, which mixes imaging with behavioral and social factors.
records.dataset_size: 137 adolescents (70 later initiated use, 67 did not)
records.headline_result: 34 predictors identified, including thinner cortex and reduced activation in diffusely distributed regions alongside demographic and behavioral factors; discrimination not quantified in the abstract

records.title: The neural basis of responsive caregiving behaviour: Investigating temporal dynamics within the parental brain.
records.exclusion_reason: review of the neural basis of caregiving behaviour in adults; no machine learning and no pediatric imaging

records.title: DTI-based connectome analysis of adolescents with major depressive disorder reveals hypoconnectivity of the right caudate.
records.exclusion_reason: graph-based connectome comparison in adolescent depression; no machine-learning model is trained

records.title: BrainNetCNN: Convolutional neural networks for brain networks; towards predicting neurodevelopment.
records.model_family: CNN with edge-to-edge, edge-to-node and node-to-graph convolutions on connectivity matrices
records.clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth
records.patient_population: infants born preterm, scanned between 27 and 46 weeks postmenstrual age
records.model_description: Takes a structural connectivity matrix built from diffusion tensor imaging and returns predicted Bayley-III cognitive and motor scores at 18 months, corrected for prematurity. The convolutions are designed for network topology rather than image space. It also estimates postmenstrual age at scan, and the learned edge weights can be inspected to see which connections drive the prediction.
records.headline_result: outperformed a fully connected network with the same parameter count and other comparison methods; estimated postmenstrual age to within about 2 weeks
records.study_design: technical development on a preterm cohort

records.title: Individual prediction of long-term outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis: Applying machine learning techniques to brain imaging data.
records.model_family: support vector regression on structural MRI measures
records.clinical_problem: predicting six-year functional and clinical outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis, most of whom will not convert
records.patient_population: 64 ultra-high-risk and 62 typically developing adolescents aged 12-18, with outcome determined for 43 at six years
records.model_description: Predicts long-term functioning and symptom scores as continuous values rather than converting versus not converting, on the argument that most ultra-high-risk adolescents turn out resilient and a binary label throws that away. Baseline subcortical volumes carried the strongest signal. The effect size is medium and the authors are careful not to overclaim individual-level prediction from it.
records.dataset_size: 126 adolescents at baseline; 43 with six-year outcome
records.headline_result: highest predictive correlation r = 0.42 between baseline subcortical volumes and long-term level of functioning

records.title: Neural initialization of audiovisual integration in prereaders at varying risk for developmental dyslexia.
records.exclusion_reason: combined ERP and fMRI study of letter-sound learning in prereaders; no machine-learning model and no clinical imaging task

records.title: Evidence for superior neurobiological and behavioral inhibitory control abilities in non-offending as compared to offending pedophiles.
records.exclusion_reason: functional MRI of inhibitory control in adult men; children appear only as the subject of the offending behavior studied

records.title: Deep learning for automated skeletal bone age assessment in X-ray images.
records.model_family: deep CNN, several architectures compared
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
records.patient_population: children across all age ranges, races and both sexes in a public hand-radiograph dataset
records.model_description: Takes a left-hand radiograph and returns a bone age, replacing Greulich-Pyle or Tanner-Whitehouse atlas matching. The paper's contribution is as much methodological as clinical: it is the first bone-age model tested on a public dataset across all ages, races and both sexes with source code released, and it uses that setting to compare learned against hand-crafted features and to ask how to train a network on few images.
records.release_evidence: first automated bone age work tested on a public dataset for which the source code is available
records.dataset_size: a public hand-radiograph dataset; size not stated
records.headline_result: average discrepancy between manual and automatic bone age of about 0.8 years
records.study_design: technical development on a public benchmark

records.title: DeepCut: Object Segmentation From Bounding Box Annotations Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: CNN in a densely connected conditional random field, trained from bounding boxes
records.clinical_problem: segmenting fetal brain and lung on MRI without pixel-level annotation
records.patient_population: fetuses in a fetal MRI dataset
records.model_description: Turns cheap annotation into pixel-level segmentations: an annotator draws only a bounding box, and the method alternates between training a network and re-estimating the segmentation inside the box until it converges. Extends the classical GrabCut idea with a learned classifier. Tested on fetal brain and lung segmentation from MRI.
records.headline_result: encouraging accuracy on fetal brain and lung segmentation from bounding boxes alone; figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: Diagnostic model generated by MRI-derived brain features in toddlers with autism spectrum disorder.
records.journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
records.model_family: random forest classifier over regional cortical thickness, volume and surface area features
records.clinical_problem: finding an objective imaging biomarker to supplement autism diagnosis in toddlers, which currently rests on psychological evaluation, clinical observation and history and is therefore subjective and reporter-dependent
records.patient_population: 46 children with autism spectrum disorder and 39 children with developmental delay, aged 18 to 37 months
records.model_description: The comparison group is the useful design choice: developmental delay rather than typical development, which is the discrimination that is actually hard in a toddler clinic. Three anatomical feature families are compared head to head, and cortical thickness beats both volume and surface area. The authors are careful about the claim - a supplementary line of evidence for a diagnosis, not a replacement - which is the appropriate register for 85 toddlers.
records.headline_result: best performance from regional average cortical thickness of the 20 most important random forest features, outperforming volume-based and surface-area-based classification

records.title: Metrics of brain network architecture capture the impact of disease in children with epilepsy.
records.model_family: machine learning on global graph metrics of resting-state networks
records.clinical_problem: quantifying the cumulative impact of epilepsy on a developing brain, as a route to a marker of cognitive deterioration
records.patient_population: 45 children aged 4-19 with focal epilepsy, with full-scale IQ measured by a pediatric neuropsychologist
records.model_description: Parcellates the cortex into about 700 nodes, computes five global network metrics from resting-state MRI, and predicts epilepsy duration from them, using duration as a stand-in for how much the disease has affected the brain. Duration was itself inversely related to IQ. The prediction is near-perfect, which given 45 patients and five predictors warrants caution, but the framing — imaging metrics as a patient-level marker of cognitive deterioration — is the useful part.
records.headline_result: predicted and actual epilepsy duration correlated at r = 0.95 (p = 0.0001), driven mainly by network modularity

records.title: A framework for analysis of linear ultrasound videos to detect fetal presentation and heartbeat.
records.model_family: frame-by-frame classifier regularized by a conditional random field over time, with a kernelized linear dynamical model for heartbeat detection
records.clinical_problem: confirming pregnancy viability and fetal presentation - the two first questions of any obstetric ultrasound - from a simple predefined sweep that a novice can perform
records.patient_population: 323 predefined free-hand ultrasound videos sweeping the maternal abdomen
records.model_description: Task-shifting by design. The scanning protocol is engineered so that a fixed straight sweep is guaranteed to cross the skull, abdomen and heart, and the algorithm then does the interpreting - which is what lets someone with no sonography training establish viability and presentation. Temporal structure is used twice: a conditional random field smooths the per-frame labels, and heartbeat is read out of the dynamics of consecutive cardiac frames rather than from any single image.
records.headline_result: mean classification accuracy 83.4% for detecting fetal skull, abdomen and heart, and 93.1% for heartbeat detection

records.title: Novel surface features for automated detection of focal cortical dysplasias in paediatric epilepsy.
records.model_family: neural network classifier on surface-based morphometric features
records.clinical_problem: finding focal cortical dysplasia on MRI in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, where detection determines whether surgery is offered
records.patient_population: 22 children with focal epilepsy (mean age 12.1 years) and 28 healthy controls (mean age 14.6 years)
records.model_description: Scans the cortical surface vertex by vertex and flags candidate dysplastic regions. Alongside established measures (cortical thickness, gray-white blurring, FLAIR intensity, sulcal depth, curvature) it adds features designed for a developing brain: local cortical deformation, a doughnut measure of local variability against the surrounding cortex, and per-vertex interhemispheric asymmetry. Existing adult tools had not worked on children, which is precisely the gap it addresses.
records.headline_result: sensitivity rose from 59% with established features alone to 73% with the added novel features

records.title: Altered functional connectivity in default mode network in Internet gaming disorder: Influence of childhood ADHD.
records.exclusion_reason: functional connectivity study of internet gaming disorder in young adult men; childhood ADHD is a historical exposure and there is no model

records.title: GIFT-Cloud: A data sharing and collaboration platform for medical imaging research.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
records.exclusion_reason: GIFT-Cloud is a data sharing and anonymization platform for medical imaging research, built for a fetal surgery collaboration; research infrastructure rather than a machine learning model

records.title: Early brain development in infants at high risk for autism spectrum disorder.
records.model_family: deep-learning classifier on cortical surface area features
records.clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis before behavioral symptoms are established
records.patient_population: 106 infants at high familial risk of autism and 42 low-risk infants, imaged at 6, 12 and 24 months
records.model_description: Takes brain MRI acquired at 6 and 12 months of age, chiefly cortical surface area measurements, and returns a prediction of whether that individual child will meet criteria for autism at 24 months. Trained and cross-validated within a prospective high-familial-risk infant cohort. The clinical interest is identifying children before symptoms emerge, when early intervention is still possible.
records.headline_result: positive predictive value 81%, sensitivity 88% for a 24-month autism diagnosis

records.title: Deep feature learning for automatic tissue classification of coronary artery using optical coherence tomography.
records.exclusion_reason: intracoronary optical coherence tomography in Kawasaki disease; optical coherence tomography is outside radiology as scoped for this database

records.title: Fully Automated Deep Learning System for Bone Age Assessment.
records.model_family: ImageNet-pretrained CNN, fine-tuned
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in endocrine and metabolic workup
records.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment, analyzed separately by sex
records.model_description: An end-to-end pipeline: it finds and crops the hand, standardizes the radiograph, and returns a bone age, with attention maps showing which growth centers drove the estimate. The authors report deploying it in their clinical environment as a decision-support tool returning a result in under two seconds.
records.release_evidence: deployed in the authors' clinical environment as a decision-support system; no external availability stated
records.headline_result: bone age within 1 year in 90.4% (female) and 94.2% (male) of test radiographs; within 2 years in 98.1% and 99.0%
records.study_design: retrospective single-center development with clinical deployment

records.title: Tuning Up the Old Brain with New Tricks: Attention Training via Neurofeedback.
records.exclusion_reason: review of real-time neurofeedback for attention training in older adults; not imaging interpretation and not a pediatric population

records.title: FUIQA: Fetal Ultrasound Image Quality Assessment With Deep Convolutional Networks.
records.model_family: two CNNs (localization network and quality-classification network)
records.clinical_problem: automatic quality control of obstetric ultrasound images before biometric measurements are taken from them
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound examination
records.model_description: One network finds the fetal abdominal region in the image, a second scores whether the key landmarks (stomach bubble and umbilical vein) are adequately depicted. The output is a quality verdict, not a diagnosis: it is meant to catch a badly acquired or wrongly chosen slice before someone measures from it, which is a common and unmonitored source of biometric error.
records.headline_result: quality assessment comparable to the subjective ratings of three medical doctors

records.title: Ultrasound Standard Plane Detection Using a Composite Neural Network Framework.
records.model_family: composite convolutional and recurrent network with multitask learning
records.clinical_problem: acquiring the correct standard planes during obstetric ultrasound, which currently depends on operator experience
records.patient_population: fetuses in hundreds of obstetric ultrasound videos
records.model_description: Identifies several different fetal standard planes from ultrasound video with one general framework, rather than a separate detector per plane as earlier work did. The convolutional part learns appearance within a frame and the recurrent part learns how frames relate over time; multitask learning shares what is common between plane types, which is how it copes with limited training data.
records.headline_result: better standard-plane detection than plane-specific prior methods; figures not stated in the abstract

records.title: Multi-modal, Multi-measure, and Multi-class Discrimination of ADHD with Hierarchical Feature Extraction and Extreme Learning Machine Using Structural and Functional Brain MRI.
records.model_family: hierarchical sparse feature selection with an extreme learning machine
records.clinical_problem: separating ADHD inattentive from ADHD combined from typical development on imaging
records.patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset
records.model_description: Combines structural measures (cortical thickness and its variability, volume, surface area, intensity) with functional connectivity maps, selects the most discriminative features hierarchically, and classifies into three groups rather than two. Multi-class performance is much weaker than binary, which is the honest and clinically relevant part: telling ADHD from typical development is easier than telling the subtypes apart.
records.dataset_size: selected subjects from the public ADHD-200 dataset
records.headline_result: 76.19% accuracy in the three-class setting and 92.86% in the binary setting (both p < 0.0001)
records.study_design: technical development on a public dataset

records.title: Premature Brain Aging in Baboons Resulting from Moderate Fetal Undernutrition.
records.exclusion_reason: brain-age neuroimaging biomarker applied to young adult baboons exposed to fetal undernutrition; an animal model, not pediatric patient imaging

records.title: Uncovering the neuroanatomical correlates of cognitive, affective and conative theory of mind in paediatric traumatic brain injury: a neural systems perspective.
records.exclusion_reason: structural MRI study relating grey-matter volume of large-scale brain networks to theory of mind outcomes 24 months after pediatric traumatic brain injury; regression analysis, no machine learning model

records.title: Functional neuroimaging of high-risk 6-month-old infants predicts a diagnosis of autism at 24 months of age.
records.model_family: cross-validated machine-learning classifier on functional connectivity features
records.clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis at 24 months from imaging at 6 months
records.patient_population: 59 six-month-old infants at high familial risk for autism
records.model_description: Takes resting-state functional connectivity MRI acquired at 6 months of age and returns a prediction of whether that child will receive an autism diagnosis at 24 months. Functional connections were first related to 24-month social, language, motor and repetitive-behavior scores, then used as features in a fully cross-validated classifier.
records.headline_result: positive predictive value 100% (95% CI 62.9-100), sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 100%

records.title: Auto-Context Convolutional Neural Network (Auto-Net) for Brain Extraction in Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.model_family: auto-context CNN (voxelwise multi-plane and U-net variants)
records.clinical_problem: extracting the brain from surrounding tissue on MRI, including fetal brains in arbitrary orientations
records.patient_population: public adult benchmark datasets plus reconstructed fetal brain MRI
records.model_description: Separates brain from non-brain on MRI without registering to an atlas and without assuming anything about image geometry, which is what makes it work on a fetal brain lying in an arbitrary orientation inside the uterus. It feeds its own probability maps back in as context, iteratively, so the network learns the shape and connectedness of the brain rather than only local intensity.
records.dataset_size: two public benchmarks (LPBA40, OASIS) plus a fetal brain MRI set
records.headline_result: Dice 97.73% and 97.62% on the public adult benchmarks and 95.97% on arbitrarily oriented fetal brains, where competing methods performed poorly

records.model_description: Watches freehand 2D ultrasound as it is acquired and, in real time, names which of 13 standard fetal views is on screen and draws a box around the relevant anatomy. The study is designed around the assisted workflow rather than the model alone: two radiologists read the same 200 cases with the software and with the atlas, and both concordance with the reference and reading time were measured. This is the question a department actually faces before buying such a tool.

records.headline_result: software alone concordant in 69.5% of cases (r = 0.992 with reference); concordance rose from 63.0% to 72.5% and 49.5% to 57.5% for the two readers, with reading times cut by 18% and 40%

records.dataset_size: a large real-world clinical dataset; size not stated

records.model_description: A triage model rather than a diagnostic one, and the design reflects that: thresholds are fitted at 100 percent sensitivity, so the model is only allowed to rule out. What it buys is concrete and measurable in avoided studies - up to 62 percent of children spared a diuretic renogram, which for this population means avoided radiopharmaceutical, catheterization and sedation. It also beats the two scoring systems urologists actually use, the Society for Fetal Urology grade and the hydronephrosis index.
records.headline_result: at 100% sensitivity, specificity 94%, 70% and 74% for the three washout thresholds (AUC 0.98, 0.94, 0.94), significantly better than SFU grade and the hydronephrosis index; up to 62% of diuretic renograms avoidable

Eleven groups emerged, discriminated mainly by curve location, kyphosis and lordosis, and subgroups appeared within existing Lenke types. This is data-driven taxonomy rather than diagnosis, aimed at replacing a classification the field agrees is inadequate.

records.title: Ultrasound-based gestational-age estimation in late pregnancy.

records.release_evidence: the prediction equations are published in full in the abstract
records.headline_result: gestational age uncertainty of 6-7 days at 14 weeks, 12-14 days at 26 weeks, and more than 14 days in the third trimester

records.title: Surface-Based fMRI-Driven Diffusion Tractography in the Presence of Significant Brain Pathology: A Study Linking Structure and Function in Cerebral Palsy.
records.model_family: surface-mesh fMRI-seeded diffusion tractography pipeline with a machine-learning track classifier
records.clinical_problem: running diffusion tractography in brains with major pathology, where automated cortical parcellation fails, manual region drawing is slow and error-prone, and the usual structure-function assumptions break down after cortical reorganisation
records.patient_population: 31 children with unilateral cerebral palsy
records.model_description: Aimed at exactly the situation pediatric neuroimaging keeps running into: the brain is too abnormal for atlas-based methods and too numerous for hand-drawn regions. Seeding from the child's own functional activation sidesteps the atlas, surface meshes tighten the seed, and a learned track classifier removes the irrelevant pathways that fMRI smoothing drags in. The head-to-head against the standard voxelwise approach is decisive on the metric that matters for a clinical pipeline - how many children could be processed at all.
records.headline_result: processed 87% of participants versus 65% for the voxelwise approach, with 15 of 20 diffusion-clinical correlations significant (R2 0.43-0.73) versus 2 for voxelwise

It is deliberately built for both pediatric and adult protocols, because organ-level knowledge is the prerequisite for patient-specific dose estimation in exactly the population where dose matters most.
